text_es: Write a SQL script that creates three reporting views for an e-commerce fulfillment system using strictly matching records across all linked tables. The schema includes `customers`, `customer_orders`, `order_items`, `products`, `warehouses`, `shipments`, and `carriers`. Create `vw_pending_shipments` to show customer names, order dates, product names, and warehouse locations by combining the first five tables for orders with status 'PENDING'. Create `vw_shipped_revenue` to calculate total revenue per carrier by linking `customer_orders`, `shipments`, `carriers`, `order_items`, and `products` for 'SHIPPED' orders. Finally, create `vw_warehouse_volume` linking `warehouses`, `products`, `order_items`, and `customer_orders` to sum the quantity of items processed per facility. Assume standard `id` primary keys and appropriately named foreign keys (e.g., `product_id`). Example: Querying `vw_pending_shipments` should output rows like `('Alice', '2023-10-01', 'Laptop', 'Warehouse A')`. Querying `vw_shipped_revenue` should return `('FedEx', 4500.00)`.
text_nat:
CREATE VIEW vw_pending_shipments AS
SELECT
    c.name AS customer_name,
    co.order_date,
    p.name AS product_name,
    w.location AS warehouse_location
FROM customers AS c
INNER JOIN customer_orders AS co ON c.id = co.customer_id
INNER JOIN order_items AS oi ON co.id = oi.order_id
INNER JOIN products AS p ON oi.product_id = p.id
INNER JOIN warehouses AS w ON p.warehouse_id = w.id
WHERE co.status = 'PENDING';

CREATE VIEW vw_shipped_revenue AS
SELECT
    ca.name AS carrier_name,
    SUM(oi.quantity * p.price) AS total_revenue
FROM customer_orders AS co
INNER JOIN shipments AS s ON co.id = s.order_id
INNER JOIN carriers AS ca ON s.carrier_id = ca.id
INNER JOIN order_items AS oi ON co.id = oi.order_id
INNER JOIN products AS p ON oi.product_id = p.id
WHERE co.status = 'SHIPPED'
GROUP BY ca.name;

CREATE VIEW vw_warehouse_volume AS
SELECT
    w.id AS warehouse_id,
    w.location AS warehouse_location,
    SUM(oi.quantity) AS total_units
FROM warehouses AS w
INNER JOIN products AS p ON w.id = p.warehouse_id
INNER JOIN order_items AS oi ON p.id = oi.product_id
INNER JOIN customer_orders AS co ON oi.order_id = co.id
GROUP BY w.id, w.location;

CREATE VIEW vw_carrier_warehouse_load AS
SELECT
    ca.name AS carrier_name,
    w.location AS warehouse_location,
    SUM(oi.quantity) AS units_shipped,
    SUM(oi.quantity * p.price) AS shipped_value
FROM shipments AS s
INNER JOIN carriers AS ca ON s.carrier_id = ca.id
INNER JOIN customer_orders AS co ON s.order_id = co.id
INNER JOIN order_items AS oi ON co.id = oi.order_id
INNER JOIN products AS p ON oi.product_id = p.id
INNER JOIN warehouses AS w ON p.warehouse_id = w.id
WHERE co.status = 'SHIPPED'
GROUP BY ca.name, w.location;

SELECT
    v.warehouse_location,
    v.total_units,
    l.carrier_name,
    l.units_shipped
FROM vw_warehouse_volume AS v
INNER JOIN vw_carrier_warehouse_load AS l ON v.warehouse_location = l.warehouse_location
ORDER BY v.warehouse_location, l.units_shipped DESC;

SELECT customer_name, order_date, product_name, warehouse_location
FROM vw_pending_shipments
ORDER BY order_date, customer_name;

SELECT carrier_name, total_revenue
FROM vw_shipped_revenue
ORDER BY total_revenue DESC;

SELECT warehouse_location, total_units
FROM vw_warehouse_volume
ORDER BY total_units DESC;

text_es: Develop a SQL script to define three database views for a hospital billing system, ensuring you only include records that have complete corresponding data across all relations. The tables are `patients`, `appointments`, `doctors`, `departments`, `treatments`, `billing_codes`, and `insurance_claims`. Create `vw_appointment_details` linking `patients`, `appointments`, `doctors`, and `departments` to display patient names, doctor names, and department names. Create `vw_claim_generation` linking `appointments`, `treatments`, `billing_codes`, `insurance_claims`, and `patients` to show the patient name, treatment cost, and claim status. Create `vw_department_revenue` linking `departments`, `doctors`, `appointments`, and `treatments` to sum the treatment costs per department. Example output for `vw_department_revenue` could be `('Cardiology', 150000.00)`. Assume standard relational primary/foreign key pairs throughout.
text_nat:
-- Hospital billing system: reporting views over fully-linked records only.
-- Every join is an INNER JOIN so that rows lacking a counterpart in any
-- related table are excluded from the views.

DROP VIEW IF EXISTS vw_department_revenue;
DROP VIEW IF EXISTS vw_claim_generation;
DROP VIEW IF EXISTS vw_appointment_details;

CREATE VIEW vw_appointment_details AS
SELECT
    a.appointment_id,
    a.appointment_date,
    a.status                                   AS appointment_status,
    p.patient_id,
    p.first_name || ' ' || p.last_name         AS patient_name,
    d.doctor_id,
    d.first_name || ' ' || d.last_name         AS doctor_name,
    dep.department_id,
    dep.department_name
FROM appointments AS a
INNER JOIN patients AS p ON p.patient_id = a.patient_id
INNER JOIN doctors AS d ON d.doctor_id = a.doctor_id
INNER JOIN departments AS dep ON dep.department_id = d.department_id;

CREATE VIEW vw_claim_generation AS
SELECT
    ic.claim_id,
    a.appointment_id,
    p.first_name || ' ' || p.last_name         AS patient_name,
    bc.code                                    AS billing_code,
    bc.description                             AS billing_description,
    t.treatment_id,
    t.cost                                     AS treatment_cost,
    ic.claim_status,
    ic.submitted_date
FROM treatments AS t
INNER JOIN appointments AS a ON a.appointment_id = t.appointment_id
INNER JOIN patients AS p ON p.patient_id = a.patient_id
INNER JOIN billing_codes AS bc ON bc.billing_code_id = t.billing_code_id
INNER JOIN insurance_claims AS ic ON ic.treatment_id = t.treatment_id;

CREATE VIEW vw_department_revenue AS
SELECT
    dep.department_name,
    SUM(t.cost)                                AS total_revenue
FROM departments AS dep
INNER JOIN doctors AS d ON d.department_id = dep.department_id
INNER JOIN appointments AS a ON a.doctor_id = d.doctor_id
INNER JOIN treatments AS t ON t.appointment_id = a.appointment_id
GROUP BY dep.department_id, dep.department_name;

-- Reports the billing team runs from these views.

-- Unsettled claim value broken down by treating department.
SELECT
    ad.department_name,
    cg.claim_status,
    COUNT(*)                                   AS claim_count,
    SUM(cg.treatment_cost)                     AS outstanding_amount
FROM vw_claim_generation AS cg
INNER JOIN vw_appointment_details AS ad ON ad.appointment_id = cg.appointment_id
WHERE cg.claim_status IN ('PENDING', 'REJECTED')
GROUP BY ad.department_name, cg.claim_status
ORDER BY outstanding_amount DESC;

-- Revenue per department alongside the size of its medical staff.
SELECT
    dep.department_name,
    r.total_revenue,
    COUNT(DISTINCT d.doctor_id)                AS doctor_count
FROM vw_department_revenue AS r
INNER JOIN departments AS dep ON dep.department_name = r.department_name
INNER JOIN doctors AS d ON d.department_id = dep.department_id
GROUP BY dep.department_name, r.total_revenue
ORDER BY r.total_revenue DESC;

SELECT appointment_date, patient_name, doctor_name, department_name
FROM vw_appointment_details
WHERE appointment_status = 'COMPLETED'
ORDER BY appointment_date, patient_name;

SELECT patient_name, billing_code, treatment_cost, claim_status
FROM vw_claim_generation
ORDER BY submitted_date;

SELECT department_name, total_revenue
FROM vw_department_revenue
ORDER BY total_revenue DESC;

-- Hospital billing system: reporting views over fully-linked records only.
-- Every join is an INNER JOIN so that rows lacking a counterpart in any
-- related table are excluded from the views.

DROP VIEW IF EXISTS vw_claim_generation;
DROP VIEW IF EXISTS vw_appointment_details;

FROM appointments AS a, patients AS p, doctors AS d, departments AS dep
WHERE p.patient_id = a.patient_id AND d.doctor_id = a.doctor_id AND dep.department_id = d.department_id;

CREATE VIEW vw_claim_generation AS
SELECT
    ic.claim_id,
    a.appointment_id,
    p.first_name || ' ' || p.last_name         AS patient_name,
    bc.code                                    AS billing_code,
    bc.description                             AS billing_description,
    t.treatment_id,
    t.cost                                     AS treatment_cost,
    ic.claim_status,
    ic.submitted_date
FROM treatments AS t, appointments AS a, patients AS p, billing_codes AS bc, insurance_claims AS ic
WHERE a.appointment_id = t.appointment_id AND p.patient_id = a.patient_id AND bc.billing_code_id = t.billing_code_id AND ic.treatment_id = t.treatment_id;

CREATE VIEW vw_department_revenue AS

    dep.department_name,
    SUM(t.cost)                                AS total_revenue
FROM departments AS dep, doctors AS d, appointments AS a, treatments AS t
WHERE d.department_id = dep.department_id AND a.doctor_id = d.doctor_id AND t.appointment_id = a.appointment_id
GROUP BY dep.department_id, dep.department_name;

    ad.department_name,
    cg.claim_status,

    dep.department_name,
    r.total_revenue,
    COUNT(DISTINCT d.doctor_id)                AS doctor_count
FROM vw_department_revenue AS r, departments AS dep, doctors AS d
WHERE dep.department_name = r.department_name AND d.department_id = dep.department_id
GROUP BY dep.department_name, r.total_revenue
ORDER BY r.total_revenue DESC;

FROM vw_appointment_details
WHERE appointment_status = 'COMPLETED'
ORDER BY appointment_date, patient_name;

SELECT patient_name, billing_code, treatment_cost, claim_status
FROM vw_claim_generation

text_es: Write a SQL script to generate three operational views for an airline management system, strictly requiring fully matched records across the schema. The tables provided are `flights`, `schedules`, `aircraft`, `models`, `manufacturers`, `maintenance_logs`, `mechanics`, `terminals`, and `gates`. Create `vw_flight_equipment` linking `flights`, `schedules`, `aircraft`, `models`, and `manufacturers` to display the flight number, departure time, model name, and manufacturer. Create `vw_maintenance_schedule` linking `aircraft`, `maintenance_logs`, `mechanics`, and `flights` to list aircraft registration, mechanic name, log details, and assigned flight numbers. Create `vw_terminal_assignments` linking `terminals`, `gates`, `flights`, and `schedules` to project daily gate utilization. Example output for `vw_flight_equipment`: `('DL102', '2023-11-01 10:00', '737 MAX', 'Boeing')`.
text_nat:
-- Airline operations reporting module: equipment, maintenance and terminal views.

CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW vw_flight_equipment AS
SELECT
    f.flight_number,
    TO_CHAR(s.departure_time, 'YYYY-MM-DD HH24:MI') AS departure_time,
    mo.model_name,
    mf.manufacturer_name
FROM flights f
JOIN schedules s ON s.flight_id = f.flight_id
JOIN aircraft a ON a.aircraft_id = f.aircraft_id
JOIN models mo ON mo.model_id = a.model_id
JOIN manufacturers mf ON mf.manufacturer_id = mo.manufacturer_id;

CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW vw_maintenance_schedule AS
SELECT
    a.registration,
    CONCAT(me.first_name, ' ', me.last_name) AS mechanic_name,
    ml.log_id,
    ml.performed_at,
    ml.work_description,
    ml.hours_spent,
    f.flight_number AS assigned_flight_number
FROM aircraft a
JOIN maintenance_logs ml ON ml.aircraft_id = a.aircraft_id
JOIN mechanics me ON me.mechanic_id = ml.mechanic_id
JOIN flights f ON f.aircraft_id = a.aircraft_id;

CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW vw_terminal_assignments AS
SELECT
    t.terminal_code,
    g.gate_number,
    CAST(s.departure_time AS DATE) AS service_date,
    COUNT(f.flight_id) AS flights_handled,
    MIN(s.departure_time) AS first_departure,
    MAX(s.departure_time) AS last_departure
FROM terminals t
JOIN gates g ON g.terminal_id = t.terminal_id
JOIN flights f ON f.gate_id = g.gate_id
JOIN schedules s ON s.flight_id = f.flight_id
GROUP BY t.terminal_code, g.gate_number, CAST(s.departure_time AS DATE);

-- Operational reports built on top of the three views.

SELECT flight_number, departure_time, model_name, manufacturer_name
FROM vw_flight_equipment
ORDER BY departure_time, flight_number;

SELECT
    fe.manufacturer_name,
    fe.model_name,
    ms.registration,
    ms.mechanic_name,
    ms.performed_at,
    ms.work_description,
    ms.hours_spent
FROM vw_maintenance_schedule ms
JOIN vw_flight_equipment fe ON fe.flight_number = ms.assigned_flight_number
ORDER BY fe.manufacturer_name, ms.performed_at;

SELECT
    t.terminal_code,
    g.gate_number,
    f.flight_number,
    mo.model_name,
    s.departure_time
FROM terminals t
JOIN gates g ON g.terminal_id = t.terminal_id
JOIN flights f ON f.gate_id = g.gate_id
JOIN schedules s ON s.flight_id = f.flight_id
JOIN aircraft a ON a.aircraft_id = f.aircraft_id
JOIN models mo ON mo.model_id = a.model_id
ORDER BY t.terminal_code, g.gate_number, s.departure_time;

SELECT
    ta.terminal_code,
    ta.gate_number,
    ta.service_date,
    ta.flights_handled,
    COUNT(DISTINCT ms.registration) AS aircraft_in_maintenance
FROM vw_terminal_assignments ta
JOIN gates g ON g.gate_number = ta.gate_number
JOIN flights f ON f.gate_id = g.gate_id
JOIN vw_maintenance_schedule ms ON ms.assigned_flight_number = f.flight_number
GROUP BY ta.terminal_code, ta.gate_number, ta.service_date, ta.flights_handled
ORDER BY ta.service_date, ta.terminal_code, ta.gate_number;

text_es: Create a SQL script defining three academic reporting views for a university, strictly linking only fully matching records. The schema utilizes `students`, `enrollments`, `sections`, `courses`, `semesters`, `professors`, `departments`, `buildings`, and `rooms`. Create `vw_student_transcripts` connecting `students`, `enrollments`, `sections`, `courses`, and `semesters` to output student names, course titles, grades, and semester names. Create `vw_faculty_load` connecting `professors`, `sections`, `courses`, `departments`, and `buildings` to output professor names, department names, course credits, and building names. Create `vw_room_utilization` connecting `buildings`, `rooms`, `sections`, and `enrollments` to count total enrolled students per room. Example output for `vw_student_transcripts`: `('John Doe', 'Database Systems', 'A', 'Fall 2023')`.
text_nat:
CREATE VIEW vw_student_transcripts AS
SELECT
    s.first_name || ' ' || s.last_name AS student_name,
    c.title AS course_title,
    e.grade AS grade,
    sem.name AS semester_name
FROM students AS s
INNER JOIN enrollments AS e ON e.student_id = s.student_id
INNER JOIN sections AS sec ON sec.section_id = e.section_id
INNER JOIN courses AS c ON c.course_id = sec.course_id
INNER JOIN semesters AS sem ON sem.semester_id = sec.semester_id
WHERE e.grade IS NOT NULL;

CREATE VIEW vw_faculty_load AS
SELECT
    p.first_name || ' ' || p.last_name AS professor_name,
    d.name AS department_name,
    c.credits AS course_credits,
    b.name AS building_name
FROM professors AS p
INNER JOIN sections AS sec ON sec.professor_id = p.professor_id
INNER JOIN courses AS c ON c.course_id = sec.course_id
INNER JOIN departments AS d ON d.department_id = p.department_id
INNER JOIN rooms AS r ON r.room_id = sec.room_id
INNER JOIN buildings AS b ON b.building_id = r.building_id;

CREATE VIEW vw_room_utilization AS
SELECT
    b.name AS building_name,
    r.room_number AS room_number,
    r.capacity AS room_capacity,
    COUNT(e.enrollment_id) AS total_enrolled
FROM buildings AS b
INNER JOIN rooms AS r ON r.building_id = b.building_id
INNER JOIN sections AS sec ON sec.room_id = r.room_id
INNER JOIN enrollments AS e ON e.section_id = sec.section_id
GROUP BY b.name, r.room_number, r.capacity;

SELECT
    d.name AS department_name,
    sem.name AS semester_name,
    COUNT(DISTINCT e.student_id) AS distinct_students,
    ROUND(AVG(c.credits), 2) AS average_credits
FROM departments AS d
INNER JOIN courses AS c ON c.department_id = d.department_id
INNER JOIN sections AS sec ON sec.course_id = c.course_id
INNER JOIN semesters AS sem ON sem.semester_id = sec.semester_id
INNER JOIN enrollments AS e ON e.section_id = sec.section_id

SELECT
    s.first_name || ' ' || s.last_name AS student_name,
    d.name AS department_name,
    COUNT(*) AS top_grade_count
FROM students AS s
INNER JOIN enrollments AS e ON e.student_id = s.student_id
INNER JOIN sections AS sec ON sec.section_id = e.section_id
INNER JOIN courses AS c ON c.course_id = sec.course_id

SELECT

INNER JOIN professors AS p ON p.professor_id = sec.professor_id

CREATE VIEW vw_room_utilization AS

text_es: Write a SQL script establishing three supply chain views for a manufacturing plant, enforcing strict relational matching without missing references. The database includes `finished_goods`, `bom_lines`, `components`, `suppliers`, `purchase_orders`, `po_lines`, `receipts`, `warehouses`, and `inspectors`. Create `vw_product_suppliers` linking `finished_goods`, `bom_lines`, `components`, and `suppliers` to map out which supplier provides parts for which final good. Create `vw_pending_receipts` linking `suppliers`, `purchase_orders`, `po_lines`, `components`, and `warehouses` for orders marked 'IN_TRANSIT'. Create `vw_inspection_queue` linking `components`, `receipts`, `warehouses`, and `inspectors` to list recently received parts needing QA. Example output for `vw_product_suppliers`: `('Tractor', 'Engine Block', 'HeavyMetals Inc')`.
text_nat:
CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW vw_product_suppliers AS
SELECT
    fg.product_name,
    c.component_name,
    s.supplier_name,
    bl.quantity_per_unit,
    c.unit_cost * bl.quantity_per_unit AS extended_cost
FROM finished_goods AS fg
INNER JOIN bom_lines AS bl ON bl.product_id = fg.product_id
INNER JOIN components AS c ON c.component_id = bl.component_id
INNER JOIN suppliers AS s ON s.supplier_id = c.preferred_supplier_id
WHERE fg.is_active = 1
  AND bl.quantity_per_unit > 0;

CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW vw_pending_receipts AS
SELECT
    s.supplier_name,
    po.po_number,
    po.order_date,
    po.expected_date,
    c.component_name,
    pl.ordered_qty,
    pl.received_qty,
    pl.ordered_qty - pl.received_qty AS open_qty,
    w.warehouse_name,
    w.location_code
FROM suppliers AS s
INNER JOIN purchase_orders AS po ON po.supplier_id = s.supplier_id
INNER JOIN po_lines AS pl ON pl.po_id = po.po_id
INNER JOIN components AS c ON c.component_id = pl.component_id
INNER JOIN warehouses AS w ON w.warehouse_id = po.destination_warehouse_id
WHERE po.status = 'IN_TRANSIT'
  AND pl.received_qty < pl.ordered_qty;

CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW vw_inspection_queue AS
SELECT
    c.component_name,
    c.component_code,
    r.receipt_id,
    r.received_date,
    r.received_qty,
    r.lot_number,
    w.warehouse_name,
    i.inspector_name,
    i.certification_level
FROM components AS c
INNER JOIN receipts AS r ON r.component_id = c.component_id
INNER JOIN warehouses AS w ON w.warehouse_id = r.warehouse_id
INNER JOIN inspectors AS i ON i.inspector_id = r.assigned_inspector_id
WHERE r.qa_status = 'PENDING'
  AND r.received_date >= CURRENT_DATE - INTERVAL '30' DAY;

SELECT
    ps.product_name,
    ps.component_name,
    pr.po_number,
    pr.open_qty,
    pr.expected_date
FROM vw_product_suppliers AS ps
INNER JOIN vw_pending_receipts AS pr ON pr.component_name = ps.component_name
ORDER BY pr.expected_date, ps.product_name;

SELECT
    iq.component_name,
    iq.lot_number,
    iq.received_date,
    iq.inspector_name,
    pr.supplier_name
FROM vw_inspection_queue AS iq
INNER JOIN vw_pending_receipts AS pr ON pr.component_name = iq.component_name
ORDER BY iq.received_date DESC, iq.component_name;

SELECT product_name, component_name, supplier_name
FROM vw_product_suppliers
ORDER BY product_name, component_name;

SELECT
    ps.product_name,
    SUM(ps.extended_cost) AS material_cost,
    COUNT(DISTINCT ps.supplier_name) AS supplier_count
FROM vw_product_suppliers AS ps
GROUP BY ps.product_name
ORDER BY material_cost DESC;

SELECT
    iq.inspector_name,
    iq.certification_level,
    COUNT(*) AS lots_waiting,
    SUM(iq.received_qty) AS units_waiting
FROM vw_inspection_queue AS iq
GROUP BY iq.inspector_name, iq.certification_level
ORDER BY units_waiting DESC;

text_es: Design a SQL script that compiles three administrative views for a multi-branch library system, relying exclusively on records with intact relationships across tables. The tables are `members`, `loans`, `book_copies`, `books`, `authors`, `fines`, `branches`, and `publishers`. Create `vw_active_loans` by linking `members`, `loans`, `book_copies`, `books`, and `authors` to output member names, book titles, author names, and due dates. Create `vw_fine_notices` linking `fines`, `loans`, `members`, `book_copies`, and `branches` to aggregate unpaid fines per member per branch. Create `vw_publisher_inventory` linking `branches`, `book_copies`, `books`, and `publishers` to count available copies grouped by publisher and branch. Example `vw_active_loans` output: `('Jane Smith', 'Dune', 'Frank Herbert', '2023-12-01')`.
text_nat:
CREATE VIEW vw_active_loans AS
SELECT
    m.member_id,
    m.first_name || ' ' || m.last_name AS member_name,
    b.title AS book_title,
    a.first_name || ' ' || a.last_name AS author_name,
    l.due_date
FROM loans AS l
INNER JOIN members AS m ON l.member_id = m.member_id
INNER JOIN book_copies AS bc ON l.copy_id = bc.copy_id
INNER JOIN books AS b ON bc.book_id = b.book_id
INNER JOIN authors AS a ON b.author_id = a.author_id
WHERE l.return_date IS NULL;

CREATE VIEW vw_fine_notices AS
SELECT
    m.member_id,
    m.first_name || ' ' || m.last_name AS member_name,
    br.branch_id,
    br.branch_name,
    COUNT(f.fine_id) AS unpaid_fine_count,
    SUM(f.amount) AS unpaid_total
FROM fines AS f
INNER JOIN loans AS l ON f.loan_id = l.loan_id
INNER JOIN members AS m ON l.member_id = m.member_id
INNER JOIN book_copies AS bc ON l.copy_id = bc.copy_id
INNER JOIN branches AS br ON bc.branch_id = br.branch_id
WHERE f.paid_date IS NULL
GROUP BY m.member_id, m.first_name, m.last_name, br.branch_id, br.branch_name;

CREATE VIEW vw_publisher_inventory AS
SELECT
    p.publisher_id,
    p.publisher_name,
    br.branch_id,
    br.branch_name,
    COUNT(bc.copy_id) AS available_copies
FROM branches AS br
INNER JOIN book_copies AS bc ON br.branch_id = bc.branch_id
INNER JOIN books AS b ON bc.book_id = b.book_id
INNER JOIN publishers AS p ON b.publisher_id = p.publisher_id
WHERE bc.status = 'available'
GROUP BY p.publisher_id, p.publisher_name, br.branch_id, br.branch_name;

SELECT
    al.member_name,
    al.book_title,
    al.due_date,
    fn.branch_name,
    fn.unpaid_total
FROM vw_active_loans AS al
INNER JOIN vw_fine_notices AS fn ON al.member_id = fn.member_id
WHERE al.due_date < CURRENT_DATE
ORDER BY fn.unpaid_total DESC, al.due_date;

SELECT
    stock.branch_name,
    SUM(stock.available_copies) AS shelf_stock,
    SUM(debt.unpaid_total) AS outstanding_fines
FROM vw_publisher_inventory AS stock
INNER JOIN vw_fine_notices AS debt ON stock.branch_id = debt.branch_id
GROUP BY stock.branch_name
ORDER BY outstanding_fines DESC;

SELECT member_name, book_title, author_name, due_date
FROM vw_active_loans
ORDER BY due_date, member_name;

SELECT branch_name, member_name, unpaid_fine_count, unpaid_total
FROM vw_fine_notices
WHERE unpaid_total >= 5.00
ORDER BY unpaid_total DESC;

SELECT branch_name, publisher_name, available_copies
FROM vw_publisher_inventory
ORDER BY branch_name, available_copies DESC;

text_es: Construct a SQL script defining three operational views for a network of auto repair shops, processing only entities that completely match across the relations. The database entails `customers`, `vehicles`, `work_orders`, `shops`, `parts_used`, `inventory`, `suppliers`, and `mechanics`. Create `vw_customer_invoices` linking `customers`, `vehicles`, `work_orders`, and `shops` to generate basic invoice headers with shop locations. Create `vw_part_consumption` linking `work_orders`, `parts_used`, `inventory`, `suppliers`, and `mechanics` to track which mechanic used which supplier's parts. Create `vw_mechanic_workload` linking `shops`, `mechanics`, `work_orders`, and `vehicles` to count active work orders per mechanic. Example `vw_customer_invoices` output: `('Bob Jones', 'Ford F150', 'Completed', 'Downtown Auto')`.
text_nat:
CREATE VIEW vw_customer_invoices AS
SELECT
    wo.work_order_id,
    wo.mechanic_id,
    c.customer_name,
    v.make || ' ' || v.model AS vehicle,
    v.license_plate,
    wo.status,
    s.shop_name,
    s.city || ', ' || s.state AS shop_location,
    wo.labor_total + wo.parts_total AS invoice_total
FROM work_orders AS wo
INNER JOIN vehicles AS v ON wo.vehicle_id = v.vehicle_id
INNER JOIN customers AS c ON v.customer_id = c.customer_id
INNER JOIN shops AS s ON wo.shop_id = s.shop_id;

CREATE VIEW vw_part_consumption AS
SELECT
    wo.work_order_id,
    wo.status AS work_order_status,
    m.mechanic_name,
    m.certification_level,
    i.part_number,
    i.part_description,
    sup.supplier_id,
    sup.supplier_name,
    pu.quantity_used,
    pu.quantity_used * i.unit_cost AS extended_cost
FROM parts_used AS pu
INNER JOIN work_orders AS wo ON pu.work_order_id = wo.work_order_id
INNER JOIN inventory AS i ON pu.inventory_id = i.inventory_id
INNER JOIN suppliers AS sup ON i.supplier_id = sup.supplier_id
INNER JOIN mechanics AS m ON wo.mechanic_id = m.mechanic_id;

CREATE VIEW vw_mechanic_workload AS
SELECT
    s.shop_id,
    s.shop_name,
    m.mechanic_id,
    m.mechanic_name,
    COUNT(wo.work_order_id) AS active_work_orders,
    COUNT(DISTINCT v.vehicle_id) AS distinct_vehicles,
    SUM(wo.estimated_hours) AS estimated_hours_booked
FROM shops AS s
INNER JOIN mechanics AS m ON s.shop_id = m.shop_id
INNER JOIN work_orders AS wo ON m.mechanic_id = wo.mechanic_id
INNER JOIN vehicles AS v ON wo.vehicle_id = v.vehicle_id
WHERE wo.status IN ('Open', 'In Progress')
GROUP BY s.shop_id, s.shop_name, m.mechanic_id, m.mechanic_name;

SELECT
    ci.customer_name,
    ci.vehicle,
    ci.status,
    ci.shop_name,
    mw.active_work_orders AS mechanic_open_orders
FROM vw_customer_invoices AS ci
INNER JOIN vw_mechanic_workload AS mw ON ci.mechanic_id = mw.mechanic_id
ORDER BY ci.work_order_id;

SELECT
    pc.supplier_name,
    pc.mechanic_name,
    SUM(pc.quantity_used) AS parts_installed,
    SUM(pc.extended_cost) AS spend
FROM vw_part_consumption AS pc
INNER JOIN suppliers AS sup ON pc.supplier_id = sup.supplier_id

GROUP BY pc.supplier_name, pc.mechanic_name
ORDER BY spend DESC;

text_es: Develop a SQL script containing three dashboard views for a real estate brokerage, returning only records with complete corresponding foreign key matches. The tables consist of `offices`, `agents`, `listings`, `properties`, `property_types`, `transactions`, `buyers`, and `sellers`. Create `vw_active_listings` linking `offices`, `agents`, `listings`, `properties`, and `property_types` to display office locations, agent names, property addresses, and listing prices. Create `vw_closed_deals` linking `transactions`, `listings`, `agents`, `buyers`, and `sellers` to output closed dates, buyer names, seller names, and agent commissions. Create `vw_office_performance` linking `offices`, `agents`, `transactions`, and `properties` to aggregate total transaction volume per office. Example `vw_active_listings` output: `('Uptown', 'Alice', '123 Main St', 'Condo', 450000)`.
text_nat:
CREATE VIEW vw_active_listings AS
SELECT
    o.city AS office_location,
    a.first_name || ' ' || a.last_name AS agent_name,
    p.street_address AS property_address,
    pt.type_name AS property_type,
    l.list_price AS listing_price
FROM offices o
INNER JOIN agents a ON a.office_id = o.office_id
INNER JOIN listings l ON l.agent_id = a.agent_id
INNER JOIN properties p ON p.property_id = l.property_id
INNER JOIN property_types pt ON pt.type_id = p.type_id
WHERE l.status = 'ACTIVE';

CREATE VIEW vw_closed_deals AS
SELECT
    t.listing_id,
    t.closed_on AS closed_date,
    b.first_name || ' ' || b.last_name AS buyer_name,
    s.first_name || ' ' || s.last_name AS seller_name,
    a.first_name || ' ' || a.last_name AS agent_name,
    ROUND(t.sale_price * t.commission_rate, 2) AS agent_commission
FROM transactions t
INNER JOIN listings l ON l.listing_id = t.listing_id
INNER JOIN agents a ON a.agent_id = l.agent_id
INNER JOIN buyers b ON b.buyer_id = t.buyer_id
INNER JOIN sellers s ON s.seller_id = t.seller_id
WHERE t.status = 'CLOSED';

CREATE VIEW vw_office_performance AS
SELECT
    o.name AS office_name,
    o.city AS office_city,
    COUNT(t.transaction_id) AS closed_transactions,
    SUM(t.sale_price) AS total_transaction_volume,
    ROUND(AVG(p.square_feet), 0) AS average_square_feet
FROM offices o
INNER JOIN agents a ON a.office_id = o.office_id
INNER JOIN transactions t ON t.agent_id = a.agent_id
INNER JOIN listings l ON l.listing_id = t.listing_id
INNER JOIN properties p ON p.property_id = l.property_id
WHERE t.status = 'CLOSED'
GROUP BY o.name, o.city;

SELECT
    cd.closed_date,
    cd.buyer_name,
    cd.seller_name,
    cd.agent_commission,
    p.street_address AS property_address,
    pt.type_name AS property_type
FROM vw_closed_deals cd
INNER JOIN listings l ON l.listing_id = cd.listing_id
INNER JOIN properties p ON p.property_id = l.property_id
INNER JOIN property_types pt ON pt.type_id = p.type_id
ORDER BY cd.closed_date DESC;

SELECT
    o.name AS office_name,
    a.first_name || ' ' || a.last_name AS agent_name,
    COUNT(t.transaction_id) AS deals_closed,
    SUM(ROUND(t.sale_price * t.commission_rate, 2)) AS commission_earned
FROM agents a
INNER JOIN offices o ON o.office_id = a.office_id
INNER JOIN transactions t ON t.agent_id = a.agent_id
WHERE t.status = 'CLOSED'
GROUP BY o.name, a.first_name, a.last_name
ORDER BY commission_earned DESC;

SELECT
    perf.office_name,
    perf.total_transaction_volume,
    COUNT(al.listing_price) AS active_listings,
    SUM(al.listing_price) AS active_pipeline_value
FROM vw_office_performance perf
INNER JOIN vw_active_listings al ON al.office_location = perf.office_city
GROUP BY perf.office_name, perf.total_transaction_volume
ORDER BY perf.total_transaction_volume DESC;

text_es: Write a SQL script to produce three back-office views for a restaurant chain, stipulating that only records with full matching associations are included. The tables are `menus`, `menu_items`, `recipes`, `ingredients`, `vendors`, `locations`, `managers`, and `deliveries`. Create `vw_menu_costing` linking `menus`, `menu_items`, `recipes`, `ingredients`, and `vendors` to calculate the total ingredient cost per menu item. Create `vw_delivery_tracking` linking `locations`, `managers`, `deliveries`, `vendors`, and `ingredients` to show upcoming deliveries by manager name and vendor. Create `vw_location_offerings` linking `locations`, `menus`, `menu_items`, and `recipes` to list all localized dish offerings. Example `vw_menu_costing` output: `('Dinner', 'Steak Frites', 'Beef Supplier Inc', 12.50)`.
text_nat:
CREATE TABLE vendors (vendor_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, vendor_name VARCHAR(80) NOT NULL);

CREATE TABLE managers (manager_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, manager_name VARCHAR(80) NOT NULL);

CREATE TABLE locations (location_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, location_name VARCHAR(80) NOT NULL,
    city VARCHAR(60) NOT NULL, manager_id INTEGER REFERENCES managers (manager_id));

CREATE TABLE menus (menu_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, menu_name VARCHAR(60) NOT NULL,
    location_id INTEGER REFERENCES locations (location_id));

CREATE TABLE recipes (recipe_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, recipe_name VARCHAR(80) NOT NULL,
    prep_minutes INTEGER NOT NULL);

CREATE TABLE menu_items (menu_item_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, menu_id INTEGER REFERENCES menus (menu_id),
    recipe_id INTEGER REFERENCES recipes (recipe_id), item_name VARCHAR(80) NOT NULL,
    sale_price NUMERIC(8, 2) NOT NULL);

CREATE TABLE ingredients (ingredient_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, recipe_id INTEGER REFERENCES recipes (recipe_id),
    vendor_id INTEGER REFERENCES vendors (vendor_id), ingredient_name VARCHAR(80) NOT NULL,
    quantity NUMERIC(8, 3) NOT NULL, unit_cost NUMERIC(8, 2) NOT NULL);

CREATE TABLE deliveries (delivery_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, location_id INTEGER REFERENCES locations (location_id),
    vendor_id INTEGER REFERENCES vendors (vendor_id), ingredient_id INTEGER REFERENCES ingredients (ingredient_id),
    delivery_date DATE NOT NULL, cases_ordered INTEGER NOT NULL);

CREATE VIEW vw_menu_costing AS
SELECT m.menu_name, mi.item_name, v.vendor_name,
       ROUND(SUM(i.quantity * i.unit_cost), 2) AS ingredient_cost
FROM menus AS m
INNER JOIN menu_items AS mi ON mi.menu_id = m.menu_id
INNER JOIN recipes AS r ON r.recipe_id = mi.recipe_id
INNER JOIN ingredients AS i ON i.recipe_id = r.recipe_id
INNER JOIN vendors AS v ON v.vendor_id = i.vendor_id
GROUP BY m.menu_name, mi.item_name, v.vendor_name;

CREATE VIEW vw_delivery_tracking AS
SELECT l.location_name, mg.manager_name, v.vendor_name, i.ingredient_name,
       d.delivery_date, d.cases_ordered
FROM locations AS l
INNER JOIN managers AS mg ON mg.manager_id = l.manager_id
INNER JOIN deliveries AS d ON d.location_id = l.location_id
INNER JOIN vendors AS v ON v.vendor_id = d.vendor_id
INNER JOIN ingredients AS i ON i.ingredient_id = d.ingredient_id
WHERE d.delivery_date >= CURRENT_DATE;

CREATE VIEW vw_location_offerings AS
SELECT l.location_name, l.city, m.menu_name, mi.item_name,
       r.recipe_name, r.prep_minutes, mi.sale_price
FROM locations AS l
INNER JOIN menus AS m ON m.location_id = l.location_id
INNER JOIN menu_items AS mi ON mi.menu_id = m.menu_id
INNER JOIN recipes AS r ON r.recipe_id = mi.recipe_id;

SELECT o.city, o.location_name, o.item_name, o.sale_price, c.ingredient_cost,
       ROUND(o.sale_price - c.ingredient_cost, 2) AS margin
FROM vw_location_offerings AS o
INNER JOIN vw_menu_costing AS c ON c.menu_name = o.menu_name AND c.item_name = o.item_name
ORDER BY margin DESC;

SELECT v.vendor_name, COUNT(*) AS open_deliveries,
       SUM(d.cases_ordered * i.unit_cost) AS committed_spend
FROM deliveries AS d
INNER JOIN vendors AS v ON v.vendor_id = d.vendor_id
INNER JOIN ingredients AS i ON i.ingredient_id = d.ingredient_id
WHERE d.delivery_date >= CURRENT_DATE
GROUP BY v.vendor_name
ORDER BY committed_spend DESC;

SELECT mg.manager_name, l.location_name, COUNT(DISTINCT m.menu_id) AS menus_offered,
       COUNT(mi.menu_item_id) AS dishes_offered
FROM managers AS mg
INNER JOIN locations AS l ON l.manager_id = mg.manager_id
INNER JOIN menus AS m ON m.location_id = l.location_id
INNER JOIN menu_items AS mi ON mi.menu_id = m.menu_id
GROUP BY mg.manager_name, l.location_name
ORDER BY mg.manager_name, l.location_name;

SELECT location_name, manager_name, vendor_name, ingredient_name, delivery_date, cases_ordered
FROM vw_delivery_tracking
ORDER BY delivery_date, location_name;

text_es: Create a SQL script defining three financial views for a music streaming platform, keeping only entries that have complete metadata links. The schema spans `users`, `listening_sessions`, `tracks`, `albums`, `artists`, `record_labels`, `payout_rates`, and `countries`. Create `vw_track_streams` linking `users`, `listening_sessions`, `tracks`, `albums`, and `artists` to output user emails, track names, artist names, and play durations. Create `vw_label_payouts` linking `listening_sessions`, `tracks`, `albums`, `record_labels`, and `payout_rates` to calculate total owed royalties per label. Create `vw_regional_tastes` linking `users`, `countries`, `listening_sessions`, and `tracks` to find the most played tracks per country. Example `vw_track_streams` output: `('user1@mail.com', 'Song A', 'Artist B', 215)`.
text_nat:
-- Financial reporting views for the music streaming platform; inner joins only, so sessions with incomplete metadata links are dropped.

DROP VIEW IF EXISTS vw_track_streams;
DROP VIEW IF EXISTS vw_label_payouts;
DROP VIEW IF EXISTS vw_regional_tastes;

CREATE VIEW vw_track_streams AS
SELECT u.email                  AS user_email,
       t.track_name             AS track_name,
       ar.artist_name           AS artist_name,
       ls.play_duration_seconds AS play_duration
FROM users AS u
INNER JOIN listening_sessions AS ls ON ls.user_id = u.user_id
INNER JOIN tracks AS t ON t.track_id = ls.track_id
INNER JOIN albums AS al ON al.album_id = t.album_id
INNER JOIN artists AS ar ON ar.artist_id = al.artist_id
WHERE ls.play_duration_seconds > 0;

CREATE VIEW vw_label_payouts AS
SELECT rl.label_id                    AS label_id,
       rl.label_name                  AS label_name,
       COUNT(ls.session_id)           AS billable_streams,
       SUM(ls.play_duration_seconds)  AS total_seconds_played,
       ROUND(SUM(ls.play_duration_seconds * pr.rate_per_second), 2) AS total_owed
FROM listening_sessions AS ls
INNER JOIN tracks AS t ON t.track_id = ls.track_id
INNER JOIN albums AS al ON al.album_id = t.album_id
INNER JOIN record_labels AS rl ON rl.label_id = al.label_id
INNER JOIN payout_rates AS pr ON pr.label_id = rl.label_id
WHERE ls.play_duration_seconds > 0
GROUP BY rl.label_id, rl.label_name;

CREATE VIEW vw_regional_tastes AS
WITH country_play_counts AS (
    SELECT c.country_id, c.country_name, t.track_id, t.track_name,
           COUNT(*) AS play_count
    FROM users AS u
    INNER JOIN countries AS c ON c.country_id = u.country_id
    INNER JOIN listening_sessions AS ls ON ls.user_id = u.user_id
    INNER JOIN tracks AS t ON t.track_id = ls.track_id
    GROUP BY c.country_id, c.country_name, t.track_id, t.track_name
),
ranked_plays AS (
    SELECT cpc.*,
           RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY cpc.country_id ORDER BY cpc.play_count DESC) AS play_rank
    FROM country_play_counts AS cpc
)
SELECT rp.country_name, rp.track_id, rp.track_name, rp.play_count
FROM ranked_plays AS rp
WHERE rp.play_rank = 1;

-- Regional favourites, annotated with the artist behind each track.
SELECT rt.country_name, rt.track_name, ar.artist_name, rt.play_count
FROM vw_regional_tastes AS rt
INNER JOIN tracks AS t ON t.track_id = rt.track_id
INNER JOIN albums AS al ON al.album_id = t.album_id
INNER JOIN artists AS ar ON ar.artist_id = al.artist_id
ORDER BY rt.country_name;

-- Royalties owed per label, broken down by the listener's country.
SELECT rl.label_name, c.country_name,
       ROUND(SUM(ls.play_duration_seconds * pr.rate_per_second), 2) AS owed
FROM listening_sessions AS ls
INNER JOIN users AS u ON u.user_id = ls.user_id
INNER JOIN countries AS c ON c.country_id = u.country_id
INNER JOIN tracks AS t ON t.track_id = ls.track_id
INNER JOIN albums AS al ON al.album_id = t.album_id
INNER JOIN record_labels AS rl ON rl.label_id = al.label_id
INNER JOIN payout_rates AS pr ON pr.label_id = rl.label_id
WHERE ls.play_duration_seconds > 0

text_alt:
-- Financial reporting views for the music streaming platform; inner joins only, so sessions with incomplete metadata links are dropped.

DROP VIEW IF EXISTS vw_track_streams;
DROP VIEW IF EXISTS vw_label_payouts;
DROP VIEW IF EXISTS vw_regional_tastes;

CREATE VIEW vw_track_streams AS
SELECT u.email                  AS user_email,
       t.track_name             AS track_name,
       ar.artist_name           AS artist_name,
       ls.play_duration_seconds AS play_duration
FROM users AS u, listening_sessions AS ls, tracks AS t, albums AS al, artists AS ar
WHERE ls.user_id = u.user_id AND t.track_id = ls.track_id AND al.album_id = t.album_id AND ar.artist_id = al.artist_id AND ls.play_duration_seconds > 0;

CREATE VIEW vw_label_payouts AS
SELECT rl.label_id                    AS label_id,
       rl.label_name                  AS label_name,
       COUNT(ls.session_id)           AS billable_streams,
       SUM(ls.play_duration_seconds)  AS total_seconds_played,
       ROUND(SUM(ls.play_duration_seconds * pr.rate_per_second), 2) AS total_owed
FROM listening_sessions AS ls, tracks AS t, albums AS al, record_labels AS rl, payout_rates AS pr
WHERE t.track_id = ls.track_id AND al.album_id = t.album_id AND rl.label_id = al.label_id AND pr.label_id = rl.label_id AND ls.play_duration_seconds > 0
GROUP BY rl.label_id, rl.label_name;

CREATE VIEW vw_regional_tastes AS
WITH country_play_counts AS (
    SELECT c.country_id, c.country_name, t.track_id, t.track_name,
           COUNT(*) AS play_count
    FROM users AS u, countries AS c, listening_sessions AS ls, tracks AS t
    WHERE c.country_id = u.country_id AND ls.user_id = u.user_id AND t.track_id = ls.track_id
    GROUP BY c.country_id, c.country_name, t.track_id, t.track_name
),
ranked_plays AS (
    SELECT cpc.*,
           RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY cpc.country_id ORDER BY cpc.play_count DESC) AS play_rank
    FROM country_play_counts AS cpc
)
SELECT rp.country_name, rp.track_id, rp.track_name, rp.play_count
FROM ranked_plays AS rp
WHERE rp.play_rank = 1;

-- Regional favourites, annotated with the artist behind each track.
SELECT rt.country_name, rt.track_name, ar.artist_name, rt.play_count
FROM vw_regional_tastes AS rt, tracks AS t, albums AS al, artists AS ar
WHERE t.track_id = rt.track_id AND al.album_id = t.album_id AND ar.artist_id = al.artist_id
ORDER BY rt.country_name;

-- Royalties owed per label, broken down by the listener's country.
SELECT rl.label_name, c.country_name,
       ROUND(SUM(ls.play_duration_seconds * pr.rate_per_second), 2) AS owed
FROM listening_sessions AS ls, users AS u, countries AS c, tracks AS t, albums AS al, record_labels AS rl, payout_rates AS pr
WHERE u.user_id = ls.user_id AND c.country_id = u.country_id AND t.track_id = ls.track_id AND al.album_id = t.album_id AND rl.label_id = al.label_id AND pr.label_id = rl.label_id AND ls.play_duration_seconds > 0
GROUP BY rl.label_name, c.country_name
ORDER BY owed DESC;

SELECT user_email, track_name, artist_name, play_duration
FROM vw_track_streams
ORDER BY play_duration DESC
LIMIT 20;

SELECT label_name, billable_streams, total_owed
FROM vw_label_payouts
ORDER BY total_owed DESC;

text_es: Design a SQL script to establish three metric views for an IT helpdesk system, strictly restricting results to entries with flawless relational mapping. The tables involved are `employees`, `departments`, `office_locations`, `tickets`, `hardware_assets`, `asset_models`, `technicians`, and `resolutions`. Create `vw_open_tickets` linking `employees`, `departments`, `office_locations`, `tickets`, and `hardware_assets` to display employee names, department names, and assigned hardware for 'OPEN' tickets. Create `vw_hardware_repairs` linking `tickets`, `hardware_assets`, `asset_models`, `technicians`, and `resolutions` to log repair notes against specific asset models. Create `vw_department_incidents` linking `technicians`, `departments`, `tickets`, and `resolutions` to count resolved tickets per department. Example `vw_open_tickets` output: `('John Smith', 'HR', 'NY-Floor2', 'Laptop Issue')`.
text_nat:
CREATE VIEW vw_open_tickets AS
SELECT
    e.first_name || ' ' || e.last_name AS employee_name,
    d.department_name,
    o.location_code,
    t.title AS ticket_title,
    h.asset_tag
FROM tickets AS t
INNER JOIN employees AS e ON t.requester_id = e.employee_id
INNER JOIN departments AS d ON e.department_id = d.department_id
INNER JOIN office_locations AS o ON d.location_id = o.location_id
INNER JOIN hardware_assets AS h ON t.asset_id = h.asset_id
WHERE t.status = 'OPEN'
  AND h.assigned_to = e.employee_id;

CREATE VIEW vw_hardware_repairs AS
SELECT
    t.ticket_id,
    m.manufacturer,
    m.model_name,
    h.asset_tag,
    tech.technician_id,
    tech.first_name || ' ' || tech.last_name AS technician_name,
    r.resolution_notes,
    r.closed_at
FROM resolutions AS r
INNER JOIN tickets AS t ON r.ticket_id = t.ticket_id
INNER JOIN hardware_assets AS h ON t.asset_id = h.asset_id
INNER JOIN asset_models AS m ON h.model_id = m.model_id
INNER JOIN technicians AS tech ON r.technician_id = tech.technician_id
WHERE r.resolution_notes IS NOT NULL;

CREATE VIEW vw_department_incidents AS
SELECT
    d.department_name,
    o.location_code,
    COUNT(DISTINCT t.ticket_id) AS resolved_tickets,
    COUNT(DISTINCT tech.technician_id) AS technicians_involved
FROM resolutions AS r
INNER JOIN tickets AS t ON r.ticket_id = t.ticket_id
INNER JOIN technicians AS tech ON r.technician_id = tech.technician_id
INNER JOIN departments AS d ON tech.department_id = d.department_id
INNER JOIN office_locations AS o ON d.location_id = o.location_id
WHERE t.status = 'RESOLVED'
GROUP BY d.department_name, o.location_code;

SELECT employee_name, department_name, location_code, ticket_title
FROM vw_open_tickets
ORDER BY department_name, employee_name;

SELECT
    v.department_name,
    v.employee_name,
    v.ticket_title,
    m.manufacturer,
    m.model_name
FROM vw_open_tickets AS v
INNER JOIN hardware_assets AS h ON v.asset_tag = h.asset_tag
INNER JOIN asset_models AS m ON h.model_id = m.model_id
ORDER BY m.manufacturer, m.model_name, v.employee_name;

SELECT
    d.department_name,
    r.technician_name,
    COUNT(r.ticket_id) AS repairs_logged
FROM vw_hardware_repairs AS r
INNER JOIN technicians AS tech ON r.technician_id = tech.technician_id
INNER JOIN departments AS d ON tech.department_id = d.department_id
WHERE r.closed_at >= DATE('now', '-30 day')
GROUP BY d.department_name, r.technician_name
ORDER BY repairs_logged DESC;

SELECT
    i.department_name,
    i.location_code,
    i.resolved_tickets,
    i.technicians_involved,
    COUNT(DISTINCT v.ticket_title) AS still_open
FROM vw_department_incidents AS i
INNER JOIN vw_open_tickets AS v ON i.department_name = v.department_name
GROUP BY i.department_name, i.location_code, i.resolved_tickets, i.technicians_involved
ORDER BY i.resolved_tickets DESC;
text_alt:
CREATE VIEW vw_open_tickets AS
SELECT
    e.first_name || ' ' || e.last_name AS employee_name,
    d.department_name,
    o.location_code,
    t.title AS ticket_title,
    h.asset_tag
FROM tickets AS t, employees AS e, departments AS d, office_locations AS o, hardware_assets AS h
WHERE t.requester_id = e.employee_id
  AND e.department_id = d.department_id
  AND d.location_id = o.location_id
  AND t.asset_id = h.asset_id
  AND t.status = 'OPEN'
  AND h.assigned_to = e.employee_id;

CREATE VIEW vw_hardware_repairs AS
SELECT
    t.ticket_id,
    m.manufacturer,
    m.model_name,
    h.asset_tag,
    tech.technician_id,
    tech.first_name || ' ' || tech.last_name AS technician_name,
    r.resolution_notes,
    r.closed_at
FROM resolutions AS r, tickets AS t, hardware_assets AS h, asset_models AS m, technicians AS tech
WHERE r.ticket_id = t.ticket_id
  AND t.asset_id = h.asset_id
  AND h.model_id = m.model_id
  AND r.technician_id = tech.technician_id
  AND r.resolution_notes IS NOT NULL;

CREATE VIEW vw_department_incidents AS
SELECT
    d.department_name,
    o.location_code,
    COUNT(DISTINCT t.ticket_id) AS resolved_tickets,
    COUNT(DISTINCT tech.technician_id) AS technicians_involved
FROM resolutions AS r, tickets AS t, technicians AS tech, departments AS d, office_locations AS o
WHERE r.ticket_id = t.ticket_id
  AND r.technician_id = tech.technician_id
  AND tech.department_id = d.department_id
  AND d.location_id = o.location_id
  AND t.status = 'RESOLVED'
GROUP BY d.department_name, o.location_code;

SELECT employee_name, department_name, location_code, ticket_title
FROM vw_open_tickets
ORDER BY department_name, employee_name;

SELECT
    v.department_name,
    v.employee_name,
    v.ticket_title,
    m.manufacturer,
    m.model_name
FROM vw_open_tickets AS v, hardware_assets AS h, asset_models AS m
WHERE v.asset_tag = h.asset_tag
  AND h.model_id = m.model_id
ORDER BY m.manufacturer, m.model_name, v.employee_name;

SELECT
    d.department_name,
    r.technician_name,
    COUNT(r.ticket_id) AS repairs_logged
FROM vw_hardware_repairs AS r, technicians AS tech, departments AS d
WHERE r.technician_id = tech.technician_id
  AND tech.department_id = d.department_id
  AND r.closed_at >= DATE('now', '-30 day')
GROUP BY d.department_name, r.technician_name
ORDER BY repairs_logged DESC;

SELECT
    i.department_name,
    i.location_code,
    i.resolved_tickets,
    i.technicians_involved,
    COUNT(DISTINCT v.ticket_title) AS still_open
FROM vw_department_incidents AS i, vw_open_tickets AS v
WHERE i.department_name = v.department_name
GROUP BY i.department_name, i.location_code, i.resolved_tickets, i.technicians_involved
ORDER BY i.resolved_tickets DESC;

text_es: Write a SQL script creating three reporting views for a local elections system, evaluating only records that possess complete reference chains across tables. The database contains `voters`, `precincts`, `districts`, `polling_stations`, `votes`, `ballots`, `candidates`, and `parties`. Create `vw_polling_logistics` linking `voters`, `precincts`, `districts`, and `polling_stations` to count registered voters per physical polling station. Create `vw_candidate_results` linking `votes`, `ballots`, `candidates`, `parties`, and `districts` to aggregate total votes per candidate and their party affiliation. Create `vw_precinct_turnout` linking `precincts`, `polling_stations`, `ballots`, and `votes` to calculate the number of cast ballots against the station capacity. Example `vw_candidate_results` output: `('Jane Doe', 'Independent', 'District 9', 14500)`.
text_nat:
-- Local elections reporting: the views expose only rows whose reference chains are
-- complete across every lookup table, so each link below is an inner join.

CREATE VIEW vw_polling_logistics AS
SELECT ps.station_id, ps.station_name, ps.address, d.district_name, p.precinct_code,
       COUNT(DISTINCT v.voter_id) AS registered_voters
FROM voters AS v
JOIN precincts AS p ON v.precinct_id = p.precinct_id
JOIN districts AS d ON p.district_id = d.district_id
JOIN polling_stations AS ps ON p.station_id = ps.station_id
GROUP BY ps.station_id, ps.station_name, ps.address, d.district_name, p.precinct_code;

CREATE VIEW vw_candidate_results AS
SELECT c.candidate_name, pa.party_name, d.district_name, COUNT(vt.vote_id) AS total_votes
FROM votes AS vt
JOIN ballots AS b ON vt.ballot_id = b.ballot_id
JOIN candidates AS c ON vt.candidate_id = c.candidate_id
JOIN parties AS pa ON c.party_id = pa.party_id
JOIN districts AS d ON c.district_id = d.district_id
GROUP BY c.candidate_id, c.candidate_name, pa.party_name, d.district_name;

CREATE VIEW vw_precinct_turnout AS
SELECT p.precinct_id, p.precinct_code, ps.station_name, ps.capacity AS station_capacity,
       COUNT(DISTINCT b.ballot_id) AS ballots_cast,
       ROUND(100.0 * COUNT(DISTINCT b.ballot_id) / NULLIF(ps.capacity, 0), 2) AS capacity_used_pct
FROM precincts AS p
JOIN polling_stations AS ps ON p.station_id = ps.station_id
JOIN ballots AS b ON b.precinct_id = p.precinct_id
JOIN votes AS vt ON vt.ballot_id = b.ballot_id
GROUP BY p.precinct_id, p.precinct_code, ps.station_name, ps.capacity;

-- Reporting queries run against the views above.

SELECT
    t.precinct_code,
    t.station_name,
    t.ballots_cast,
    t.station_capacity,
    t.capacity_used_pct,
    l.registered_voters
FROM vw_precinct_turnout AS t
JOIN vw_polling_logistics AS l ON t.precinct_code = l.precinct_code
ORDER BY t.capacity_used_pct DESC;

SELECT
    r.district_name,
    r.candidate_name,
    r.party_name,
    r.total_votes,
    l.station_name,
    l.registered_voters
FROM vw_candidate_results AS r
JOIN vw_polling_logistics AS l ON r.district_name = l.district_name
ORDER BY r.district_name, r.total_votes DESC, l.station_name;

SELECT
    ps.station_name,
    c.candidate_name,
    pa.party_name,
    COUNT(vt.vote_id) AS votes_at_station
FROM votes AS vt
JOIN ballots AS b ON vt.ballot_id = b.ballot_id
JOIN precincts AS p ON b.precinct_id = p.precinct_id
JOIN polling_stations AS ps ON p.station_id = ps.station_id
JOIN candidates AS c ON vt.candidate_id = c.candidate_id
JOIN parties AS pa ON c.party_id = pa.party_id
GROUP BY ps.station_name, c.candidate_name, pa.party_name
ORDER BY ps.station_name, votes_at_station DESC;

SELECT station_name, address, district_name, registered_voters
FROM vw_polling_logistics
ORDER BY registered_voters DESC;

SELECT candidate_name, party_name, district_name, total_votes
FROM vw_candidate_results
ORDER BY district_name, total_votes DESC;

text_es: Create a SQL stored procedure named `summarize(date)` that generates four reporting tables for a given day. The first query must link trips, riders, drivers, and vehicles to output all fully completed rides with their associated user details. The second query must combine drivers, shifts, regions, and dispatchers to calculate the total hours worked where all entities are present. The third query needs to intersect payments, trips, riders, and promotions to sum the discounts applied to valid rides, while the fourth combines vehicles, maintenance logs, mechanics, and garages to list successful repair jobs. Assume all base tables exist and only include records that have corresponding matches in all linked tables to ensure accuracy. For example, given the date string Monday, the procedure populates the four summary tables with matching records.
text_nat:
CREATE OR REPLACE PROCEDURE summarize(report_day DATE)
LANGUAGE SQL
AS $$
    DELETE FROM completed_rides_summary WHERE ride_date = report_day;
    DELETE FROM driver_hours_summary WHERE shift_date = report_day;
    DELETE FROM promo_discount_summary WHERE paid_date = report_day;
    DELETE FROM repair_job_summary WHERE repair_date = report_day;

    INSERT INTO completed_rides_summary (ride_date, trip_id, rider_name, driver_name, plate_number, fare)
    SELECT report_day, t.trip_id, r.full_name, d.full_name, v.plate_number, t.fare
    FROM trips AS t
    JOIN riders AS r ON r.rider_id = t.rider_id
    JOIN drivers AS d ON d.driver_id = t.driver_id
    JOIN vehicles AS v ON v.vehicle_id = t.vehicle_id
    WHERE t.trip_date = report_day
      AND t.status = 'COMPLETED';

    INSERT INTO driver_hours_summary (shift_date, driver_id, driver_name, region_name, dispatcher_name, total_hours)
    SELECT report_day,
           d.driver_id,
           d.full_name,
           g.region_name,
           p.full_name,
           SUM(EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM (s.ended_at - s.started_at)) / 3600.0)
    FROM shifts AS s
    JOIN drivers AS d ON d.driver_id = s.driver_id
    JOIN regions AS g ON g.region_id = s.region_id
    JOIN dispatchers AS p ON p.dispatcher_id = s.dispatcher_id
    WHERE s.shift_date = report_day
      AND s.ended_at IS NOT NULL
    GROUP BY d.driver_id, d.full_name, g.region_name, p.full_name;

    INSERT INTO promo_discount_summary (paid_date, promotion_code, rider_id, rider_name, total_discount)
    SELECT report_day,
           pr.code,
           r.rider_id,
           r.full_name,
           SUM(pay.discount_amount)
    FROM payments AS pay
    JOIN trips AS t ON t.trip_id = pay.trip_id
    JOIN riders AS r ON r.rider_id = t.rider_id
    JOIN promotions AS pr ON pr.promotion_id = pay.promotion_id
    WHERE pay.paid_on = report_day
      AND pay.status = 'CAPTURED'
      AND t.status = 'COMPLETED'
    GROUP BY pr.code, r.rider_id, r.full_name;

    INSERT INTO repair_job_summary (repair_date, log_id, plate_number, mechanic_name, garage_name, labour_cost)
    SELECT report_day, m.log_id, v.plate_number, k.full_name, ga.garage_name, m.labour_cost
    FROM maintenance_logs AS m
    JOIN vehicles AS v ON v.vehicle_id = m.vehicle_id
    JOIN mechanics AS k ON k.mechanic_id = m.mechanic_id
    JOIN garages AS ga ON ga.garage_id = k.garage_id
    WHERE m.closed_on = report_day
      AND m.outcome = 'SUCCESS';
$$;

CALL summarize(DATE '2024-04-01');

SELECT c.trip_id, c.rider_name, c.driver_name, h.total_hours, h.region_name
FROM completed_rides_summary AS c
JOIN driver_hours_summary AS h ON h.driver_name = c.driver_name
WHERE c.ride_date = DATE '2024-04-01'
  AND h.shift_date = DATE '2024-04-01'
ORDER BY c.trip_id;

SELECT d.promotion_code, d.rider_name, d.total_discount, rj.plate_number
FROM promo_discount_summary AS d
JOIN completed_rides_summary AS cr ON cr.rider_name = d.rider_name
JOIN repair_job_summary AS rj ON rj.plate_number = cr.plate_number
WHERE d.paid_date = DATE '2024-04-01'
  AND rj.repair_date = DATE '2024-04-01'
ORDER BY d.promotion_code, d.rider_name;
text_alt:
CREATE OR REPLACE PROCEDURE summarize(report_day DATE)

text_es: Write a procedure named `analyze(studio)` that populates four insight tables for a specific studio. First, link actors, roles, movies, and directors to list all main cast members and their directors for released films. Second, combine crew members, departments, movies, and equipment to detail the gear assigned to each department. Third, intersect financial backers, budgets, movies, and producers to calculate the total funding provided, and then join theaters, screenings, movies, and regions to summarize box office earnings. Require that all linked records exist to ensure complete data integrity. For example, providing a studio identifier like Paramount inserts data into the four predefined reporting structures.
text_nat:
DELIMITER $$

CREATE PROCEDURE analyze(IN studio VARCHAR(100))
BEGIN
    DELETE FROM main_cast_insight       WHERE studio_name = studio;
    DELETE FROM department_gear_insight WHERE studio_name = studio;
    DELETE FROM funding_insight         WHERE studio_name = studio;
    DELETE FROM box_office_insight      WHERE studio_name = studio;

    INSERT INTO main_cast_insight (studio_name, movie_title, actor_name, character_name, director_name)
    SELECT studio, m.title, a.full_name, r.character_name, d.full_name
    FROM actors AS a
    JOIN roles AS r ON a.actor_id = r.actor_id
    JOIN movies AS m ON r.movie_id = m.movie_id
    JOIN directors AS d ON m.director_id = d.director_id
    WHERE m.studio_name = studio
      AND r.is_main_cast = 1
      AND m.release_status = 'Released';

    INSERT INTO department_gear_insight (studio_name, movie_title, department_name, crew_member, equipment_name, quantity)
    SELECT studio, m.title, dp.department_name, c.full_name, e.equipment_name, e.quantity
    FROM crew_members AS c
    JOIN departments AS dp ON c.department_id = dp.department_id
    JOIN movies AS m ON c.movie_id = m.movie_id
    JOIN equipment AS e ON e.department_id = dp.department_id
                       AND e.movie_id = m.movie_id
    WHERE m.studio_name = studio
    ORDER BY dp.department_name, e.equipment_name;

    INSERT INTO funding_insight (studio_name, movie_title, backer_name, producer_name, total_funding)
    SELECT studio, m.title, b.backer_name, p.full_name, SUM(bg.amount)
    FROM backers AS b
    JOIN budgets AS bg ON b.backer_id = bg.backer_id
    JOIN movies AS m ON bg.movie_id = m.movie_id
    JOIN producers AS p ON m.producer_id = p.producer_id
    WHERE m.studio_name = studio
    GROUP BY m.title, b.backer_name, p.full_name
    HAVING SUM(bg.amount) > 0;

    INSERT INTO box_office_insight (studio_name, movie_title, region_name, theater_count, gross_earnings)
    SELECT studio,
           m.title,
           rg.region_name,
           COUNT(DISTINCT t.theater_id),
           SUM(s.tickets_sold * s.ticket_price)
    FROM theaters AS t
    JOIN screenings AS s ON t.theater_id = s.theater_id
    JOIN movies AS m ON s.movie_id = m.movie_id
    JOIN regions AS rg ON t.region_id = rg.region_id
    WHERE m.studio_name = studio
      AND m.release_status = 'Released'
    GROUP BY m.title, rg.region_name;
END$$

CREATE PROCEDURE refresh_all_studios()
BEGIN
    DECLARE finished INT DEFAULT 0;
    DECLARE current_studio VARCHAR(100);
    DECLARE studio_cursor CURSOR FOR
        SELECT DISTINCT st.studio_name
        FROM studios AS st
        JOIN movies AS m ON m.studio_name = st.studio_name
        WHERE m.release_status = 'Released'
        ORDER BY st.studio_name;
    DECLARE CONTINUE HANDLER FOR NOT FOUND SET finished = 1;

    OPEN studio_cursor;
    studio_loop: LOOP
        FETCH studio_cursor INTO current_studio;
        IF finished = 1 THEN
            LEAVE studio_loop;
        END IF;
        CALL analyze(current_studio);
    END LOOP;
    CLOSE studio_cursor;
END$$

DELIMITER ;

text_es: Implement a procedure called `audit(month)` that builds four casework summaries for a specific month. The first summary must connect clients, cases, lawyers, and legal departments to list active representations. The second must link courtrooms, hearings, cases, and judges to output the schedule of proceedings. The third intersects billings, cases, clients, and payment plans to calculate collected revenues, and the fourth combines paralegals, research tasks, cases, and law libraries to detail billable research hours. Ensure that only records with full associations across all mentioned entities are included. For example, providing the month October populates the four result tables with complete records.
text_nat:
DROP PROCEDURE IF EXISTS audit_overview;
DROP PROCEDURE IF EXISTS audit;
DELIMITER $$
CREATE PROCEDURE audit_overview()
BEGIN
    SELECT AR.case_number, AR.client_name, AR.lawyer_name,
           PS.room_code, PS.hearing_starts_at,
           CR.collected_amount, BR.research_hours
    FROM active_representations AS AR
    JOIN proceeding_schedule AS PS ON PS.case_number = AR.case_number
    JOIN collected_revenue AS CR ON CR.case_number = AR.case_number
    JOIN billable_research AS BR ON BR.case_number = AR.case_number
    ORDER BY AR.case_number, PS.hearing_starts_at;
END$$

CREATE PROCEDURE audit(IN p_month VARCHAR(20))
BEGIN
    DECLARE v_month_num INT;

    SET v_month_num = MONTH(STR_TO_DATE(CONCAT(p_month, ' 1 2000'), '%M %d %Y'));

    IF v_month_num IS NULL THEN
        SIGNAL SQLSTATE '45000' SET MESSAGE_TEXT = 'audit: unrecognised month name';
    END IF;

    DELETE FROM active_representations;
    DELETE FROM proceeding_schedule;
    DELETE FROM collected_revenue;
    DELETE FROM billable_research;

    INSERT INTO active_representations (client_name, case_number, lawyer_name, department_name)
    SELECT CL.full_name, CA.case_number, LW.full_name, LD.department_name
    FROM clients AS CL
    JOIN cases AS CA ON CA.client_id = CL.client_id
    JOIN lawyers AS LW ON LW.lawyer_id = CA.lead_lawyer_id
    JOIN legal_departments AS LD ON LD.department_id = LW.department_id
    WHERE MONTH(CA.opened_on) = v_month_num
      AND CA.status = 'ACTIVE';

    INSERT INTO proceeding_schedule (room_code, hearing_starts_at, case_number, judge_name)
    SELECT CR.room_code, HE.starts_at, CA.case_number, JU.full_name
    FROM courtrooms AS CR
    JOIN hearings AS HE ON HE.courtroom_id = CR.courtroom_id
    JOIN cases AS CA ON CA.case_id = HE.case_id
    JOIN judges AS JU ON JU.judge_id = HE.judge_id
    WHERE MONTH(HE.starts_at) = v_month_num
    ORDER BY HE.starts_at, CR.room_code;

    INSERT INTO collected_revenue (client_name, case_number, plan_name, collected_amount)
    SELECT CL.full_name, CA.case_number, PP.plan_name, SUM(BI.amount_paid)
    FROM billings AS BI
    JOIN cases AS CA ON CA.case_id = BI.case_id
    JOIN clients AS CL ON CL.client_id = CA.client_id
    JOIN payment_plans AS PP ON PP.plan_id = BI.plan_id
    WHERE MONTH(BI.paid_on) = v_month_num
      AND BI.amount_paid > 0
    GROUP BY CL.full_name, CA.case_number, PP.plan_name;

    INSERT INTO billable_research (paralegal_name, case_number, library_name, research_hours)
    SELECT PA.full_name, CA.case_number, LL.library_name, SUM(RT.hours_logged)
    FROM paralegals AS PA
    JOIN research_tasks AS RT ON RT.paralegal_id = PA.paralegal_id
    JOIN cases AS CA ON CA.case_id = RT.case_id
    JOIN law_libraries AS LL ON LL.library_id = RT.library_id
    WHERE MONTH(RT.logged_on) = v_month_num
      AND RT.billable = 1
    GROUP BY PA.full_name, CA.case_number, LL.library_name
    HAVING SUM(RT.hours_logged) > 0;
END$$
DELIMITER ;

text_es: Write a stored routine called `track(region)` that generates four shipping analytics sets for a specific region. The first set connects shipments, trucks, drivers, and routes to list all successfully delivered cargo. The second links depots, employees, shifts, and managers to calculate warehouse staffing hours. The third combines maintenance requests, trucks, mechanics, and parts to summarize vehicle upkeep, and the fourth intersects customers, invoices, shipments, and billing agents to tally the total freight charges paid. Include only those records that perfectly match across all joined tables. For example, given a regional code like north, the procedure inserts records into four analytics destinations.
text_nat:
DELIMITER $$

DROP PROCEDURE IF EXISTS track $$

CREATE PROCEDURE track(IN region VARCHAR(32))
BEGIN
    DELETE FROM delivered_cargo_analytics WHERE region_code = region;
    DELETE FROM staffing_hours_analytics WHERE region_code = region;
    DELETE FROM vehicle_upkeep_analytics WHERE region_code = region;
    DELETE FROM freight_charge_analytics WHERE region_code = region;

    INSERT INTO delivered_cargo_analytics
        (region_code, shipment_id, truck_plate, driver_name, route_name, cargo_weight)
    SELECT region, s.shipment_id, t.plate_number, d.full_name, r.route_name, s.cargo_weight
    FROM shipments AS s
    INNER JOIN trucks AS t ON t.truck_id = s.truck_id
    INNER JOIN drivers AS d ON d.driver_id = s.driver_id
    INNER JOIN routes AS r ON r.route_id = s.route_id
    WHERE r.region_code = region
      AND s.status = 'DELIVERED';

    INSERT INTO staffing_hours_analytics
        (region_code, depot_id, depot_name, employee_id, employee_name, manager_name, total_hours)
    SELECT region, dp.depot_id, dp.depot_name, e.employee_id, e.full_name, m.full_name,
           SUM(TIMESTAMPDIFF(MINUTE, sh.shift_start, sh.shift_end) / 60.0)
    FROM depots AS dp
    INNER JOIN employees AS e ON e.depot_id = dp.depot_id
    INNER JOIN shifts AS sh ON sh.employee_id = e.employee_id
    INNER JOIN managers AS m ON m.manager_id = e.manager_id
    WHERE dp.region_code = region
      AND sh.shift_end IS NOT NULL
    GROUP BY dp.depot_id, dp.depot_name, e.employee_id, e.full_name, m.full_name;

    INSERT INTO vehicle_upkeep_analytics
        (region_code, request_id, truck_plate, mechanic_name, part_name, part_quantity, part_cost)
    SELECT region, mr.request_id, t.plate_number, mc.full_name, p.part_name,
           mr.part_quantity, p.unit_cost * mr.part_quantity
    FROM maintenance_requests AS mr
    INNER JOIN trucks AS t ON t.truck_id = mr.truck_id
    INNER JOIN mechanics AS mc ON mc.mechanic_id = mr.mechanic_id
    INNER JOIN parts AS p ON p.part_id = mr.part_id
    WHERE t.region_code = region
      AND mr.status = 'COMPLETED';

    INSERT INTO freight_charge_analytics
        (region_code, customer_id, customer_name, agent_name, invoice_count, total_paid)
    SELECT region, c.customer_id, c.customer_name, ba.agent_name,
           COUNT(DISTINCT i.invoice_id), SUM(i.amount_paid)
    FROM customers AS c
    INNER JOIN invoices AS i ON i.customer_id = c.customer_id
    INNER JOIN shipments AS s ON s.shipment_id = i.shipment_id
    INNER JOIN billing_agents AS ba ON ba.agent_id = i.agent_id
    WHERE c.region_code = region
      AND i.payment_status = 'PAID'
      AND s.status = 'DELIVERED'
    GROUP BY c.customer_id, c.customer_name, ba.agent_name;
END $$

DELIMITER ;

CALL track('north');

SELECT dca.shipment_id, dca.driver_name, dca.route_name, fca.customer_name, fca.total_paid
FROM delivered_cargo_analytics AS dca
INNER JOIN invoices AS i ON i.shipment_id = dca.shipment_id
INNER JOIN freight_charge_analytics AS fca ON fca.customer_id = i.customer_id
WHERE dca.region_code = 'north'
  AND fca.region_code = 'north'
ORDER BY dca.shipment_id;

SELECT sha.depot_name, sha.manager_name, SUM(sha.total_hours) AS depot_hours,
       SUM(vua.part_cost) AS upkeep_cost
FROM staffing_hours_analytics AS sha
INNER JOIN depots AS dp ON dp.depot_id = sha.depot_id
INNER JOIN trucks AS t ON t.depot_id = dp.depot_id
INNER JOIN vehicle_upkeep_analytics AS vua ON vua.truck_plate = t.plate_number
WHERE sha.region_code = 'north'
GROUP BY sha.depot_name, sha.manager_name
ORDER BY sha.depot_name;

DELIMITER $$

DROP PROCEDURE IF EXISTS track $$

CREATE PROCEDURE track(IN region VARCHAR(32))
BEGIN
    DELETE FROM delivered_cargo_analytics WHERE region_code = region;
    DELETE FROM staffing_hours_analytics WHERE region_code = region;
    DELETE FROM vehicle_upkeep_analytics WHERE region_code = region;
    DELETE FROM freight_charge_analytics WHERE region_code = region;

    INSERT INTO delivered_cargo_analytics
        (region_code, shipment_id, truck_plate, driver_name, route_name, cargo_weight)
    SELECT region, s.shipment_id, t.plate_number, d.full_name, r.route_name, s.cargo_weight
    FROM shipments AS s, trucks AS t, drivers AS d, routes AS r
    WHERE t.truck_id = s.truck_id
      AND d.driver_id = s.driver_id
      AND r.route_id = s.route_id
      AND r.region_code = region
      AND s.status = 'DELIVERED';

    INSERT INTO staffing_hours_analytics
        (region_code, depot_id, depot_name, employee_id, employee_name, manager_name, total_hours)
    SELECT region, dp.depot_id, dp.depot_name, e.employee_id, e.full_name, m.full_name,
           SUM(TIMESTAMPDIFF(MINUTE, sh.shift_start, sh.shift_end) / 60.0)
    FROM depots AS dp, employees AS e, shifts AS sh, managers AS m
    WHERE e.depot_id = dp.depot_id
      AND sh.employee_id = e.employee_id
      AND m.manager_id = e.manager_id
      AND dp.region_code = region
      AND sh.shift_end IS NOT NULL
    GROUP BY dp.depot_id, dp.depot_name, e.employee_id, e.full_name, m.full_name;

    INSERT INTO vehicle_upkeep_analytics
        (region_code, request_id, truck_plate, mechanic_name, part_name, part_quantity, part_cost)
    SELECT region, mr.request_id, t.plate_number, mc.full_name, p.part_name,
           mr.part_quantity, p.unit_cost * mr.part_quantity
    FROM maintenance_requests AS mr, trucks AS t, mechanics AS mc, parts AS p
    WHERE t.truck_id = mr.truck_id
      AND mc.mechanic_id = mr.mechanic_id
      AND p.part_id = mr.part_id
      AND t.region_code = region
      AND mr.status = 'COMPLETED';

    INSERT INTO freight_charge_analytics
        (region_code, customer_id, customer_name, agent_name, invoice_count, total_paid)
    SELECT region, c.customer_id, c.customer_name, ba.agent_name,
           COUNT(DISTINCT i.invoice_id), SUM(i.amount_paid)
    FROM customers AS c, invoices AS i, shipments AS s, billing_agents AS ba
    WHERE i.customer_id = c.customer_id
      AND s.shipment_id = i.shipment_id
      AND ba.agent_id = i.agent_id
      AND c.region_code = region
      AND i.payment_status = 'PAID'
      AND s.status = 'DELIVERED'
    GROUP BY c.customer_id, c.customer_name, ba.agent_name;
END $$

DELIMITER ;

CALL track('north');

SELECT dca.shipment_id, dca.driver_name, dca.route_name, fca.customer_name, fca.total_paid
FROM delivered_cargo_analytics AS dca, invoices AS i, freight_charge_analytics AS fca
WHERE i.shipment_id = dca.shipment_id
  AND fca.customer_id = i.customer_id
  AND dca.region_code = 'north'
  AND fca.region_code = 'north'
ORDER BY dca.shipment_id;

SELECT sha.depot_name, sha.manager_name, SUM(sha.total_hours) AS depot_hours,
       SUM(vua.part_cost) AS upkeep_cost
FROM staffing_hours_analytics AS sha, depots AS dp, trucks AS t, vehicle_upkeep_analytics AS vua
WHERE dp.depot_id = sha.depot_id
  AND t.depot_id = dp.depot_id
  AND vua.truck_plate = t.plate_number
  AND sha.region_code = 'north'
GROUP BY sha.depot_name, sha.manager_name
ORDER BY sha.depot_name;

text_es: Develop a SQL procedure named `curate(quarter)` that produces four museum operations summaries for a given quarter. First, link artifacts, exhibitions, galleries, and curators to catalog the items currently on display. Second, combine donors, donations, artifacts, and appraisers to list the acquired historical pieces. Third, intersect tickets, visitors, exhibitions, and guides to calculate tour attendance figures, and fourth, join preservation logs, artifacts, conservators, and laboratories to detail the restoration work completed. Restrict the data to entries that possess valid matches across all related entities. For example, providing the quarter number two populates the four curation summary tables.
text_nat:
DELIMITER //

CREATE PROCEDURE curate(IN quarter TINYINT)
BEGIN
    IF quarter IS NULL OR quarter < 1 OR quarter > 4 THEN
        SIGNAL SQLSTATE '45000' SET MESSAGE_TEXT = 'quarter must be between 1 and 4';
    END IF;

    DELETE FROM display_catalog WHERE report_quarter = quarter;
    DELETE FROM acquisition_summary WHERE report_quarter = quarter;
    DELETE FROM tour_attendance WHERE report_quarter = quarter;
    DELETE FROM restoration_detail WHERE report_quarter = quarter;

    INSERT INTO display_catalog (report_quarter, artifact_id, artifact_name, exhibition_name, gallery_name, curator_name)
    SELECT quarter, a.artifact_id, a.artifact_name, e.exhibition_name, g.gallery_name,
           CONCAT(c.first_name, ' ', c.last_name)
    FROM artifacts AS a
    JOIN exhibitions AS e ON a.exhibition_id = e.exhibition_id
    JOIN galleries AS g ON e.gallery_id = g.gallery_id
    JOIN curators AS c ON g.curator_id = c.curator_id
    WHERE QUARTER(e.opening_date) = quarter
      AND a.on_display = 1;

    INSERT INTO acquisition_summary (report_quarter, donation_id, donor_name, artifact_name, appraised_value, appraiser_name)
    SELECT quarter, d.donation_id, dn.donor_name, a.artifact_name, d.appraised_value,
           CONCAT(ap.first_name, ' ', ap.last_name)
    FROM donations AS d
    JOIN donors AS dn ON d.donor_id = dn.donor_id
    JOIN artifacts AS a ON d.artifact_id = a.artifact_id
    JOIN appraisers AS ap ON d.appraiser_id = ap.appraiser_id
    WHERE QUARTER(d.donation_date) = quarter
      AND a.era IS NOT NULL;

    INSERT INTO tour_attendance (report_quarter, exhibition_name, guide_name, visitor_count, ticket_revenue)
    SELECT quarter, e.exhibition_name, CONCAT(gd.first_name, ' ', gd.last_name),
           COUNT(DISTINCT v.visitor_id), SUM(t.price)
    FROM tickets AS t
    JOIN visitors AS v ON t.visitor_id = v.visitor_id
    JOIN exhibitions AS e ON t.exhibition_id = e.exhibition_id
    JOIN guides AS gd ON t.guide_id = gd.guide_id
    WHERE QUARTER(t.visit_date) = quarter
    GROUP BY e.exhibition_name, gd.guide_id, gd.first_name, gd.last_name;

    INSERT INTO restoration_detail (report_quarter, log_id, artifact_name, conservator_name, laboratory_name, treatment, hours_spent)
    SELECT quarter, p.log_id, a.artifact_name,
           CONCAT(cs.first_name, ' ', cs.last_name), l.laboratory_name, p.treatment, p.hours_spent
    FROM preservation_logs AS p
    JOIN artifacts AS a ON p.artifact_id = a.artifact_id
    JOIN conservators AS cs ON p.conservator_id = cs.conservator_id
    JOIN laboratories AS l ON cs.laboratory_id = l.laboratory_id
    WHERE QUARTER(p.completed_date) = quarter
      AND p.status = 'COMPLETED';
END //

CREATE PROCEDURE curation_report(IN quarter TINYINT)
BEGIN
    CALL curate(quarter);

    SELECT dc.gallery_name, dc.curator_name, COUNT(*) AS items_on_display, SUM(asum.appraised_value) AS display_value
    FROM display_catalog AS dc
    JOIN acquisition_summary AS asum ON dc.artifact_name = asum.artifact_name
    WHERE dc.report_quarter = quarter
      AND asum.report_quarter = quarter
    GROUP BY dc.gallery_name, dc.curator_name;

    SELECT ta.exhibition_name, ta.guide_name, ta.visitor_count, SUM(rd.hours_spent) AS restoration_hours
    FROM tour_attendance AS ta
    JOIN display_catalog AS dc ON ta.exhibition_name = dc.exhibition_name
    JOIN restoration_detail AS rd ON dc.artifact_name = rd.artifact_name
    WHERE ta.report_quarter = quarter
      AND rd.report_quarter = quarter
    GROUP BY ta.exhibition_name, ta.guide_name, ta.visitor_count;
END //

DELIMITER ;

CALL curation_report(2);

text_es: Write a routine called `publish(genre)` that populates four literary distribution reports for a given genre. The first report links authors, books, editors, and publishing imprints to list all finalized manuscripts. The second connects printers, print runs, books, and warehouses to track the physical inventory produced. The third combines distributors, shipments, books, and retail partners to summarize the outbound logistics, and the fourth intersects reviewers, promotional campaigns, books, and publicists to gauge media coverage. Exclude any orphaned records by enforcing strict relational matches across all sets. For example, providing the genre string fiction populates the four statistics tables with matched data.
text_nat:
DELIMITER $$

CREATE PROCEDURE load_manuscript_stats(IN p_genre VARCHAR(40))
BEGIN
    DELETE FROM manuscript_stats WHERE genre = p_genre;
    INSERT INTO manuscript_stats (genre, author_name, book_title, editor_name, imprint_name)
    SELECT b.genre, a.full_name, b.title, e.full_name, i.imprint_name
    FROM books AS b
    JOIN authors AS a ON a.author_id = b.author_id
    JOIN editors AS e ON e.editor_id = b.editor_id
    JOIN imprints AS i ON i.imprint_id = b.imprint_id
    WHERE b.genre = p_genre
      AND b.status = 'finalized';
END$$

CREATE PROCEDURE load_inventory_stats(IN p_genre VARCHAR(40))
BEGIN
    DELETE FROM inventory_stats WHERE genre = p_genre;
    INSERT INTO inventory_stats (genre, printer_name, book_title, warehouse_name, copies_printed)
    SELECT b.genre, p.printer_name, b.title, w.warehouse_name, SUM(r.copies)
    FROM print_runs AS r
    JOIN books AS b ON b.book_id = r.book_id
    JOIN printers AS p ON p.printer_id = r.printer_id
    JOIN warehouses AS w ON w.warehouse_id = r.warehouse_id
    WHERE b.genre = p_genre
    GROUP BY b.genre, p.printer_name, b.title, w.warehouse_name;
END$$

CREATE PROCEDURE load_logistics_stats(IN p_genre VARCHAR(40))
BEGIN
    DELETE FROM logistics_stats WHERE genre = p_genre;
    INSERT INTO logistics_stats (genre, distributor_name, book_title, retailer_name, units_shipped, shipment_count)
    SELECT b.genre, d.distributor_name, b.title, rp.partner_name, SUM(s.units), COUNT(*)
    FROM shipments AS s
    JOIN books AS b ON b.book_id = s.book_id
    JOIN distributors AS d ON d.distributor_id = s.distributor_id
    JOIN retail_partners AS rp ON rp.partner_id = s.partner_id
    WHERE b.genre = p_genre
    GROUP BY b.genre, d.distributor_name, b.title, rp.partner_name;
END$$

CREATE PROCEDURE load_coverage_stats(IN p_genre VARCHAR(40))
BEGIN
    DELETE FROM coverage_stats WHERE genre = p_genre;
    INSERT INTO coverage_stats (genre, reviewer_name, book_title, publicist_name, campaign_name, avg_score)
    SELECT b.genre, rv.reviewer_name, b.title, pu.publicist_name, c.campaign_name, AVG(rv.score)
    FROM reviews AS rv
    JOIN books AS b ON b.book_id = rv.book_id
    JOIN campaigns AS c ON c.campaign_id = rv.campaign_id
    JOIN publicists AS pu ON pu.publicist_id = c.publicist_id
    WHERE b.genre = p_genre
      AND c.book_id = b.book_id
    GROUP BY b.genre, rv.reviewer_name, b.title, pu.publicist_name, c.campaign_name;
END$$

CREATE PROCEDURE publish(IN genre VARCHAR(40))
BEGIN
    DECLARE known_genre INT DEFAULT 0;

    SELECT COUNT(*) INTO known_genre
    FROM books AS b
    JOIN authors AS a ON a.author_id = b.author_id
    WHERE b.genre = genre;

    IF known_genre = 0 THEN
        SIGNAL SQLSTATE '45000'
            SET MESSAGE_TEXT = 'no authored titles exist for the requested genre';
    END IF;

    START TRANSACTION;
    CALL load_manuscript_stats(genre);
    CALL load_inventory_stats(genre);
    CALL load_logistics_stats(genre);
    CALL load_coverage_stats(genre);
    COMMIT;
END$$

DELIMITER ;

CALL publish('fiction');
