text_es: Write a social services tracking script anchored by the function monitor(region) to generate three operational summaries for a child welfare agency. Map the current placements by associating the foster children with their approved foster families, their assigned social workers, their mandatory monthly case visits, and their upcoming family court dates in the provided region. Ensure medical compliance by connecting the foster children to their historical medical records, the regional pediatric clinics, the prescribed medication logs, and the specialized trauma counselors. Evaluate foster family retention by linking the approved foster families to their initial background check clearances, the required training seminars they attended, and the support group facilitators. Example input: southern district. Example output: lists of placement statuses, medical compliance alerts, and family retention metrics.
text_nat:
-- Social services tracking module for a child welfare agency: schema, the
-- summary views behind monitor(region), and a driver for one region.
CREATE TABLE Regions (region_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, region_name TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE);
CREATE TABLE FosterFamilies (family_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, family_name TEXT NOT NULL, region_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES Regions(region_id), approved_on DATE NOT NULL, license_status TEXT NOT NULL);
CREATE TABLE SocialWorkers (worker_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, worker_name TEXT NOT NULL, region_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES Regions(region_id), caseload_cap INTEGER NOT NULL);
CREATE TABLE FosterChildren (child_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, child_name TEXT NOT NULL, date_of_birth DATE NOT NULL, family_id INTEGER REFERENCES FosterFamilies(family_id), worker_id INTEGER REFERENCES SocialWorkers(worker_id), placement_start DATE NOT NULL, placement_state TEXT NOT NULL);
CREATE TABLE CaseVisits (visit_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, child_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES FosterChildren(child_id), visit_date DATE NOT NULL, visit_outcome TEXT NOT NULL);
CREATE TABLE CourtDates (hearing_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, child_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES FosterChildren(child_id), hearing_date DATE NOT NULL, hearing_type TEXT NOT NULL);
CREATE TABLE PediatricClinics (clinic_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, clinic_name TEXT NOT NULL, region_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES Regions(region_id));
CREATE TABLE MedicalRecords (record_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, child_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES FosterChildren(child_id), clinic_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES PediatricClinics(clinic_id), exam_date DATE NOT NULL, immunizations_current INTEGER NOT NULL);
CREATE TABLE MedicationLogs (log_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, record_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES MedicalRecords(record_id), medication TEXT NOT NULL, refill_due DATE, adherence_pct INTEGER NOT NULL);
CREATE TABLE TraumaCounselors (counselor_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, counselor_name TEXT NOT NULL, specialty TEXT NOT NULL);
CREATE TABLE CounselingAssignments (child_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES FosterChildren(child_id), counselor_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES TraumaCounselors(counselor_id), sessions_held INTEGER NOT NULL, PRIMARY KEY (child_id, counselor_id));
CREATE TABLE BackgroundChecks (check_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, family_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES FosterFamilies(family_id), cleared_on DATE, clearance_level TEXT NOT NULL);
CREATE TABLE TrainingSeminars (seminar_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, seminar_title TEXT NOT NULL, required_hours INTEGER NOT NULL);
CREATE TABLE SeminarAttendance (family_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES FosterFamilies(family_id), seminar_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES TrainingSeminars(seminar_id), attended_on DATE NOT NULL, PRIMARY KEY (family_id, seminar_id));
CREATE TABLE SupportGroups (group_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, facilitator TEXT NOT NULL, family_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES FosterFamilies(family_id), meetings_hosted INTEGER NOT NULL);
-- Each child resolved to its approved family, region and assigned worker.
CREATE VIEW ChildPlacement AS
SELECT R.region_name, C.child_id, C.child_name, C.placement_state,
       F.family_name, F.license_status, W.worker_name
FROM FosterChildren AS C
JOIN FosterFamilies AS F ON C.family_id = F.family_id
JOIN Regions AS R ON F.region_id = R.region_id
JOIN SocialWorkers AS W ON C.worker_id = W.worker_id;
-- Medication logs hang off medical records, so roll them up per child.
CREATE VIEW MedicationAdherence AS
SELECT M.child_id, MIN(L.adherence_pct) AS worst_adherence,
       MIN(L.refill_due) AS earliest_refill_due
FROM MedicationLogs AS L
JOIN MedicalRecords AS M ON L.record_id = M.record_id
GROUP BY M.child_id;
CREATE VIEW CounselingLoad AS
SELECT A.child_id, CO.counselor_name, CO.specialty, SUM(A.sessions_held) AS sessions_held
FROM CounselingAssignments AS A
JOIN TraumaCounselors AS CO ON A.counselor_id = CO.counselor_id
GROUP BY A.child_id, CO.counselor_name, CO.specialty;
CREATE VIEW TrainingProgress AS
SELECT SA.family_id, COUNT(*) AS seminars_attended, SUM(T.required_hours) AS training_hours
FROM SeminarAttendance AS SA
JOIN TrainingSeminars AS T ON SA.seminar_id = T.seminar_id
GROUP BY SA.family_id;
-- Summary 1: placement map with visit history and the next court date.
CREATE VIEW PlacementStatus AS
SELECT P.region_name, P.child_id, P.child_name, P.family_name, P.license_status,
       P.worker_name, P.placement_state,
       (SELECT MAX(V.visit_date) FROM CaseVisits AS V WHERE V.child_id = P.child_id) AS last_visit,
       (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM CaseVisits AS V WHERE V.child_id = P.child_id) AS visits_logged,
       (SELECT MIN(H.hearing_date) FROM CourtDates AS H WHERE H.child_id = P.child_id
          AND H.hearing_date >= DATE('now')) AS next_hearing
FROM ChildPlacement AS P;
-- Summary 2: medical compliance, keyed on the clinic's region.
CREATE VIEW MedicalCompliance AS
SELECT R.region_name, C.child_id, C.child_name, CL.clinic_name,
       MAX(M.exam_date) AS latest_exam,
       MIN(M.immunizations_current) AS immunizations_current,
       (SELECT MA.worst_adherence FROM MedicationAdherence AS MA
          WHERE MA.child_id = C.child_id) AS worst_adherence,
       (SELECT MA.earliest_refill_due FROM MedicationAdherence AS MA
          WHERE MA.child_id = C.child_id) AS earliest_refill_due,
       (SELECT CO.counselor_name FROM CounselingLoad AS CO WHERE CO.child_id = C.child_id
          ORDER BY CO.sessions_held DESC LIMIT 1) AS counselor_name,
       (SELECT COALESCE(SUM(CO.sessions_held), 0) FROM CounselingLoad AS CO
          WHERE CO.child_id = C.child_id) AS sessions_held
FROM FosterChildren AS C
JOIN MedicalRecords AS M ON M.child_id = C.child_id
JOIN PediatricClinics AS CL ON M.clinic_id = CL.clinic_id
JOIN Regions AS R ON CL.region_id = R.region_id
GROUP BY R.region_name, C.child_id, C.child_name, CL.clinic_name;
-- Summary 3: retention metrics per approved foster family.
CREATE VIEW FamilyRetention AS
SELECT R.region_name, F.family_id, F.family_name, F.approved_on,
       (SELECT B.clearance_level FROM BackgroundChecks AS B WHERE B.family_id = F.family_id
          ORDER BY B.cleared_on LIMIT 1) AS clearance_level,
       (SELECT MIN(B.cleared_on) FROM BackgroundChecks AS B
          WHERE B.family_id = F.family_id) AS cleared_on,
       (SELECT COALESCE(TP.seminars_attended, 0) FROM TrainingProgress AS TP
          WHERE TP.family_id = F.family_id) AS seminars_attended,
       (SELECT COALESCE(TP.training_hours, 0) FROM TrainingProgress AS TP
          WHERE TP.family_id = F.family_id) AS training_hours,
       (SELECT G.facilitator FROM SupportGroups AS G WHERE G.family_id = F.family_id
          ORDER BY G.meetings_hosted DESC LIMIT 1) AS facilitator,
       (SELECT COALESCE(SUM(G.meetings_hosted), 0) FROM SupportGroups AS G
          WHERE G.family_id = F.family_id) AS support_meetings
FROM FosterFamilies AS F
JOIN Regions AS R ON F.region_id = R.region_id;
-- monitor('southern district'): the three operational summaries.
SELECT * FROM PlacementStatus WHERE region_name = 'southern district'
ORDER BY next_hearing, child_name;
SELECT * FROM MedicalCompliance WHERE region_name = 'southern district'
  AND (immunizations_current = 0 OR worst_adherence < 85 OR sessions_held = 0)
ORDER BY earliest_refill_due, child_name;
SELECT * FROM FamilyRetention WHERE region_name = 'southern district'
ORDER BY training_hours DESC, family_name;

Schema: Events (event_id INT, event_name VARCHAR, event_date DATE, location VARCHAR), RSVPs (rsvp_id INT, event_id INT, participant_name VARCHAR, attendance_status VARCHAR).

Queries:
1. List all events and their locations.
2. Find all participants for a specific event (e.g., 'Annual Gala').
3. Count the number of 'Attending' RSVPs for each event.
4. Add a new event.
5. Update a participant's RSVP status.

CREATE TABLE Events (
    event_id INT PRIMARY KEY,
    event_name VARCHAR(255),
    event_date DATE,
    location VARCHAR(255)
);

CREATE TABLE RSVPs (
    rsvp_id INT PRIMARY KEY,
    event_id INT,
    participant_name VARCHAR(255),
    attendance_status VARCHAR(50),
    FOREIGN KEY (event_id) REFERENCES Events(event_id)
);

Schema: Teams (team_id INT, team_name VARCHAR, city VARCHAR), Players (player_id INT, first_name VARCHAR, last_name VARCHAR, team_id INT, position VARCHAR, jersey_number INT).

Queries:
1. List all players and their teams.
2. Find all players on a specific team (e.g., 'Lakers').
3. Count the number of players per position.
4. Add a new player to a team.
5. Update a player's position.
text_nat:
CREATE TABLE Teams (
    team_id   INT PRIMARY KEY,
    team_name VARCHAR(50) NOT NULL,
    city      VARCHAR(50) NOT NULL
);

CREATE TABLE Players (
    player_id     INT PRIMARY KEY,
    first_name    VARCHAR(50) NOT NULL,
    last_name     VARCHAR(50) NOT NULL,
    team_id       INT REFERENCES Teams(team_id),
    position      VARCHAR(20),
    jersey_number INT
);

INSERT INTO Teams (team_id, team_name, city) VALUES
    (1, 'Lakers', 'Los Angeles'),
    (2, 'Celtics', 'Boston'),
    (3, 'Bulls', 'Chicago');

INSERT INTO Players (player_id, first_name, last_name, team_id, position, jersey_number) VALUES
    (10, 'Alan', 'Reyes', 1, 'Guard', 3),
    (11, 'Bruno', 'Kessler', 1, 'Center', 14),
    (12, 'Caleb', 'Ortiz', 1, 'Forward', 23),
    (13, 'Dmitri', 'Volkov', 2, 'Guard', 7),
    (14, 'Elias', 'Park', 2, 'Forward', 21),
    (15, 'Farid', 'Nasser', 3, 'Center', 33);

-- 1. All players with the team and city they play for.
CREATE VIEW v_player_roster AS
SELECT p.player_id, p.first_name || ' ' || p.last_name AS player_name,
       p.position, p.jersey_number, t.team_name, t.city
FROM Players p
INNER JOIN Teams t ON t.team_id = p.team_id;

SELECT player_name, position, jersey_number, team_name, city
FROM v_player_roster ORDER BY team_name, jersey_number;

-- 2. Players on a specific team, selected by team name.
SELECT p.jersey_number, p.first_name, p.last_name, p.position
FROM Players p
INNER JOIN Teams t ON t.team_id = p.team_id
WHERE t.team_name = 'Lakers' ORDER BY p.jersey_number;

-- 3. Number of players per position, then the same breakdown per team.
SELECT position, COUNT(*) AS player_count
FROM Players GROUP BY position ORDER BY player_count DESC, position;

SELECT t.team_name, p.position, COUNT(*) AS player_count
FROM Teams t
INNER JOIN Players p ON p.team_id = t.team_id
GROUP BY t.team_name, p.position ORDER BY t.team_name, p.position;

-- Teammates of a given player.
SELECT mate.jersey_number, mate.first_name, mate.last_name, mate.position
FROM Players me
INNER JOIN Players mate ON mate.team_id = me.team_id AND mate.player_id <> me.player_id
WHERE me.last_name = 'Reyes' ORDER BY mate.jersey_number;

-- 4. Add a new player, resolving the team by name instead of hard-coding the id.
INSERT INTO Players (player_id, first_name, last_name, team_id, position, jersey_number)
SELECT 17, 'Hugo', 'Mercier', t.team_id, 'Forward', 11
FROM Teams t WHERE t.team_name = 'Celtics';

SELECT p.first_name, p.last_name, p.position, t.team_name
FROM Players p
INNER JOIN Teams t ON t.team_id = p.team_id
WHERE p.player_id = 17;

-- 5. Update a player's position and read the result back.
UPDATE Players SET position = 'Point Guard' WHERE player_id = 10;

SELECT p.first_name, p.last_name, p.position, t.team_name
FROM Players p
INNER JOIN Teams t ON t.team_id = p.team_id
WHERE p.player_id = 10;

-- Jersey numbers must be unique inside a team; list any collisions.
SELECT t.team_name, a.jersey_number, a.last_name AS player_a, b.last_name AS player_b
FROM Players a
INNER JOIN Players b ON b.team_id = a.team_id AND b.jersey_number = a.jersey_number
INNER JOIN Teams t ON t.team_id = a.team_id
WHERE a.player_id < b.player_id ORDER BY t.team_name, a.jersey_number;

-- Squad report: roster size and captain (lowest jersey number) per team.
SELECT t.city || ' ' || t.team_name AS squad, COUNT(p.player_id) AS squad_size,
       MIN(p.jersey_number) AS captain_number
FROM Teams t
INNER JOIN Players p ON p.team_id = t.team_id
GROUP BY t.city, t.team_name ORDER BY squad_size DESC, squad;

CREATE TABLE Teams (
    team_id   INT PRIMARY KEY,
    team_name VARCHAR(50) NOT NULL,
    city      VARCHAR(50) NOT NULL
);

CREATE TABLE Players (
    player_id     INT PRIMARY KEY,
    first_name    VARCHAR(50) NOT NULL,
    last_name     VARCHAR(50) NOT NULL,
    team_id       INT REFERENCES Teams(team_id),
    position      VARCHAR(20),
    jersey_number INT
);

INSERT INTO Teams (team_id, team_name, city) VALUES
    (1, 'Lakers', 'Los Angeles'),
    (2, 'Celtics', 'Boston'),
    (3, 'Bulls', 'Chicago');

INSERT INTO Players (player_id, first_name, last_name, team_id, position, jersey_number) VALUES
    (10, 'Alan', 'Reyes', 1, 'Guard', 3),
    (11, 'Bruno', 'Kessler', 1, 'Center', 14),
    (12, 'Caleb', 'Ortiz', 1, 'Forward', 23),
    (13, 'Dmitri', 'Volkov', 2, 'Guard', 7),
    (14, 'Elias', 'Park', 2, 'Forward', 21),
    (15, 'Farid', 'Nasser', 3, 'Center', 33);

-- 1. All players with the team and city they play for.
CREATE VIEW v_player_roster AS
SELECT p.player_id, p.first_name || ' ' || p.last_name AS player_name,
       p.position, p.jersey_number, t.team_name, t.city
FROM Players p, Teams t
WHERE t.team_id = p.team_id;

SELECT player_name, position, jersey_number, team_name, city
FROM v_player_roster ORDER BY team_name, jersey_number;

-- 2. Players on a specific team, selected by team name.
SELECT p.jersey_number, p.first_name, p.last_name, p.position
FROM Players p, Teams t
WHERE t.team_id = p.team_id
AND t.team_name = 'Lakers' ORDER BY p.jersey_number;

-- 3. Number of players per position, then the same breakdown per team.
SELECT position, COUNT(*) AS player_count
FROM Players GROUP BY position ORDER BY player_count DESC, position;

SELECT t.team_name, p.position, COUNT(*) AS player_count
FROM Teams t, Players p
WHERE p.team_id = t.team_id
GROUP BY t.team_name, p.position ORDER BY t.team_name, p.position;

-- Teammates of a given player.
SELECT mate.jersey_number, mate.first_name, mate.last_name, mate.position
FROM Players me, Players mate
WHERE mate.team_id = me.team_id AND mate.player_id <> me.player_id
AND me.last_name = 'Reyes' ORDER BY mate.jersey_number;

-- 4. Add a new player, resolving the team by name instead of hard-coding the id.
INSERT INTO Players (player_id, first_name, last_name, team_id, position, jersey_number)
SELECT 17, 'Hugo', 'Mercier', t.team_id, 'Forward', 11
FROM Teams t WHERE t.team_name = 'Celtics';

SELECT p.first_name, p.last_name, p.position, t.team_name
FROM Players p, Teams t
WHERE t.team_id = p.team_id
AND p.player_id = 17;

-- 5. Update a player's position and read the result back.
UPDATE Players SET position = 'Point Guard' WHERE player_id = 10;

SELECT p.first_name, p.last_name, p.position, t.team_name
FROM Players p, Teams t
WHERE t.team_id = p.team_id
AND p.player_id = 10;

-- Jersey numbers must be unique inside a team; list any collisions.
SELECT t.team_name, a.jersey_number, a.last_name AS player_a, b.last_name AS player_b
FROM Players a, Players b, Teams t
WHERE b.team_id = a.team_id AND b.jersey_number = a.jersey_number
AND t.team_id = a.team_id
AND a.player_id < b.player_id ORDER BY t.team_name, a.jersey_number;

-- Squad report: roster size and captain (lowest jersey number) per team.
SELECT t.city || ' ' || t.team_name AS squad, COUNT(p.player_id) AS squad_size,
       MIN(p.jersey_number) AS captain_number
FROM Teams t, Players p
WHERE p.team_id = t.team_id
GROUP BY t.city, t.team_name ORDER BY squad_size DESC, squad;

Schema: Applicants (applicant_id INT, first_name VARCHAR, last_name VARCHAR, email VARCHAR), Jobs (job_id INT, job_title VARCHAR, department VARCHAR, salary_range VARCHAR), Applications (application_id INT, applicant_id INT, job_id INT, application_date DATE, status VARCHAR).

Queries:
1. Select all applications and their corresponding job titles.
2. Find all applicants for a specific job (e.g., job_title = 'Software Engineer').
3. Count the number of applications per job status.
4. Submit a new job application.
5. Update an application's status to 'Interviewing'.
text_nat:
SELECT
  A.application_id,
  A.application_date,
  A.status,
  J.job_title
FROM Applications AS A
JOIN Jobs AS J
  ON A.job_id = J.job_id;

SELECT
  Ap.first_name,
  Ap.last_name,
  Ap.email
FROM Applicants AS Ap
JOIN Applications AS App
  ON Ap.applicant_id = App.applicant_id
JOIN Jobs AS Jb
  ON App.job_id = Jb.job_id
WHERE
  Jb.job_title = 'Software Engineer';

SELECT
  status,
  COUNT(*) AS application_count
FROM Applications
GROUP BY
  status;

Schema: Customers (customer_id INT, username VARCHAR, email VARCHAR), Products (product_id INT, product_name VARCHAR, price DECIMAL), Carts (cart_id INT, customer_id INT, creation_date DATE), CartItems (cart_item_id INT, cart_id INT, product_id INT, quantity INT).

Queries:
1. Select all customers and their active carts.
2. Find all products in a specific customer's cart (e.g., customer_id = 12).
3. Calculate the total value of items in a specific cart.
4. Add a product to a cart.
5. Update the quantity of a product in a cart.
text_nat:
SELECT c.customer_id, c.username, ca.cart_id, ca.creation_date
FROM Customers AS c
JOIN Carts AS ca ON c.customer_id = ca.customer_id;

SELECT p.product_id, p.product_name, p.price, ci.quantity
FROM Customers AS cust
JOIN Carts AS cart ON cust.customer_id = cart.customer_id
JOIN CartItems AS ci ON cart.cart_id = ci.cart_id
JOIN Products AS p ON ci.product_id = p.product_id
WHERE cust.customer_id = 12;

SELECT ca.cart_id, SUM(p.price * ci.quantity) AS total_value
FROM Carts AS ca
JOIN CartItems AS ci ON ca.cart_id = ci.cart_id
JOIN Products AS p ON ci.product_id = p.product_id
WHERE ca.cart_id = 101
GROUP BY ca.cart_id;

Schema: Patients (patient_id INT, first_name VARCHAR, last_name VARCHAR, phone VARCHAR), Doctors (doctor_id INT, first_name VARCHAR, last_name VARCHAR, specialty VARCHAR), Appointments (appointment_id INT, patient_id INT, doctor_id INT, appointment_date DATETIME, reason VARCHAR).

Queries:
1. List all appointments with patient and doctor names.
2. Find all appointments for a specific doctor (e.g., doctor_id = 2).
3. Count the number of appointments per specialty.
4. Schedule a new appointment.
5. Update an appointment's reason.
text_nat:
SELECT A.appointment_id, P.first_name AS patient_first_name, P.last_name AS patient_last_name, D.first_name AS doctor_first_name, D.last_name AS doctor_last_name, A.appointment_date, A.reason
FROM Appointments AS A
JOIN Patients AS P ON A.patient_id = P.patient_id
JOIN Doctors AS D ON A.doctor_id = D.doctor_id;

SELECT A.appointment_id, P.first_name, P.last_name, A.appointment_date, A.reason
FROM Appointments AS A
JOIN Patients AS P ON A.patient_id = P.patient_id
WHERE A.doctor_id = 2;

SELECT A.appointment_id, D.first_name, D.last_name, A.appointment_date, A.reason
FROM Appointments AS A
JOIN Doctors AS D ON A.doctor_id = D.doctor_id
WHERE A.doctor_id = 2;

SELECT D.specialty, COUNT(A.appointment_id) AS total_appointments
FROM Appointments AS A
JOIN Doctors AS D ON A.doctor_id = D.doctor_id
GROUP BY D.specialty;

SELECT P.first_name, P.last_name, A.appointment_date
FROM Patients AS P
JOIN Appointments AS A ON P.patient_id = A.patient_id;

SELECT D.first_name, D.last_name, COUNT(A.appointment_id) AS num_appointments
FROM Doctors AS D
JOIN Appointments AS A ON D.doctor_id = A.doctor_id
GROUP BY D.doctor_id;

WHERE appointment_id = 5;

FROM Appointments AS A

JOIN Doctors AS D ON A.doctor_id = D.doctor_id

SELECT A.appointment_id, D.first_name, D.last_name, P.phone

JOIN Doctors AS D ON A.doctor_id = D.doctor_id
JOIN Patients AS P ON A.patient_id = P.patient_id

SELECT P.first_name, P.last_name, D.specialty
FROM Patients AS P
JOIN Appointments AS A ON P.patient_id = A.patient_id
JOIN Doctors AS D ON A.doctor_id = D.doctor_id

SELECT D.first_name, D.last_name, P.first_name, P.last_name

Schema: Users (user_id INT, username VARCHAR, email VARCHAR), Plans (plan_id INT, plan_name VARCHAR, price_monthly DECIMAL, features TEXT), Subscriptions (subscription_id INT, user_id INT, plan_id INT, start_date DATE, end_date DATE, status VARCHAR).

Queries:
1. Select all users and their active subscriptions.
2. Find all users subscribed to a specific plan (e.g., 'Premium Plan').
3. Count the number of subscriptions per plan.
4. Create a new subscription for a user.
5. Change a subscription's status to 'Cancelled'.
text_nat:
SELECT u.username, u.email, s.start_date, s.end_date, s.status
FROM Users AS u
JOIN Subscriptions AS s
ON u.user_id = s.user_id
WHERE s.status = 'Active';

SELECT u.username, u.email, s.start_date, s.end_date
FROM Users AS u
JOIN Subscriptions AS s
ON u.user_id = s.user_id
JOIN Plans AS p
ON s.plan_id = p.plan_id
WHERE p.plan_name = 'Premium Plan';

SELECT p.plan_name, COUNT(s.subscription_id) AS subscription_count
FROM Plans AS p
JOIN Subscriptions AS s
ON p.plan_id = s.plan_id
GROUP BY p.plan_name;

SELECT
    A.asset_name,
    A.asset_type,
    L.location_name
FROM
    Assets AS A
JOIN AssetLocations AS AL ON A.asset_id = AL.asset_id
JOIN Locations AS L ON AL.location_id = L.location_id;

FROM

FROM

-- Setup: Create tables and insert sample data
CREATE TABLE Players (
    player_id INT PRIMARY KEY,
    username VARCHAR(50),
    join_date DATE
);

CREATE TABLE Games (
    game_id INT PRIMARY KEY,
    game_name VARCHAR(100),
    genre VARCHAR(50)
);

CREATE TABLE Scores (
    score_id INT PRIMARY KEY,
    player_id INT,
    game_id INT,
    score INT,
    score_date DATETIME,
    FOREIGN KEY (player_id) REFERENCES Players(player_id),
    FOREIGN KEY (game_id) REFERENCES Games(game_id)
);

3. Count the number of 5-star reviews for each instructor.
4. Add a new course review.
5. Update a review's comment.
text_nat:
SELECT c.course_name, AVG(r.rating) AS average_rating
FROM Courses AS c
JOIN Reviews AS r
ON c.course_id = r.course_id
GROUP BY c.course_name;

SELECT r.review_id, s.first_name, s.last_name, r.rating, r.comment
FROM Reviews AS r
JOIN Students AS s
ON r.student_id = s.student_id
JOIN Courses AS c
ON r.course_id = c.course_id
WHERE c.course_name = 'Introduction to Python';

SELECT c.instructor, COUNT(r.review_id) AS five_star_reviews
FROM Courses AS c
JOIN Reviews AS r
ON c.course_id = r.course_id
WHERE r.rating = 5
GROUP BY c.instructor;

Queries:
1. Select all sales transactions and their associated products and stores.
2. Find all sales of a specific product category (e.g., 'Apparel').
3. Calculate the total revenue generated by each store.
4. Record a new sale transaction.
5. Update the quantity of an item in a sale.
text_nat:
SELECT
  s.sale_id,
  s.sale_date,
  s.quantity,
  s.unit_price,
  p.product_name,
  p.category,
  st.store_name,
  st.city
FROM Sales AS s
JOIN Products AS p
  ON s.product_id = p.product_id
JOIN Stores AS st
  ON s.store_id = st.store_id;

SELECT
  s.sale_id,
  s.sale_date,
  s.quantity,
  s.unit_price,
  p.product_name
FROM Sales AS s
JOIN Products AS p
  ON s.product_id = p.product_id
WHERE
  p.category = 'Apparel';

SELECT
  st.store_name,
  SUM(s.quantity * s.unit_price) AS total_revenue
FROM Sales AS s
JOIN Stores AS st
  ON s.store_id = st.store_id
GROUP BY
  st.store_name;

Schema: Employees (employee_id INT, first_name VARCHAR, last_name VARCHAR, department VARCHAR), TrainingCourses (course_id INT, course_name VARCHAR, duration_hours INT), Enrollments (enrollment_id INT, employee_id INT, course_id INT, enrollment_date DATE, completion_status VARCHAR).

Queries:
1. List all employees and the training courses they are enrolled in.
2. Find all employees who completed a specific course (e.g., 'Data Security Basics').
3. Count the number of employees per department who completed at least one course.
4. Enroll an employee in a new training course.
5. Update an enrollment's completion status to 'Completed'.
text_nat:
SELECT
    E.first_name,
    E.last_name,
    TC.course_name
FROM
    Employees AS E
JOIN
    Enrollments AS EN ON E.employee_id = EN.employee_id
JOIN
    TrainingCourses AS TC ON EN.course_id = TC.course_id;

SELECT
    E.first_name,
    E.last_name
FROM
    Employees AS E
JOIN
    Enrollments AS EN ON E.employee_id = EN.employee_id
JOIN
    TrainingCourses AS TC ON EN.course_id = TC.course_id
WHERE
    TC.course_name = 'Data Security Basics' AND EN.completion_status = 'Completed';

SELECT
    E.department,
    COUNT(DISTINCT E.employee_id) AS completed_employees_count
FROM
    Employees AS E
JOIN
    Enrollments AS EN ON E.employee_id = EN.employee_id
WHERE
    EN.completion_status = 'Completed'
GROUP BY
    E.department;

Schema: Customers (customer_id INT, name VARCHAR, email VARCHAR), Tickets (ticket_id INT, customer_id INT, subject VARCHAR, description TEXT, status VARCHAR, assigned_to VARCHAR, created_date DATETIME).

Queries:
1. List all tickets and the customers who opened them.
2. Find all 'Open' tickets assigned to a specific agent (e.g., 'John Doe').
3. Count the number of tickets per status.
4. Create a new support ticket.
5. Update a ticket's status to 'Resolved'.
text_nat:
SELECT
    T.ticket_id,
    T.subject,
    C.name AS customer_name,
    C.email AS customer_email
FROM
    Tickets AS T
JOIN
    Customers AS C
ON
    T.customer_id = C.customer_id;

SELECT
    T.ticket_id,
    T.subject,
    T.description,
    C.name AS customer_name
FROM
    Tickets AS T
JOIN
    Customers AS C
ON
    T.customer_id = C.customer_id
WHERE
    T.status = 'Open' AND T.assigned_to = 'John Doe';

SELECT
    status,
    COUNT(ticket_id) AS ticket_count
FROM
    Tickets
GROUP BY
    status;

FROM Milestones AS M
JOIN Projects AS P ON M.project_id = P.project_id

FROM Projects AS P
JOIN Milestones AS M ON P.project_id = M.project_id

Queries:
1. Select all referrals and the names of the referring and referred providers.
2. Find all patients referred by a specific provider (e.g., referring_provider_id = 1).
3. Count the number of referrals per specialty.
4. Add a new healthcare provider.

SELECT
  R.referral_id,
  P.first_name AS patient_first_name,
  P.last_name AS patient_last_name,
  RP.provider_name AS referring_provider_name,
  RP.specialty AS referring_provider_specialty,
  TP.provider_name AS referred_provider_name,
  TP.specialty AS referred_provider_specialty,
  R.referral_date,
  R.reason
FROM Referrals AS R
JOIN Patients AS P
  ON R.patient_id = P.patient_id
JOIN Providers AS RP
  ON R.referring_provider_id = RP.provider_id
JOIN Providers AS TP
  ON R.referred_provider_id = TP.provider_id;

WHERE
  R.referring_provider_id = 1;

GROUP BY

Queries:
1. Select all donations and the donors and campaigns they relate to.
2. Find all donations made to a specific campaign (e.g., 'Winter Appeal').
3. Calculate the total amount donated by each donor.
4. Add a new donor.
5. Record a new donation.
text_nat:
SELECT
    d.donation_id,
    d.donation_amount,
    d.donation_date,
    dr.first_name,
    dr.last_name,
    c.campaign_name
FROM
    Donations AS d
JOIN Donors AS dr ON d.donor_id = dr.donor_id
JOIN Campaigns AS c ON d.campaign_id = c.campaign_id;

SELECT
    d.donation_id,
    dr.first_name,
    c.campaign_name,
    d.donation_amount
FROM
    Donations AS d
JOIN Campaigns AS c ON d.campaign_id = c.campaign_id
WHERE
    c.campaign_name = 'Winter Appeal';

SELECT
    dr.first_name,
    dr.last_name,
    SUM(d.donation_amount) AS total_donated
FROM
    Donors AS dr
JOIN Donations AS d ON dr.donor_id = d.donor_id

Queries:
1. List all courses and their departments.
2. Find all professors in a specific department (e.g., 'Physics').
3. Count the number of courses offered by each department.
4. Add a new course to a department.
5. Update a course's level.
text_nat:

-- Query 1: List all courses and their departments.
SELECT C.course_name, D.department_name
FROM Courses AS C
JOIN Departments AS D ON C.department_id = D.department_id;

-- Query 2: Find all professors in a specific department (e.g., 'Physics').
SELECT P.first_name, P.last_name, D.department_name
FROM Professors AS P
JOIN Departments AS D ON P.department_id = D.department_id
WHERE D.department_name = 'Physics';

-- Query 3: Count the number of courses offered by each department.
SELECT D.department_name, COUNT(C.course_id) AS num_courses
FROM Departments AS D
JOIN Courses AS C ON D.department_id = C.department_id
GROUP BY D.department_name;

-- Query 4: Add a new course to a department.
INSERT INTO Courses (course_id, course_name, department_id, credits, level)
VALUES (103, 'Astrophysics', (SELECT department_id FROM Departments WHERE department_name = 'Physics'), 3, 'Graduate');

UPDATE Courses
SET level = 'Advanced Undergraduate'
WHERE course_name = 'Thermodynamics';

ON P.supplier_id = S.supplier_id

FROM Products;

Schema: Customers(CustomerID INT, Name VARCHAR(50), Email VARCHAR(100)), Orders(OrderID INT, CustomerID INT, OrderDate DATE, TotalAmount DECIMAL(10,2)), OrderItems(OrderItemID INT, OrderID INT, Product VARCHAR(100), Quantity INT, PricePerUnit DECIMAL(10,2)).
Queries:
1. Select all customers who placed an order in the last month.
2. Calculate the total revenue for each customer.
3. Find the top 5 most ordered products.
4. Insert a new customer and an associated order with two items.
5. Update the total amount of a specific order after adding a new item.
text_nat:
SELECT *
FROM Customers
JOIN Orders
ON Customers.CustomerID = Orders.CustomerID
WHERE OrderDate >= DATE('now', '-1 month');

SELECT
    C.Name,
    SUM(O.TotalAmount) AS TotalRevenue
FROM Customers AS C
JOIN Orders AS O
ON C.CustomerID = O.CustomerID
GROUP BY C.Name;

SELECT
    OI.Product,
    SUM(OI.Quantity) AS TotalQuantityOrdered
FROM OrderItems AS OI
GROUP BY OI.Product
ORDER BY TotalQuantityOrdered DESC
LIMIT 5;

WHERE OrderID = 2001;

SELECT O.OrderDate, C.Name, OI.Product, OI.Quantity
FROM Orders O
JOIN Customers C
ON O.CustomerID = C.CustomerID
JOIN OrderItems OI
ON O.OrderID = OI.OrderID
WHERE O.OrderID = 2001;

SELECT FlightID, FlightNumber, DepartureAirport, ArrivalAirport, DepartureTime, ArrivalTime
FROM Flights
WHERE DepartureAirport = 'JFK'
  AND ArrivalAirport = 'LAX'
  AND CAST(DepartureTime AS DATE) = '2023-10-26';

SELECT f.DepartureAirport, AVG(DATEDIFF(minute, f.DepartureTime, f.ArrivalTime)) AS AverageDurationMinutes
FROM Flights AS f
GROUP BY f.DepartureAirport;

SELECT DISTINCT a.Model
FROM Aircrafts AS a
JOIN FlightAircrafts AS fa ON a.AircraftID = fa.AircraftID
WHERE a.Capacity > 200;

FROM Members

FROM Members AS M
JOIN MemberClasses AS MC ON M.MemberID = MC.MemberID
JOIN Classes AS C ON MC.ClassID = C.ClassID
WHERE C.ClassName = 'Yoga'
GROUP BY M.MemberID, M.FirstName, M.LastName
HAVING COUNT(MC.ClassID) > 3;

Schema: Posts(PostID INT, Title VARCHAR(255), Content TEXT, AuthorID INT, PublishDate DATETIME), Authors(AuthorID INT, FirstName VARCHAR(50), LastName VARCHAR(50), Email VARCHAR(100)), Categories(CategoryID INT, CategoryName VARCHAR(100)), PostCategories(PostID INT, CategoryID INT).
Queries:
1. Find all posts published by 'Jane Doe' in the 'Technology' category.
2. Count the number of posts in each category.
3. List authors who have published more than 10 posts.
4. Create a new blog post and assign it to an author and two categories.
5. Update the content of a specific post.
text_nat:
SELECT
    P.Title,
    P.Content
FROM
    Posts AS P
JOIN Authors AS A
    ON P.AuthorID = A.AuthorID
JOIN PostCategories AS PC
    ON P.PostID = PC.PostID
JOIN Categories AS C
    ON PC.CategoryID = C.CategoryID
WHERE
    A.FirstName = 'Jane' AND A.LastName = 'Doe' AND C.CategoryName = 'Technology';

SELECT
    C.CategoryName,
    COUNT(PC.PostID) AS NumberOfPosts
FROM
    Categories AS C
LEFT JOIN PostCategories AS PC
    ON C.CategoryID = PC.CategoryID
GROUP BY
    C.CategoryName;

SELECT
    A.FirstName,
    A.LastName,
    COUNT(P.PostID) AS NumberOfPosts
FROM
    Authors AS A
JOIN Posts AS P
    ON A.AuthorID = P.AuthorID
GROUP BY
    A.AuthorID, A.FirstName, A.LastName
HAVING
    COUNT(P.PostID) > 10;

Queries:
1. List all players on the 'Lions' team who play 'Forward'.
2. Calculate the total wins for each team.
3. Find teams that have played more than 10 games.
4. Add a new player to an existing team.
5. Update the score of a specific game.
text_nat:
SELECT P.FirstName, P.LastName
FROM Players AS P
JOIN Teams AS T ON P.TeamID = T.TeamID
WHERE T.TeamName = 'Lions' AND P.Position = 'Forward';

SELECT T.TeamName,
       SUM(CASE WHEN G.HomeTeamID = T.TeamID AND G.HomeScore > G.AwayScore THEN 1
                WHEN G.AwayTeamID = T.TeamID AND G.AwayScore > G.HomeScore THEN 1
                ELSE 0 END) AS Wins
FROM Teams AS T
JOIN Games AS G ON T.TeamID = G.HomeTeamID OR T.TeamID = G.AwayTeamID
GROUP BY T.TeamName
ORDER BY Wins DESC;

SELECT T.TeamName, COUNT(G.GameID) AS GamesPlayed
FROM Teams AS T
JOIN Games AS G ON T.TeamID = G.HomeTeamID OR T.TeamID = G.AwayTeamID
GROUP BY T.TeamName
HAVING COUNT(G.GameID) > 10;

Schema: Courses(CourseID INT, CourseName VARCHAR(100), Instructor VARCHAR(100)), Modules(ModuleID INT, CourseID INT, ModuleName VARCHAR(100), OrderInCourse INT), Enrollments(EnrollmentID INT, UserID INT, CourseID INT, StartDate DATE, CompletionDate DATE), Progress(ProgressID INT, EnrollmentID INT, ModuleID INT, CompletionStatus VARCHAR(20), CompletionDate DATETIME).
Queries:
1. List all 'In Progress' modules for 'User A' in 'Introduction to SQL'.
2. Calculate the percentage of modules completed by each user in a specific course.
3. Find courses where all enrolled students have completed at least 50% of the modules.
4. Enroll a new user in a course and mark the first module as 'Completed'.
5. Update the 'CompletionStatus' of a module for a user.
text_nat:
SELECT
    C.CourseName,
    M.ModuleName,
    P.CompletionStatus
FROM
    Courses AS C
JOIN
    Modules AS M ON C.CourseID = M.CourseID
JOIN
    Enrollments AS E ON C.CourseID = E.CourseID
JOIN
    Progress AS P ON E.EnrollmentID = P.EnrollmentID AND M.ModuleID = P.ModuleID
WHERE
    C.CourseName = 'Introduction to SQL'
    AND E.UserID = (SELECT UserID FROM Users WHERE UserName = 'User A')
    AND P.CompletionStatus = 'In Progress';

SELECT
    E.UserID,
    C.CourseName,
    CAST(COUNT(CASE WHEN P.CompletionStatus = 'Completed' THEN 1 END) AS REAL) * 100 / COUNT(M.ModuleID) AS CompletionPercentage
FROM
    Enrollments AS E
JOIN

Queries:
1. List all members whose membership is currently active.
2. Count the number of books currently on loan by each member.

JOIN Loans AS L
ON M.MemberID = L.MemberID
WHERE L.ReturnDate IS NULL
GROUP BY M.MemberID, M.FirstName, M.LastName;

FROM Books AS B

ON B.BookID = L.BookID

Queries:
1. Find all reviews for 'Course Z' with a rating of 4 or 5 stars.
2. Calculate the average rating for each course.
3. List students who have reviewed more than 2 courses.
4. Insert a new review for a course by a student.
5. Update the 'Comment' for an existing review.
text_nat:
SELECT
    R.ReviewID,
    R.Rating,
    R.Comment
FROM
    Reviews AS R
JOIN
    Courses AS C ON R.CourseID = C.CourseID
WHERE
    C.CourseName = 'Course Z' AND R.Rating >= 4;

SELECT
    C.CourseName,
    AVG(R.Rating) AS AverageRating
FROM
    Courses AS C
JOIN
    Reviews AS R ON C.CourseID = R.CourseID
GROUP BY
    C.CourseName;

SELECT
    S.FirstName,
    S.LastName,
    COUNT(DISTINCT R.CourseID) AS CoursesReviewed
FROM
    Students AS S
JOIN
    Reviews AS R ON S.StudentID = R.StudentID
GROUP BY
    S.StudentID, S.FirstName, S.LastName
HAVING
    COUNT(DISTINCT R.CourseID) > 2;

Queries:
1. List all 'High' priority tickets that are 'Open' and assigned to 'Agent Smith'.
2. Count the number of tickets by 'Status' for each customer.
3. Find agents who have resolved more than 50 tickets.
4. Create a new support ticket for a customer and assign it to an agent.
5. Update the 'Status' of a ticket to 'Resolved' and add a resolution note.
text_nat:
SELECT T.TicketID, T.Subject, T.Description
FROM Tickets AS T
JOIN Customers AS C ON T.CustomerID = C.CustomerID
JOIN Agents AS A ON T.AgentID = A.AgentID
WHERE T.Priority = 'High'
  AND T.Status = 'Open'
  AND A.AgentName = 'Agent Smith';

SELECT C.FirstName, C.LastName, T.Status, COUNT(T.TicketID) AS NumberOfTickets
FROM Customers AS C
JOIN Tickets AS T ON C.CustomerID = T.CustomerID
GROUP BY C.FirstName, C.LastName, T.Status;

SELECT A.AgentName, COUNT(T.TicketID) AS ResolvedTickets
FROM Agents AS A
JOIN Tickets AS T ON A.AgentID = T.AgentID
WHERE T.Status = 'Resolved'
GROUP BY A.AgentName
HAVING COUNT(T.TicketID) > 50;

text_es: Schema: Documents (doc_id, title, latest_version_id), Versions (version_id, doc_id, version_number, content, created_at, created_by). Queries: 1. Retrieve the latest content for a specific document. 2. Find all versions of a document, ordered by version number. 3. Insert a new version for an existing document, updating the latest_version_id in Documents. 4. Find all documents created by a specific user. 5. Get the count of versions for each document.
text_nat:
-- 1. Retrieve the latest content for a specific document.
SELECT
    V.content
FROM
    Documents AS D
JOIN Versions AS V
    ON D.latest_version_id = V.version_id
WHERE
    D.doc_id = 1;

-- 2. Find all versions of a document, ordered by version number.
SELECT
    V.version_number,
    V.content,
    V.created_at,
    V.created_by
FROM
    Versions AS V
JOIN Documents AS D
    ON V.doc_id = D.doc_id
WHERE
    D.doc_id = 1
ORDER BY
    V.version_number;

-- 3. Insert a new version for an existing document, updating the latest_version_id in Documents.
-- Assuming doc_id = 1, new content 'New content', created_by = 'UserA'
INSERT INTO Versions (doc_id, version_number, content, created_at, created_by)
SELECT
    1,
    COALESCE(MAX(version_number), 0) + 1,
    'New content',
    CURRENT_TIMESTAMP,
    'UserA'
FROM
    Versions
WHERE
    doc_id = 1;

UPDATE Documents
SET
    latest_version_id = (SELECT V.version_id FROM Versions AS V WHERE V.doc_id = Documents.doc_id ORDER BY V.version_number DESC LIMIT 1)
WHERE
    doc_id = 1;

-- 4. Find all documents created by a specific user.
SELECT
    D.doc_id,
    D.title,
    V.version_number,
    V.created_at
FROM
    Documents AS D
JOIN Versions AS V
    ON D.latest_version_id = V.version_id
WHERE
    V.created_by = 'UserA';

-- 5. Get the count of versions for each document.
SELECT
    D.doc_id,
    D.title,
    COUNT(V.version_id) AS version_count
FROM
    Documents AS D
JOIN Versions AS V
    ON D.doc_id = V.doc_id
GROUP BY
    D.doc_id, D.title;

SELECT D.doc_id, D.title FROM Documents AS D JOIN Versions AS V ON D.doc_id = V.doc_id;
SELECT V.version_id, V.content FROM Versions AS V JOIN Documents AS D ON V.doc_id = D.doc_id;

SELECT V.created_by FROM Versions AS V JOIN Documents AS D ON V.doc_id = D.doc_id GROUP BY V.created_by;
SELECT D.title FROM Documents AS D JOIN Versions AS V ON D.latest_version_id = V.version_id WHERE V.created_at > '2023-01-01';

text_es: Schema: Rooms (room_id, room_name, capacity), Bookings (booking_id, room_id, user_id, start_time, end_time, purpose). Queries: 1. Find all available rooms for a specific time slot. 2. text_es: Schema: Users (user_id, username, email), Subscriptions (sub_id, user_id, tier_id, start_date, end_date, is_active), Tiers (tier_id, tier_name, price_monthly). Queries: 1. Find the current active subscription tier for a user. 2. List all users on a specific subscription tier. 3. Update a user's subscription to a new tier (end current, start new). 4. Get the count of active users per tier. 5. Find all users whose subscriptions are expiring in the next 30 days.

SELECT
    U.username,
    T.tier_name
FROM
    Users AS U
JOIN
    Subscriptions AS S ON U.user_id = S.user_id
JOIN
    Tiers AS T ON S.tier_id = T.tier_id
WHERE
    U.username = 'example_user' AND S.is_active = TRUE;

text_es: Schema: Customers (customer_id, customer_name, email), Transactions (transaction_id, customer_id, amount, transaction_date), LoyaltyPoints (customer_id, points_balance, last_updated). Queries: 1. Get the current loyalty points for a customer. 2. Update a customer's loyalty points after a transaction (add points). 3. Find all customers with more than X points. 4. Get the total transaction amount for each customer. 5. List customers who haven't earned points in the last 90 days.
text_nat:
SELECT
    lp.points_balance
FROM
    LoyaltyPoints AS lp
JOIN
    Customers AS c
ON
    lp.customer_id = c.customer_id
WHERE
    c.customer_name = 'John Doe';

UPDATE LoyaltyPoints
SET
    points_balance = points_balance + 10
WHERE
    customer_id = (SELECT customer_id FROM Customers WHERE customer_name = 'Jane Smith');

SELECT
    c.customer_name,
    lp.points_balance
FROM
    Customers AS c
JOIN
    LoyaltyPoints AS lp
ON
    c.customer_id = lp.customer_id
WHERE
    lp.points_balance > 100;

SELECT
    c.customer_name,
    SUM(t.amount) AS total_transaction_amount
FROM
    Customers AS c
JOIN
    Transactions AS t
ON
    c.customer_id = t.customer_id
GROUP BY
    c.customer_name;

SELECT
    c.customer_name,
    c.email
FROM
    Customers AS c
LEFT JOIN
    LoyaltyPoints AS lp
ON
    c.customer_id = lp.customer_id
WHERE
    lp.last_updated < DATE('now', '-90 days') OR lp.last_updated IS NULL;

SELECT
    c.customer_name,
    t.transaction_id
FROM
    Customers AS c
JOIN
    Transactions AS t
ON
    c.customer_id = t.customer_id;

SELECT
    lp.customer_id,
    c.customer_name
FROM
    LoyaltyPoints AS lp
JOIN
    Customers AS c
ON
    lp.customer_id = c.customer_id;

SELECT
    t.transaction_id,

text_es: Schema: Courses (course_id, course_title, instructor_id), Lectures (lecture_id, course_id, lecture_title, lecture_date, duration_minutes), Students (student_id, student_name). Queries: 1. List all lectures for a specific course. 2. Find all courses taught by a particular instructor. 3. Insert a new lecture for an existing course. 4. Update the duration of a lecture. 5. Get the total duration of lectures for each course.
text_nat:
-- 1. List all lectures for a specific course
SELECT l.lecture_title, l.lecture_date, l.duration_minutes
FROM Lectures l
JOIN Courses c ON l.course_id = c.course_id
WHERE c.course_title = 'Database Fundamentals';

-- 2. Find all courses taught by a particular instructor
SELECT c.course_title
FROM Courses c
WHERE c.instructor_id = 101;

-- 3. Insert a new lecture for an existing course
INSERT INTO Lectures (course_id, lecture_title, lecture_date, duration_minutes)
SELECT c.course_id, 'New Lecture Topic', '2023-11-20', 90
FROM Courses c
WHERE c.course_title = 'Advanced SQL';

-- 4. Update the duration of a lecture
UPDATE Lectures
SET duration_minutes = 75
WHERE lecture_id = 5;

-- 5. Get the total duration of lectures for each course
SELECT c.course_title, SUM(l.duration_minutes) AS total_duration_minutes
FROM Courses c
JOIN Lectures l ON c.course_id = l.course_id
GROUP BY c.course_title;

Schema: Conferences (conference_id, conference_name, start_date), Speakers (speaker_id, speaker_name, bio, company), Sessions (session_id, conference_id, speaker_id, session_title, start_time, end_time). Queries: 1. List all sessions at a specific conference. 2. Find all sessions presented by a particular speaker. 3. Insert a new session for a conference with a speaker. 4. Update a speaker's bio. 5. Get the count of sessions per speaker.
text_nat:
-- 1. List all sessions at a specific conference.
SELECT
  s.session_title,
  s.start_time,
  s.end_time
FROM Sessions s
JOIN Conferences c ON s.conference_id = c.conference_id
WHERE
  c.conference_name = 'Tech Summit 2024';

-- 2. Find all sessions presented by a particular speaker.
SELECT
  s.session_title,
  c.conference_name,
  s.start_time
FROM Sessions s
JOIN Speakers sp ON s.speaker_id = sp.speaker_id
WHERE
  sp.speaker_name = 'Alice Wonderland';

-- Separate query 1
SELECT s.session_title FROM Sessions s JOIN Conferences c ON s.conference_id = c.conference_id;

-- Separate query 2
SELECT sp.speaker_name FROM Speakers sp JOIN Sessions s ON sp.speaker_id = s.speaker_id;

-- 3. Insert a new session for a conference with a speaker.
INSERT INTO Sessions (
  conference_id,
  speaker_id,
  session_title,
  start_time,
  end_time
)
SELECT
  c.conference_id,
  sp.speaker_id,
  'Advanced SQL Techniques',
  '2024-11-15 14:00:00',
  '2024-11-15 15:00:00'
FROM Conferences c
JOIN Speakers sp ON c.conference_name = 'DevOps World 2024'
AND sp.speaker_name = 'Bob The Builder';

-- Separate query 3
SELECT c.conference_name FROM Conferences c JOIN Sessions s ON c.conference_id = s.conference_id;

-- 4. Update a speaker's bio.
UPDATE Speakers
SET
  bio = 'Experienced software engineer focusing on cloud architecture.'
WHERE
  speaker_name = 'Alice Wonderland';

-- Separate query 4
SELECT s.session_title FROM Sessions s JOIN Speakers sp ON s.speaker_id = sp.speaker_id;

-- 5. Get the count of sessions per speaker.
SELECT
  sp.speaker_name,
  COUNT(s.session_id) AS session_count
FROM Speakers sp
JOIN Sessions s ON sp.speaker_id = s.speaker_id
GROUP BY
  sp.speaker_name;

-- Separate query 5
SELECT c.start_date FROM Conferences c JOIN Sessions s ON c.conference_id = s.conference_id;

-- Separate query 6
SELECT sp.company FROM Speakers sp JOIN Sessions s ON sp.speaker_id = s.speaker_id;

-- Separate query 7
SELECT s.session_title FROM Sessions s JOIN Conferences c ON s.conference_id = c.conference_id;

-- Separate query 8
SELECT c.conference_name FROM Conferences c JOIN Sessions s ON c.conference_id = s.conference_id;

text_es: Schema: Courses (course_id, course_code, course_title, credits), Prerequisites (prereq_id, course_id, required_course_id). Queries: 1. Find all direct prerequisites for a specific course. 2. text_nat:

WHERE
  P.required_course_id = (
    SELECT

    FROM Courses
    WHERE
      course_code = 'MA101'
  );

)
SELECT

  C2.course_id
FROM Courses AS C1
JOIN Courses AS C2
  ON C1.course_code = 'CS301'

FROM Courses AS C

WHERE

text_es: Schema: Users (user_id, username), Posts (post_id, user_id, content, posted_at), Likes (like_id, post_id, user_id, liked_at), Comments (comment_id, post_id, user_id, comment_text, commented_at). Queries: 1. Get the total number of likes for a specific post. 2. List all comments on a particular post. 3. Insert a new like for a post by a user. 4. Find posts with more than X comments. 5. Get the total engagement (likes + comments) for each post.
text_nat:
SELECT COUNT(L.like_id) AS total_likes
FROM Likes AS L
JOIN Posts AS P
ON L.post_id = P.post_id
WHERE P.post_id = 1;

SELECT C.comment_text, U.username
FROM Comments AS C
JOIN Posts AS P ON C.post_id = P.post_id
JOIN Users AS U ON C.user_id = U.user_id
WHERE P.post_id = 2;

INSERT INTO Likes (post_id, user_id, liked_at)
VALUES (3, 1, CURRENT_TIMESTAMP);

SELECT P.post_id, P.content
FROM Posts AS P
JOIN Comments AS C ON P.post_id = C.post_id
GROUP BY P.post_id, P.content
HAVING COUNT(C.comment_id) > 1;

SELECT P.post_id, P.content,
       (COUNT(DISTINCT L.like_id) + COUNT(DISTINCT C.comment_id)) AS total_engagement
FROM Posts AS P
LEFT JOIN Likes AS L ON P.post_id = L.post_id
LEFT JOIN Comments AS C ON P.post_id = C.post_id
GROUP BY P.post_id, P.content;

SELECT P.post_id, P.content, U.username AS post_author
FROM Posts AS P
JOIN Users AS U ON P.user_id = U.user_id;

JOIN Posts AS P ON L.post_id = P.post_id;

JOIN Users AS U ON C.user_id = U.user_id;

FROM Posts AS P
LEFT JOIN Likes AS L ON P.post_id = L.post_id
GROUP BY P.post_id, P.content;

SELECT P.post_id, P.content, COUNT(C.comment_id) AS comment_count
FROM Posts AS P
LEFT JOIN Comments AS C ON P.post_id = C.post_id
GROUP BY P.post_id, P.content;

SELECT U.username, COUNT(P.post_id) AS number_of_posts
FROM Users AS U
JOIN Posts AS P ON U.user_id = P.user_id
GROUP BY U.username;

SELECT U.username, COUNT(L.like_id) AS likes_given
FROM Users AS U
JOIN Likes AS L ON U.user_id = L.user_id
GROUP BY U.username;

SELECT U.username, COUNT(C.comment_id) AS comments_made
FROM Users AS U
JOIN Comments AS C ON U.user_id = C.user_id
GROUP BY U.username;

INNER JOIN Users AS U ON P.user_id = U.user_id
WHERE P.posted_at > '2023-01-01';

SELECT L.like_id, U.username AS liker_username

INNER JOIN Users AS U ON L.user_id = U.user_id

SELECT C.comment_id, P.content AS commented_post_content
FROM Comments AS C
INNER JOIN Posts AS P ON C.post_id = P.post_id
WHERE C.commented_at > '2023-03-01';

text_es: Schema: Vehicles (vehicle_id, make, model, year, license_plate), MaintenanceRecords (record_id, vehicle_id, service_type, service_date, cost, mileage_at_service). Queries: 1. Get all maintenance records for a specific vehicle. 2. Find the total maintenance cost for each vehicle. 3. Insert a new maintenance record. 4. Find vehicles that haven't had a specific service type in over a year. 5. List vehicles due for service based on mileage (e.g., last service at 50k, due every 10k, current mileage 59k).
text_nat:
SELECT *
FROM MaintenanceRecords
JOIN Vehicles ON MaintenanceRecords.vehicle_id = Vehicles.vehicle_id
WHERE Vehicles.vehicle_id = 1;

SELECT
    v.make,
    v.model,
    SUM(mr.cost) AS total_maintenance_cost
FROM Vehicles AS v
JOIN MaintenanceRecords AS mr ON v.vehicle_id = mr.vehicle_id
GROUP BY
    v.make,
    v.model;

INSERT INTO MaintenanceRecords (vehicle_id, service_type, service_date, cost, mileage_at_service)
VALUES (1, 'Oil Change', '2023-10-26', 75.00, 65000);

SELECT v.make, v.model
FROM Vehicles AS v
LEFT JOIN MaintenanceRecords AS mr ON v.vehicle_id = mr.vehicle_id
WHERE mr.service_type = 'Tire Rotation'
  AND mr.service_date < DATE('now', '-1 year')
GROUP BY v.vehicle_id
HAVING COUNT(mr.record_id) = 1;

SELECT
    v.make,
    v.model,
    v.license_plate
FROM Vehicles AS v
JOIN MaintenanceRecords AS mr ON v.vehicle_id = mr.vehicle_id
WHERE mr.service_type = 'Oil Change'
  AND mr.service_date = (
    SELECT MAX(mr2.service_date)
    FROM MaintenanceRecords AS mr2
    WHERE mr2.vehicle_id = v.vehicle_id
      AND mr2.service_type = 'Oil Change'
  )
  AND mr.mileage_at_service + 10000 < 59000;

List users who have not attempted a specific quiz.
text_nat:

WHERE Q.quiz_title = 'Math Basics' AND A.user_id = 101;

text_nat:
SELECT AVG(r.rating_value)
FROM Ratings AS r
WHERE r.recipe_id = 1;

SELECT r.rating_value, r.comment
FROM Ratings AS r
WHERE r.recipe_id = 1;

INSERT INTO Ratings (recipe_id, user_id, rating_value, rating_date, comment)

FROM Recipes AS rec
JOIN Ratings AS rtg ON rec.recipe_id = rtg.recipe_id
WHERE rtg.user_id = 1;

SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT r.recipe_id)
FROM Recipes AS r
JOIN Ratings AS ra ON r.recipe_id = ra.recipe_id

text_es: Schema: Products (product_id, product_name), Prices (price_id, product_id, effective_date, price_usd). Queries: 1. Get the current price for a specific product. 2. List the full pricing history for a product. 3. Insert a new price for a product (new effective date). 4. Find products whose price has increased in the last year. 5. Get the latest price for all products.
text_nat:
CREATE TABLE Products (
    product_id INT PRIMARY KEY,
    product_name VARCHAR(255)
);

CREATE TABLE Prices (
    price_id INT PRIMARY KEY,
    product_id INT,
    effective_date DATE,
    price_usd DECIMAL(10, 2),
    FOREIGN KEY (product_id) REFERENCES Products(product_id)
);

-- Query 1: Get the current price for a specific product
SELECT p.product_name, pr.price_usd
FROM Products p
JOIN Prices pr
  ON p.product_id = pr.product_id
WHERE p.product_name = 'Laptop'
  AND pr.effective_date = (
    SELECT MAX(effective_date)
    FROM Prices
    WHERE product_id = p.product_id
  );

-- Query 2: List the full pricing history for a product
SELECT pr.effective_date, pr.price_usd
FROM Products p
JOIN Prices pr
  ON p.product_id = pr.product_id
WHERE p.product_name = 'Laptop'
ORDER BY pr.effective_date DESC;

-- Query 3: Insert a new price for a product (new effective date)
INSERT INTO Prices (price_id, product_id, effective_date, price_usd)
VALUES (4, (SELECT product_id FROM Products WHERE product_name = 'Laptop'), '2024-03-01', 1250.00);

-- Query 4: Find products whose price has increased in the last year
SELECT DISTINCT p.product_name
FROM Products p
JOIN Prices pr1
  ON p.product_id = pr1.product_id
JOIN Prices pr2
  ON p.product_id = pr2.product_id
WHERE pr1.effective_date >= DATE('now', '-1 year')
  AND pr2.effective_date >= DATE('now', '-1 year')
  AND pr1.effective_date < pr2.effective_date
  AND pr2.price_usd > pr1.price_usd;

-- Query 5: Get the latest price for all products
SELECT p.product_name, pr.price_usd
FROM Products p
JOIN Prices pr
  ON p.product_id = pr.product_id
WHERE pr.effective_date = (
    SELECT MAX(effective_date)
    FROM Prices
    WHERE product_id = p.product_id
);

-- Additional queries with exactly ONE join between two tables

SELECT p.product_id, p.product_name
FROM Products p
JOIN Prices pr
  ON p.product_id = pr.product_id
WHERE pr.price_usd > 1000;

SELECT pr.price_id, pr.effective_date
FROM Prices pr
JOIN Products p
  ON pr.product_id = p.product_id
WHERE p.product_name = 'Keyboard';

  ON p.product_id = pr.product_id
ORDER BY pr.price_usd DESC;

FROM Products p
JOIN Prices pr
  ON p.product_id = pr.product_id
WHERE pr.effective_date < '2023-01-01';

SELECT pr.price_id, p.product_name
FROM Prices pr
JOIN Products p
  ON pr.product_id = p.product_id
WHERE pr.price_usd < 50;

SELECT p.product_id, pr.effective_date
FROM Products p
JOIN Prices pr
  ON p.product_id = pr.product_id
WHERE p.product_name LIKE 'M%';

SELECT pr.price_usd, p.product_name
FROM Prices pr
JOIN Products p
  ON pr.product_id = p.product_id
ORDER BY p.product_name ASC;

SELECT p.product_name
FROM Products p
JOIN Prices pr
  ON p.product_id = pr.product_id
GROUP BY p.product_id
HAVING COUNT(pr.price_id) > 1;

FROM Expenses AS E
JOIN Departments AS D

WHERE D.dept_name = 'Marketing';

Get the total votes for each option in a specific poll. 2. Find all polls created by a particular user. 3. Insert a new vote for an option. 4. List all active polls. 5. Get the total number of votes cast by each user.
text_nat:
SELECT
  O.option_text,
  COUNT(V.vote_id) AS total_votes
FROM Options AS O
JOIN Votes AS V
  ON O.option_id = V.option_id
WHERE
  O.poll_id = 1 -- Replace with your desired poll_id

text_es: Schema: Agents (agent_id, agent_name, department), Tickets (ticket_id, agent_id, customer_id, opened_at, closed_at, status, resolution_notes). Queries: 1. Get the number of tickets closed by a specific agent. 2. List all open tickets assigned to an agent. 3. Assign a ticket to an agent. 4. Close a ticket with resolution notes. 5. Find agents with an average resolution time longer than X hours.
text_nat:
SELECT COUNT(T.ticket_id)
FROM Tickets AS T
JOIN Agents AS A ON T.agent_id = A.agent_id
WHERE A.agent_name = 'Alice Smith' AND T.status = 'Closed';

SELECT T.ticket_id, T.opened_at
FROM Tickets AS T
JOIN Agents AS A ON T.agent_id = A.agent_id
WHERE A.agent_name = 'Bob Johnson' AND T.status = 'Open';

UPDATE Tickets
SET agent_id = (SELECT agent_id FROM Agents WHERE agent_name = 'Charlie Brown')
WHERE ticket_id = 101;

UPDATE Tickets
SET status = 'Closed', closed_at = NOW(), resolution_notes = 'Issue resolved after troubleshooting.'
WHERE ticket_id = 102;

SELECT A.agent_name,
       AVG(EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM (T.closed_at - T.opened_at))) / 3600 AS avg_resolution_hours
FROM Agents AS A
JOIN Tickets AS T ON A.agent_id = T.agent_id
WHERE T.status = 'Closed'
GROUP BY A.agent_name
HAVING AVG(EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM (T.closed_at - T.opened_at))) / 3600 > 24;

text_es: Schema: Courses (course_id, course_title), Modules (module_id, course_id, module_title, order_index), Lessons (lesson_id, module_id, lesson_title, lesson_type, duration_minutes). Queries: 1. CREATE TABLE Courses (
    course_id INT PRIMARY KEY,
    course_title VARCHAR(255)
);

CREATE TABLE Modules (
    module_id INT PRIMARY KEY,
    course_id INT,
    module_title VARCHAR(255),
    order_index INT,
    FOREIGN KEY (course_id) REFERENCES Courses(course_id)
);

CREATE TABLE Lessons (
    lesson_id INT PRIMARY KEY,
    module_id INT,
    lesson_title VARCHAR(255),
    lesson_type VARCHAR(50),
    duration_minutes INT,
    FOREIGN KEY (module_id) REFERENCES Modules(module_id)
);

text_es: Schema: Events (event_id, event_name, event_date), Attendees (attendee_id, event_id, first_name, last_name, company, badge_printed). Queries: 1. List all attendees for a specific event. 2. Find all attendees from a particular company for an event. 3. Mark an attendee's badge as 'printed'. 4. Insert a new attendee for an event. 5. Get the count of attendees whose badges have not been printed.
text_nat:
CREATE TABLE Events (
    event_id INT PRIMARY KEY,
    event_name VARCHAR(255),
    event_date DATE
);

CREATE TABLE Attendees (
    attendee_id INT PRIMARY KEY,
    event_id INT,
    first_name VARCHAR(255),
    last_name VARCHAR(255),
    company VARCHAR(255),
    badge_printed BOOLEAN
);

INSERT INTO Events (event_id, event_name, event_date) VALUES

-- Query 1: List all attendees for a specific event (e.g., event_id = 1)
SELECT A.first_name, A.last_name, E.event_name
FROM Attendees AS A
JOIN Events AS E ON A.event_id = E.event_id
WHERE E.event_id = 1;

-- Query 2: Find all attendees from a particular company for an event (e.g., event_id = 1, company = 'Innovate Corp')
SELECT A.first_name, A.last_name, A.company, E.event_name
FROM Attendees AS A
JOIN Events AS E ON A.event_id = E.event_id
WHERE E.event_id = 1 AND A.company = 'Innovate Corp';

-- Query 3: Mark an attendee's badge as 'printed' (e.g., attendee_id = 101)
UPDATE Attendees
SET badge_printed = TRUE
WHERE attendee_id = 101;

WHERE R.post_id = 123 AND R.reaction_type = 'like';

FROM Returns
JOIN Customers ON Returns.customer_id = Customers.customer_id

Queries: 1. Get the total allocated amount for a specific project. 2. List all budget allocations for a project, by category. 3. Update the spent amount for a specific allocation. 4. Find projects that have exceeded their budget in any category. 5. Calculate remaining budget per project (total_budget - sum(spent_amount)).

SELECT SUM(ba.allocated_amount) AS total_allocated
FROM BudgetAllocations AS ba
JOIN Projects AS p
ON ba.project_id = p.project_id
WHERE p.project_name = 'Alpha Project';

FROM BudgetAllocations AS ba
JOIN Projects AS p
ON ba.project_id = p.project_id

ON ba.category_id = c.category_id
WHERE p.project_name = 'Beta Project';

SET spent_amount = 1500.00
WHERE allocation_id = 101;

JOIN Projects AS p
ON ba.project_id = p.project_id

ON ba.category_id = c.category_id
WHERE ba.spent_amount > ba.allocated_amount;

SELECT p.project_name, (p.total_budget - COALESCE(SUM(ba.spent_amount), 0)) AS remaining_budget
FROM Projects AS p
LEFT JOIN BudgetAllocations AS ba
ON p.project_id = ba.project_id

text_es: Schema: Providers (provider_id, provider_name, specialty), Certifications (cert_id, cert_name, issuing_body), ProviderCertifications (provider_id, cert_id, issue_date, expiry_date). Queries: 1. List all certifications held by a specific provider. 2. Find all providers with a particular certification. 3. Insert a new certification for a provider. 4. Find providers whose certifications are expiring in the next 90 days. 5. Get the count of providers per specialty.
text_nat:
CREATE TABLE Providers (
    provider_id INT PRIMARY KEY,
    provider_name VARCHAR(255),
    specialty VARCHAR(255)
);

CREATE TABLE Certifications (
    cert_id INT PRIMARY KEY,
    cert_name VARCHAR(255),
    issuing_body VARCHAR(255)
);

CREATE TABLE ProviderCertifications (
    provider_id INT,
    cert_id INT,
    issue_date DATE,
    expiry_date DATE,
    PRIMARY KEY (provider_id, cert_id),
    FOREIGN KEY (provider_id) REFERENCES Providers(provider_id),
    FOREIGN KEY (cert_id) REFERENCES Certifications(cert_id)
);

-- Query 1: List all certifications held by a specific provider (e.g., provider_id = 1)
SELECT
    C.cert_name,
    PC.issue_date,
    PC.expiry_date
FROM
    Certifications AS C
JOIN ProviderCertifications AS PC
    ON C.cert_id = PC.cert_id
WHERE
    PC.provider_id = 1;

-- Query 2: Find all providers with a particular certification (e.g., cert_id = 101)
SELECT
    P.provider_name,
    P.specialty
FROM
    Providers AS P
JOIN ProviderCertifications AS PC
    ON P.provider_id = PC.provider_id
WHERE
    PC.cert_id = 101;

-- Query 3: Insert a new certification for a provider (e.g., provider_id = 2, cert_id = 103, dates)
INSERT INTO ProviderCertifications (provider_id, cert_id, issue_date, expiry_date)
VALUES (2, 103, '2023-01-15', '2025-01-14');

-- Query 4: Find providers whose certifications are expiring in the next 90 days
SELECT
    P.provider_name,
    C.cert_name,
    PC.expiry_date
FROM
    Providers AS P
JOIN ProviderCertifications AS PC
    ON P.provider_id = PC.provider_id
JOIN Certifications AS C
    ON PC.cert_id = C.cert_id
WHERE
    PC.expiry_date BETWEEN CURRENT_DATE AND DATE_ADD(CURRENT_DATE, INTERVAL 90 DAY);

-- Query 5: Get the count of providers per specialty
SELECT
    specialty,
    COUNT(provider_id) AS provider_count
FROM
    Providers
GROUP BY
    specialty;

-- Additional queries with exactly one join
SELECT P.provider_name, PC.issue_date
FROM Providers AS P JOIN ProviderCertifications AS PC
ON P.provider_id = PC.provider_id;

SELECT C.cert_name, PC.expiry_date
FROM Certifications AS C JOIN ProviderCertifications AS PC
ON C.cert_id = PC.cert_id;

SELECT P.provider_name, P.specialty
FROM Providers AS P JOIN ProviderCertifications AS PC
ON P.provider_id = PC.provider_id
WHERE PC.issue_date < '2023-01-01';

SELECT C.cert_name, C.issuing_body
FROM Certifications AS C JOIN ProviderCertifications AS PC
ON C.cert_id = PC.cert_id
WHERE PC.expiry_date > '2025-12-31';

SELECT P.provider_name, PC.expiry_date
FROM Providers AS P JOIN ProviderCertifications AS PC
ON P.provider_id = PC.provider_id

SELECT C.cert_name, PC.issue_date
FROM Certifications AS C JOIN ProviderCertifications AS PC
ON C.cert_id = PC.cert_id
WHERE C.issuing_body = 'Medical Board';

SELECT P.provider_name, C.cert_name

JOIN ProviderCertifications AS PC
    ON P.provider_id = PC.provider_id
JOIN Certifications AS C
    ON PC.cert_id = C.cert_id

Queries: 1. List all pending time off requests for an employee. 2. Find all time off requests awaiting approval from a specific manager. 3. Submit a new time off request. 4. Approve a time off request. 5. Get the total number of days requested per time off type.
text_nat:
-- 1. List all pending time off requests for an employee.
SELECT
    TOR.request_id,
    E.employee_name,
    TOT.type_name,
    TOR.start_date,
    TOR.end_date
FROM
    TimeOffRequests AS TOR
JOIN
    Employees AS E ON TOR.employee_id = E.employee_id
JOIN
    TimeOffTypes AS TOT ON TOR.type_id = TOT.type_id
WHERE
    E.employee_id = 101 AND TOR.status = 'Pending';

-- 2. Find all time off requests awaiting approval from a specific manager.
SELECT
    TOR.request_id,
    Emp.employee_name AS employee_requesting,
    Mgr.employee_name AS manager_to_approve,
    TOT.type_name,
    TOR.start_date,
    TOR.end_date
FROM
    TimeOffRequests AS TOR
JOIN
    Employees AS Emp ON TOR.employee_id = Emp.employee_id
JOIN
    Employees AS Mgr ON Emp.manager_id = Mgr.employee_id
JOIN
    TimeOffTypes AS TOT ON TOR.type_id = TOT.type_id
WHERE
    Mgr.employee_id = 201 AND TOR.status = 'Pending';

-- Single join queries below

SELECT R.request_id, R.start_date
FROM TimeOffRequests AS R
JOIN Employees AS E ON R.employee_id = E.employee_id;

SELECT T.type_name, T.type_id
FROM TimeOffTypes AS T
JOIN TimeOffRequests AS R ON T.type_id = R.type_id;

SELECT E.employee_name, M.employee_name AS manager_name
FROM Employees AS E
JOIN Employees AS M ON E.manager_id = M.employee_id;

-- 3. Submit a new time off request.

text_es: Schema: Articles (article_id, title, content, author_id, publish_date), Categories (category_id, category_name), ArticleCategories (article_id, category_id). Queries: 1. Find all articles in a specific category. 2. List all categories an article belongs to. 3. Insert a new article and assign it to a category. 4. Find articles containing a specific keyword in their title or content. 5. Get the count of articles per category.
text_nat:
-- 1. Find all articles in a specific category (e.g., 'Technology')
SELECT
    A.title,
    A.publish_date
FROM
    Articles AS A
JOIN
    ArticleCategories AS AC ON A.article_id = AC.article_id
JOIN
    Categories AS C ON AC.category_id = C.category_id
WHERE
    C.category_name = 'Technology';

-- 2. List all categories an article belongs to (e.g., article_id = 1)
SELECT
    C.category_name
FROM
    Categories AS C
JOIN
    ArticleCategories AS AC ON C.category_id = AC.category_id
WHERE
    AC.article_id = 1;

-- 3. Insert a new article and assign it to a category
INSERT INTO Articles (article_id, title, content, author_id, publish_date)
VALUES (101, 'New Article Title', 'Content of the new article.', 5, '2023-10-26');

INSERT INTO ArticleCategories (article_id, category_id)
VALUES (101, (SELECT category_id FROM Categories WHERE category_name = 'Science'));

-- 4. Find articles containing a specific keyword in their title or content (e.g., 'database')
SELECT
    A.title,
    A.content
FROM
    Articles AS A
WHERE
    A.title LIKE '%database%' OR A.content LIKE '%database%';

-- 5. Get the count of articles per category
SELECT
    C.category_name,
    COUNT(A.article_id) AS article_count
FROM
    Categories AS C
LEFT JOIN
    ArticleCategories AS AC ON C.category_id = AC.category_id
LEFT JOIN
    Articles AS A ON AC.article_id = A.article_id
GROUP BY
    C.category_name;

-- Separate queries, each with exactly ONE join between two tables

SELECT A.title FROM Articles AS A JOIN ArticleCategories AS AC ON A.article_id = AC.article_id;
SELECT C.category_name FROM Categories AS C JOIN ArticleCategories AS AC ON C.category_id = AC.category_id;
SELECT A.title FROM Articles AS A JOIN ArticleCategories AS AC ON A.article_id = AC.article_id WHERE AC.category_id = 1;
SELECT C.category_name FROM Categories AS C JOIN ArticleCategories AS AC ON C.category_id = AC.category_id WHERE AC.article_id = 2;
SELECT A.title FROM Articles AS A JOIN ArticleCategories AS AC ON A.article_id = AC.article_id WHERE A.author_id = 3;
SELECT C.category_name FROM Categories AS C JOIN ArticleCategories AS AC ON C.category_id = AC.category_id WHERE C.category_name LIKE 'P%';
SELECT COUNT(A.article_id) FROM Articles AS A JOIN ArticleCategories AS AC ON A.article_id = AC.article_id;
SELECT A.title FROM Articles AS A LEFT JOIN ArticleCategories AS AC ON A.article_id = AC.article_id WHERE AC.article_id IS NULL;

text_es: Schema: Products (product_id, product_name, base_price), Variants (variant_id, product_id, color, size, sku, stock_quantity, additional_cost). Queries: 1. List all variants for a specific product. 2. Find all products that have a variant with a specific color. 3. Update the stock quantity for a variant. 4. Get the full price (base_price + additional_cost) for each variant. 5. Find products with no variants currently in stock.
text_nat:
CREATE TABLE Products (
    product_id INT PRIMARY KEY,
    product_name VARCHAR(255),
    base_price DECIMAL(10, 2)
);

CREATE TABLE Variants (
    variant_id INT PRIMARY KEY,
    product_id INT,
    color VARCHAR(50),
    size VARCHAR(50),
    sku VARCHAR(100),
    stock_quantity INT,
    additional_cost DECIMAL(10, 2),
    FOREIGN KEY (product_id) REFERENCES Products(product_id)
);

INSERT INTO Products (product_id, product_name, base_price) VALUES
(1, 'T-Shirt', 15.00),
(2, 'Jeans', 45.00),
(3, 'Socks', 5.00);

INSERT INTO Variants (variant_id, product_id, color, size, sku, stock_quantity, additional_cost) VALUES
(101, 1, 'Red', 'M', 'TS-RD-M', 10, 2.00),
(102, 1, 'Blue', 'L', 'TS-BL-L', 5, 2.50),
(103, 2, 'Blue', '32', 'JN-BL-32', 8, 5.00),
(104, 2, 'Black', '34', 'JN-BK-34', 0, 6.00),
(105, 3, 'White', 'One Size', 'SK-WH-OS', 20, 0.50);

-- Query 1: List all variants for a specific product (e.g., product_id = 1)
SELECT
    p.product_name,
    v.color,
    v.size,
    v.stock_quantity
FROM
    Products AS p
JOIN
    Variants AS v ON p.product_id = v.product_id
WHERE p.product_id = 1;

-- Query 2: Find all products that have a variant with a specific color (e.g., 'Blue')
SELECT DISTINCT
    p.product_name
FROM
    Products AS p
JOIN
    Variants AS v ON p.product_id = v.product_id
WHERE v.color = 'Blue';

-- Query 3: Update the stock quantity for a variant (e.g., variant_id = 102 to 7)
UPDATE Variants
SET stock_quantity = 7
WHERE variant_id = 102;

-- Query 4: Get the full price (base_price + additional_cost) for each variant
SELECT
    p.product_name,
    v.color,
    v.size,
    (p.base_price + v.additional_cost) AS full_price
FROM
    Products AS p
JOIN
    Variants AS v ON p.product_id = v.product_id;

-- Query 5: Find products with no variants currently in stock
SELECT DISTINCT
    p.product_name
FROM
    Products AS p
LEFT JOIN
    Variants AS v ON p.product_id = v.product_id
GROUP BY p.product_id, p.product_name
HAVING SUM(v.stock_quantity) = 0 OR COUNT(v.variant_id) = 0;

-- Additional queries with single JOINs, each on its own line
SELECT product_name, color, size FROM Products JOIN Variants ON Products.product_id = Variants.product_id;

SELECT product_name, stock_quantity FROM Products JOIN Variants ON Products.product_id = Variants.product_id WHERE color = 'Red';

SELECT variant_id, sku, product_name FROM Variants JOIN Products ON Variants.product_id = Products.product_id;

SELECT p.product_name, v.color FROM Products AS p JOIN Variants AS v ON p.product_id = v.product_id WHERE v.size = 'M';

SELECT p.product_name, v.sku FROM Products AS p JOIN Variants AS v ON p.product_id = v.product_id ORDER BY p.product_name;

SELECT v.variant_id, p.base_price FROM Variants AS v JOIN Products AS p ON v.product_id = p.product_id WHERE v.stock_quantity > 5;

SELECT p.product_name FROM Products AS p JOIN Variants AS v ON p.product_id = v.product_id WHERE v.additional_cost > 3.00;

SELECT v.color FROM Variants AS v JOIN Products AS p ON v.product_id = p.product_id GROUP BY v.color HAVING COUNT(p.product_id) > 1;

Schema: Documents (doc_id INT, title VARCHAR, content TEXT, created_at DATETIME, author_id INT), Authors (author_id INT, name VARCHAR, email VARCHAR).
Queries:
1. Select all documents created by a specific author.
2. Find the total number of documents for each author.
3. Insert a new document.
4. Update the content of an existing document.
5. Select the 5 most recent documents.
text_nat:
CREATE TABLE Authors (
    author_id INT PRIMARY KEY,
    name VARCHAR(255),
    email VARCHAR(255)
);

CREATE TABLE Documents (
    doc_id INT PRIMARY KEY,
    title VARCHAR(255),
    content TEXT,
    created_at DATETIME,
    author_id INT,
    FOREIGN KEY (author_id) REFERENCES Authors(author_id)
);

-- Insert sample data
INSERT INTO Authors (author_id, name, email) VALUES
(1, 'Alice Smith', 'alice@example.com'),
(2, 'Bob Johnson', 'bob@example.com');

INSERT INTO Documents (doc_id, title, content, created_at, author_id) VALUES
(101, 'My First Post', 'This is the content of my first post.', '2023-01-01 10:00:00', 1),
(102, 'Database Design', 'Details about database design.', '2023-01-02 11:00:00', 2),
(103, 'SQL Joins', 'Understanding different types of SQL joins.', '2023-01-03 12:00:00', 1),
(104, 'New Tech Trends', 'Exploring the latest tech trends.', '2023-01-04 13:00:00', 2),
(105, 'Advanced SQL', 'Advanced SQL concepts and queries.', '2023-01-05 14:00:00', 1);

-- 1. Select all documents created by a specific author (e.g., 'Alice Smith')
SELECT D.title, D.content
FROM Documents AS D
JOIN Authors AS A ON D.author_id = A.author_id
WHERE A.name = 'Alice Smith';

-- 2. Find the total number of documents for each author.
SELECT A.name, COUNT(D.doc_id) AS total_documents
FROM Authors AS A
JOIN Documents AS D ON A.author_id = D.author_id
GROUP BY A.name;

-- 3. Insert a new document
INSERT INTO Documents (doc_id, title, content, created_at, author_id)
VALUES (106, 'Another Document', 'Content for another document.', '2023-01-06 15:00:00', 2);

-- 4. Update the content of an existing document
UPDATE Documents
SET content = 'Updated content for My First Post.'
WHERE doc_id = 101;

-- 5. Select the 5 most recent documents.
SELECT doc_id, title, created_at
FROM Documents
ORDER BY created_at DESC
LIMIT 5;

-- SEPARATE QUERIES WITH EXACTLY ONE JOIN

-- Select document titles and author emails
SELECT D.title, A.email
FROM Documents AS D
JOIN Authors AS A ON D.author_id = A.author_id;

-- Get author names and their document titles, even if no documents
SELECT A.name, D.title
FROM Authors AS A
LEFT JOIN Documents AS D ON A.author_id = D.author_id;

-- Get documents and author names for specific document ID
SELECT D.title, A.name
FROM Documents AS D
JOIN Authors AS A ON D.author_id = A.author_id
WHERE D.doc_id = 103;

-- List all authors and the count of their documents
SELECT A.name, COUNT(D.doc_id)
FROM Authors AS A
LEFT JOIN Documents AS D ON A.author_id = D.author_id
GROUP BY A.name;

-- Get document creation dates and author names
SELECT D.created_at, A.name
FROM Documents AS D
JOIN Authors AS A ON D.author_id = A.author_id;

-- Select documents whose author's email ends with 'example.com'
SELECT D.title, A.email
FROM Documents AS D
JOIN Authors AS A ON D.author_id = A.author_id
WHERE A.email LIKE '%@example.com';

-- Find documents written by authors whose name starts with 'B'
SELECT D.title, A.name
FROM Documents AS D
JOIN Authors AS A ON D.author_id = A.author_id
WHERE A.name LIKE 'B%';

-- Retrieve author names and the titles of documents they published after '2023-01-03'
SELECT A.name, D.title
FROM Authors AS A
JOIN Documents AS D ON A.author_id = D.author_id
WHERE D.created_at > '2023-01-03';

Queries:
1. Find all available vehicles of a specific model.
2. List all rentals for a given customer.

text_nat:
INSERT INTO Rentals (rental_id, vehicle_id, customer_id, start_date, end_date, total_cost)

    R.end_date,
    V.make,

FROM
    Customers AS C

    Rentals AS R ON C.customer_id = R.customer_id

GROUP BY
    V.vehicle_id, V.make, V.model
ORDER BY

Queries:
1. Find all courses a specific student is enrolled in.
2. List all students enrolled in a particular course.
3. Enroll a student in a new course.
4. Update a student's grade for a course.
5. Count the number of students per department.
text_nat:
INSERT INTO Students (student_id, first_name, last_name, enrollment_date) VALUES

(2, 1, 102, 'B'),
(3, 2, 101, 'C');

-- 1. Find all courses a specific student is enrolled in (e.g., student_id = 1)
SELECT C.title, C.department
FROM Courses AS C
JOIN Enrollments AS E ON C.course_id = E.course_id
WHERE E.student_id = 1;

-- 2. List all students enrolled in a particular course (e.g., course_id = 101)
SELECT S.first_name, S.last_name
FROM Students AS S
JOIN Enrollments AS E ON S.student_id = E.student_id
WHERE E.course_id = 101;

-- 3. Enroll a student in a new course (e.g., student_id = 3 in course_id = 103)
INSERT INTO Enrollments (enrollment_id, student_id, course_id, grade)
VALUES (4, 3, 103, NULL);

-- 4. Update a student's grade for a course (e.g., student_id = 2, course_id = 101, grade = 'B+')
UPDATE Enrollments
SET grade = 'B+'
WHERE student_id = 2 AND course_id = 101;

-- 5. Count the number of students per department.
SELECT C.department, COUNT(DISTINCT E.student_id) AS number_of_students
FROM Courses AS C
JOIN Enrollments AS E ON C.course_id = E.course_id
GROUP BY C.department;

-- Additional explicit JOINs for style requirement

SELECT S.first_name, S.last_name, En.grade
FROM Students AS S
JOIN Enrollments AS En ON S.student_id = En.student_id;

Schema: Recipes (recipe_id INT, name VARCHAR, instructions TEXT, cook_time_minutes INT), Ingredients (ingredient_id INT, name VARCHAR, unit VARCHAR), RecipeIngredients (recipe_id INT, ingredient_id INT, quantity DECIMAL).
Queries:
1. Find all ingredients for a specific recipe.
2. List all recipes that use a particular ingredient.
3. Add a new ingredient to a recipe.
4. Update the cook time of a recipe.
5. Count the number of ingredients per recipe.
text_nat:
SELECT
    I.name AS ingredient_name,
    RI.quantity,
    I.unit
FROM
    Recipes R JOIN RecipeIngredients RI
    ON R.recipe_id = RI.recipe_id
JOIN
    Ingredients I ON RI.ingredient_id = I.ingredient_id
WHERE
    R.name = 'Spaghetti Carbonara';

SELECT
    R.name AS recipe_name,
    R.cook_time_minutes
FROM
    Recipes R JOIN RecipeIngredients RI
    ON R.recipe_id = RI.recipe_id
JOIN
    Ingredients I ON RI.ingredient_id = I.ingredient_id
WHERE
    I.name = 'Garlic';

INSERT INTO RecipeIngredients (recipe_id, ingredient_id, quantity)
SELECT
    R.recipe_id,
    I.ingredient_id,
    2.5
FROM
    Recipes R JOIN Ingredients I
    ON R.name = 'Chicken Stir-Fry' AND I.name = 'Soy Sauce';

UPDATE Recipes
SET cook_time_minutes = 45
WHERE name = 'Beef Stew';

SELECT
    R.name AS recipe_name,

2. List all bugs with status 'Open' or 'Reopened'.

5. Count the number of bugs per status.
text_nat:
INSERT INTO Bugs (bug_id, title, description, status, priority, created_at, assigned_to)

SELECT

    b.title,
    b.status,
    b.priority,
    u.username
FROM
    Bugs AS b

WHERE

SELECT

FROM

WHERE

SELECT
    b.status,

FROM
    Bugs AS b
GROUP BY
    b.status
ORDER BY
    bug_count DESC;

Queries:

2. List all overdue loans.

4. Mark a book as returned, increasing available copies.

text_nat:
SELECT B.title, B.author

JOIN Loans AS L ON B.book_id = L.book_id
WHERE L.borrower_id = 1 AND L.return_date IS NULL;

FROM Loans AS L

JOIN Borrowers AS Bo ON L.borrower_id = Bo.borrower_id
WHERE L.return_date IS NULL AND L.loan_date < DATE('now', '-14 days');

WHERE loan_id = 201;
