Schema: Students (student_id INT, first_name VARCHAR, last_name VARCHAR, major VARCHAR), Courses (course_id INT, title VARCHAR, department VARCHAR, credits INT), Enrollments (enrollment_id INT, student_id INT, course_id INT, enrollment_date DATE, grade VARCHAR).
Queries:
1. Find all courses a specific student is enrolled in.
2. List all students enrolled in a particular course.
3. Enroll a student in a new course.
4. Update a student's grade for a course.
5. Count the total credits a student is enrolled in.
text_nat:
INSERT INTO Students (student_id, first_name, last_name, major) VALUES
(1, 'Alice', 'Smith', 'Computer Science'),
(2, 'Bob', 'Johnson', 'Mathematics');

INSERT INTO Courses (course_id, title, department, credits) VALUES
(101, 'Introduction to SQL', 'Computer Science', 3),
(102, 'Calculus I', 'Mathematics', 4),
(103, 'Data Structures', 'Computer Science', 3);

INSERT INTO Enrollments (enrollment_id, student_id, course_id, enrollment_date, grade) VALUES
(1, 1, 101, '2023-09-01', 'A'),
(2, 1, 103, '2023-09-01', 'B'),
(3, 2, 102, '2023-09-05', 'A');

-- 1. Find all courses a specific student is enrolled in (e.g., student_id = 1)
SELECT C.title, C.department
FROM Courses AS C
JOIN Enrollments AS E
ON C.course_id = E.course_id
WHERE E.student_id = 1;

-- 2. List all students enrolled in a particular course (e.g., course_id = 101)
SELECT S.first_name, S.last_name
FROM Students AS S
JOIN Enrollments AS E
ON S.student_id = E.student_id
WHERE E.course_id = 101;

-- Another way to get all courses for a specific student, using a different join
SELECT C.title
FROM Students AS S
JOIN Enrollments AS E ON S.student_id = E.student_id
JOIN Courses AS C ON E.course_id = C.course_id
WHERE S.first_name = 'Alice';

-- 3. Enroll a student in a new course (e.g., student_id = 2, course_id = 101)
INSERT INTO Enrollments (enrollment_id, student_id, course_id, enrollment_date, grade)
VALUES (4, 2, 101, '2023-10-15', NULL);

-- 4. Update a student's grade for a course (e.g., student_id = 2, course_id = 101, grade = 'B+')
UPDATE Enrollments
SET grade = 'B+'
WHERE student_id = 2 AND course_id = 101;

-- 5. Count the total credits a student is enrolled in (e.g., student_id = 1)
SELECT SUM(C.credits) AS total_credits
FROM Enrollments AS E
JOIN Courses AS C
ON E.course_id = C.course_id
WHERE E.student_id = 1;

-- Another join example: students with their major and all courses they are enrolled in
SELECT S.first_name, S.major, C.title
FROM Students AS S
JOIN Enrollments AS E ON S.student_id = E.student_id
JOIN Courses AS C ON E.course_id = C.course_id;

-- Yet another join: courses and the departments of students enrolled in them
SELECT C.title, S.major
FROM Courses AS C
JOIN Enrollments AS E ON C.course_id = E.course_id
JOIN Students AS S ON E.student_id = S.student_id;

-- All enrollments with student names and course titles
SELECT S.first_name, S.last_name, C.title, E.enrollment_date
FROM Enrollments AS E
JOIN Students AS S ON E.student_id = S.student_id
JOIN Courses AS C ON E.course_id = C.course_id;

-- All courses with their respective departments and credits, joined with enrollments
SELECT C.title, C.department, C.credits, E.enrollment_date
FROM Courses AS C
JOIN Enrollments AS E ON C.course_id = E.course_id;

-- Students and their enrollments
SELECT S.first_name, E.enrollment_date
FROM Students AS S
JOIN Enrollments AS E ON S.student_id = E.student_id;

-- Enrollments and the courses involved
SELECT E.enrollment_id, C.title
FROM Enrollments AS E
JOIN Courses AS C ON E.course_id = C.course_id;

-- All students and their majors
SELECT S.first_name, S.major
FROM Students AS S
LEFT JOIN Enrollments AS E ON S.student_id = E.student_id;

-- All courses and students enrolled
SELECT C.title, S.first_name
FROM Courses AS C
LEFT JOIN Enrollments AS E ON C.course_id = E.course_id
LEFT JOIN Students AS S ON E.student_id = S.student_id;

-- Courses with their departments
SELECT C.title, C.department
FROM Courses AS C
JOIN Courses AS C2 ON C.department = C2.department;

Schema: Jobs (job_id INT, title VARCHAR, company VARCHAR, location VARCHAR, post_date DATE), Applicants (applicant_id INT, first_name VARCHAR, last_name VARCHAR, email VARCHAR), Applications (application_id INT, job_id INT, applicant_id INT, application_date DATE, status VARCHAR).
Queries:
1. Find all applications for a specific job.
2. List all jobs applied to by a particular applicant.
3. Submit a new job application.
4. Update an application's status.
5. Count the number of applications per job.
text_nat:
INSERT INTO Jobs (job_id, title, company, location, post_date) VALUES
(1, 'Software Engineer', 'TechCorp', 'New York', '2023-01-15'),
(2, 'Data Analyst', 'DataCo', 'San Francisco', '2023-02-01'),
(3, 'Project Manager', 'BuildIt', 'Chicago', '2023-03-10');

INSERT INTO Applicants (applicant_id, first_name, last_name, email) VALUES
(101, 'Alice', 'Smith', 'alice.s@example.com'),
(102, 'Bob', 'Johnson', 'bob.j@example.com');

INSERT INTO Applications (application_id, job_id, applicant_id, application_date, status) VALUES
(1001, 1, 101, '2023-01-20', 'Pending'),
(1002, 2, 101, '2023-02-05', 'Approved'),
(1003, 1, 102, '2023-01-22', 'Rejected');

-- 1. Find all applications for a specific job (job_id = 1)
SELECT
    A.application_id,
    A.application_date,
    A.status,
    Ap.first_name,
    Ap.last_name
FROM
    Applications AS A
JOIN
    Applicants AS Ap ON A.applicant_id = Ap.applicant_id
WHERE
    A.job_id = 1;

-- 2. List all jobs applied to by a particular applicant (applicant_id = 101)
SELECT
    J.title,
    J.company,
    A.application_date,
    A.status
FROM
    Applications AS A
JOIN
    Jobs AS J ON A.job_id = J.job_id
WHERE
    A.applicant_id = 101;

-- 3. Submit a new job application
INSERT INTO Applications (application_id, job_id, applicant_id, application_date, status) VALUES
(1004, 3, 101, '2023-03-15', 'Pending');

-- 4. Update an application's status (application_id = 1001 to 'Reviewed')
UPDATE
    Applications
SET
    status = 'Reviewed'
WHERE
    application_id = 1001;

-- 5. Count the number of applications per job
SELECT
    J.title,
    COUNT(A.application_id) AS total_applications
FROM
    Jobs AS J
JOIN
    Applications AS A ON J.job_id = A.job_id
GROUP BY
    J.title;

-- Additional queries with exactly one join
SELECT J.title, J.company FROM Jobs AS J JOIN Applications AS A ON J.job_id = A.job_id;
SELECT Ap.first_name, Ap.email FROM Applicants AS Ap JOIN Applications AS A ON Ap.applicant_id = A.applicant_id;
SELECT A.application_id, J.title FROM Applications AS A JOIN Jobs AS J ON A.job_id = J.job_id;
SELECT A.application_id, Ap.first_name FROM Applications AS A JOIN Applicants AS Ap ON A.applicant_id = Ap.applicant_id;
SELECT J.title, COUNT(*) FROM Jobs AS J JOIN Applications AS A ON J.job_id = A.job_id GROUP BY J.title;

Schema: Posts (post_id INT, title VARCHAR, content TEXT, author_id INT, publish_date DATETIME), Authors (author_id INT, name VARCHAR, email VARCHAR), Comments (comment_id INT, post_id INT, author_id INT, content TEXT, comment_date DATETIME).
Queries:
1. Find all comments on a specific blog post.
2. List all posts written by a particular author.
3. Add a new comment to a post.
4. Update the content of a comment.
5. Count the number of comments per post.
text_nat:
SELECT C.content, C.comment_date
FROM Comments AS C
JOIN Posts AS P
  ON C.post_id = P.post_id
WHERE P.post_id = 1;

SELECT P.title, P.publish_date
FROM Posts AS P
JOIN Authors AS A
  ON P.author_id = A.author_id
WHERE A.author_id = 101;

INSERT INTO Comments (post_id, author_id, content, comment_date)
VALUES (1, 102, 'Great article!', NOW());

UPDATE Comments
SET content = 'Updated comment text.'
WHERE comment_id = 5;

SELECT P.title, COUNT(C.comment_id) AS comment_count
FROM Posts AS P
LEFT JOIN Comments AS C
  ON P.post_id = C.post_id
GROUP BY P.post_id, P.title;

SELECT P.title, A.name AS author_name, C.content AS comment_text
FROM Posts AS P
JOIN Authors AS A
  ON P.author_id = A.author_id
JOIN Comments AS C
  ON P.post_id = C.post_id
WHERE P.post_id = 2;

SELECT C.comment_id, A.name AS commenter_name, C.content
FROM Comments AS C
JOIN Authors AS A
  ON C.author_id = A.author_id
WHERE C.post_id = 3;

SELECT P.title, P.content, A.name
FROM Posts AS P
JOIN Authors AS A
  ON P.author_id = A.author_id
WHERE A.name = 'Jane Doe';

SELECT C.comment_id, P.title
FROM Comments AS C
JOIN Posts AS P
  ON C.post_id = P.post_id
WHERE C.comment_date > '2023-01-01';

SELECT A.name, COUNT(P.post_id) AS total_posts
FROM Authors AS A
LEFT JOIN Posts AS P
  ON A.author_id = P.author_id
GROUP BY A.name;

SELECT C.comment_id, C.content, A.name AS commenter_name, P.title AS post_title
FROM Comments AS C
JOIN Authors AS A
  ON C.author_id = A.author_id
JOIN Posts AS P
  ON C.post_id = P.post_id
WHERE A.author_id = 103;

SELECT P.title, P.publish_date, A.name AS author_name, A.email AS author_email
FROM Posts AS P
JOIN Authors AS A
  ON P.author_id = A.author_id
ORDER BY P.publish_date DESC;

SELECT C.comment_id, C.content, C.comment_date
FROM Comments AS C
JOIN Posts AS P
  ON C.post_id = P.post_id
WHERE P.title LIKE '%SQL%';

SELECT A.name, COUNT(C.comment_id) AS comments_made
FROM Authors AS A
LEFT JOIN Comments AS C
  ON A.author_id = C.author_id
GROUP BY A.name
ORDER BY comments_made DESC;

Schema: Items (item_id INT, name VARCHAR, weight DECIMAL, dimensions VARCHAR), Locations (location_id INT, warehouse_name VARCHAR, aisle VARCHAR, rack VARCHAR), ItemLocations (item_id INT, location_id INT, quantity INT, last_moved DATETIME).
Queries:
1. Find all items stored in a specific aisle of a warehouse.
2. List all locations where a particular item is stored.
3. Add new stock of an item to a location.
4. Move an item from one location to another.
5. Count the total quantity of each item across all locations.
text_nat:
SELECT
    I.name,
    IL.quantity
FROM
    Items I
JOIN
    ItemLocations IL ON I.item_id = IL.item_id
JOIN
    Locations L ON IL.location_id = L.location_id
WHERE
    L.warehouse_name = 'Main Warehouse' AND L.aisle = 'A1';

SELECT
    L.warehouse_name,
    L.aisle,
    L.rack,
    IL.quantity
FROM
    Locations L
JOIN
    ItemLocations IL ON L.location_id = IL.location_id
JOIN
    Items I ON IL.item_id = I.item_id
WHERE
    I.name = 'Laptop';

INSERT INTO ItemLocations (item_id, location_id, quantity, last_moved)
SELECT
    (SELECT item_id FROM Items WHERE name = 'Keyboard'),
    (SELECT location_id FROM Locations WHERE warehouse_name = 'Main Warehouse' AND aisle = 'A2' AND rack = 'R1'),
    50,
    NOW()
ON CONFLICT (item_id, location_id) DO UPDATE SET quantity = ItemLocations.quantity + EXCLUDED.quantity, last_moved = EXCLUDED.last_moved;

UPDATE ItemLocations
SET
    location_id = (SELECT location_id FROM Locations WHERE warehouse_name = 'Main Warehouse' AND aisle = 'A3' AND rack = 'R2'),
    last_moved = NOW()
WHERE
    item_id = (SELECT item_id FROM Items WHERE name = 'Mouse')
    AND location_id = (SELECT location_id FROM Locations WHERE warehouse_name = 'Main Warehouse' AND aisle = 'A1' AND rack = 'R1');

SELECT
    I.name,
    SUM(IL.quantity) AS total_quantity
FROM
    Items I
JOIN
    ItemLocations IL ON I.item_id = IL.item_id
GROUP BY
    I.name;

SELECT I.name FROM Items I JOIN ItemLocations IL ON I.item_id = IL.item_id;

SELECT L.warehouse_name FROM Locations L JOIN ItemLocations IL ON L.location_id = IL.location_id;

SELECT I.name, L.warehouse_name FROM Items I JOIN ItemLocations IL ON I.item_id = IL.item_id JOIN Locations L ON IL.location_id = L.location_id;

SELECT I.item_id, I.name FROM Items I JOIN ItemLocations IL ON I.item_id = IL.item_id;

SELECT L.location_id, L.aisle FROM Locations L JOIN ItemLocations IL ON L.location_id = IL.location_id;

SELECT I.name, L.aisle FROM Items I JOIN ItemLocations IL ON I.item_id = IL.item_id JOIN Locations L ON IL.location_id = L.location_id;

SELECT I.name, IL.quantity FROM Items I JOIN ItemLocations IL ON I.item_id = IL.item_id;

SELECT L.warehouse_name, IL.quantity FROM Locations L JOIN ItemLocations IL ON L.location_id = IL.location_id;

SELECT I.name, L.rack FROM Items I JOIN ItemLocations IL ON I.item_id = IL.item_id JOIN Locations L ON IL.location_id = L.location_id;

Schema: Customers (customer_id INT, name VARCHAR, email VARCHAR), Products (product_id INT, name VARCHAR, description TEXT), Feedback (feedback_id INT, customer_id INT, product_id INT, rating INT, comments TEXT, feedback_date DATETIME).
Queries:
1. Find all feedback for a specific product with a rating below 3.
2. List all feedback submitted by a particular customer.
3. Submit new product feedback.
4. Update the comments of an existing feedback entry.
5. Calculate the average rating for each product.
text_nat:
SELECT F.feedback_id, F.rating, F.comments
FROM Feedback AS F
JOIN Products AS P ON F.product_id = P.product_id
WHERE P.name = 'Echo Dot' AND F.rating < 3;

SELECT C.name, C.email, F.feedback_id, F.rating, F.comments
FROM Customers AS C
JOIN Feedback AS F ON C.customer_id = F.customer_id
WHERE C.name = 'Alice Smith';

INSERT INTO Feedback (customer_id, product_id, rating, comments, feedback_date)
VALUES (1, 3, 5, 'Excellent product, highly recommend!', NOW());

UPDATE Feedback
SET comments = 'Improved a lot with the new update!'
WHERE feedback_id = 101;

SELECT P.name, AVG(F.rating) AS average_rating
FROM Products AS P
JOIN Feedback AS F ON P.product_id = F.product_id
GROUP BY P.name;

SELECT C.name, P.name, F.rating, F.comments
FROM Customers AS C
JOIN Feedback AS F ON C.customer_id = F.customer_id
JOIN Products AS P ON F.product_id = P.product_id
WHERE F.rating = 5;

SELECT C.name, C.email
FROM Customers AS C
LEFT JOIN Feedback AS F ON C.customer_id = F.customer_id
WHERE F.feedback_id IS NULL;

SELECT P.name, COUNT(F.feedback_id) AS total_feedback
FROM Products AS P
JOIN Feedback AS F ON P.product_id = F.product_id
GROUP BY P.name
ORDER BY total_feedback DESC;

SELECT F.feedback_id, C.name AS customer_name
FROM Feedback AS F
JOIN Customers AS C ON F.customer_id = C.customer_id;

SELECT F.feedback_id, P.name AS product_name
FROM Feedback AS F
JOIN Products AS P ON F.product_id = P.product_id;

SELECT C.customer_id, C.name, COUNT(F.feedback_id) AS feedback_count
FROM Customers AS C
LEFT JOIN Feedback AS F ON C.customer_id = F.customer_id
GROUP BY C.customer_id, C.name
ORDER BY feedback_count DESC;

SELECT F.feedback_id, F.rating, F.comments, C.name AS customer_name, P.name AS product_name
FROM Feedback AS F
JOIN Customers AS C ON F.customer_id = C.customer_id
JOIN Products AS P ON F.product_id = P.product_id
WHERE F.feedback_date >= '2023-01-01' AND F.rating >= 4;

SELECT P.name AS product_name, P.description
FROM Products AS P
LEFT JOIN Feedback AS F ON P.product_id = F.product_id
WHERE F.feedback_id IS NULL;

SELECT C.name, C.email, F.feedback_date
FROM Customers AS C
INNER JOIN Feedback AS F ON C.customer_id = F.customer_id
ORDER BY F.feedback_date DESC;

SELECT P.name, AVG(F.rating) AS avg_rating
FROM Products AS P
INNER JOIN Feedback AS F ON P.product_id = F.product_id
GROUP BY P.name;

Schema: Transactions (transaction_id INT, user_id INT, amount DECIMAL, currency VARCHAR, transaction_date DATETIME, status VARCHAR), Users (user_id INT, username VARCHAR, email VARCHAR).
Queries:
1. Find all transactions made by a specific user that are 'completed'.
2. List all transactions with a 'failed' status.
3. Record a new transaction.
4. Update a transaction's status.
5. Calculate the total amount of transactions per currency.
text_nat:
SELECT T.transaction_id, T.amount, T.currency, T.transaction_date
FROM Transactions AS T
JOIN Users AS U ON T.user_id = U.user_id
WHERE U.username = 'specific_user_name' AND T.status = 'completed';

SELECT T.transaction_id, T.amount, T.currency, T.transaction_date, U.username
FROM Transactions AS T
JOIN Users AS U ON T.user_id = U.user_id
WHERE T.status = 'failed';

INSERT INTO Transactions (user_id, amount, currency, transaction_date, status)
VALUES (1, 50.00, 'USD', NOW(), 'pending');

UPDATE Transactions
SET status = 'completed'
WHERE transaction_id = 123;

SELECT currency, SUM(amount) AS total_amount
FROM Transactions
GROUP BY currency;

SELECT T.transaction_id, T.amount
FROM Transactions AS T
JOIN Users AS U ON T.user_id = U.user_id
WHERE U.email = 'user@example.com';

SELECT U.username, T.transaction_id
FROM Users AS U
JOIN Transactions AS T ON U.user_id = T.user_id
WHERE T.amount > 100;

SELECT T.transaction_id, T.currency
FROM Transactions AS T
JOIN Users AS U ON T.user_id = U.user_id
WHERE T.transaction_date BETWEEN '2023-01-01' AND '2023-01-31';

SELECT U.username, T.status
FROM Users AS U
JOIN Transactions AS T ON U.user_id = T.user_id
WHERE T.status = 'pending';

SELECT T.amount, U.email
FROM Transactions AS T
JOIN Users AS U ON T.user_id = U.user_id
ORDER BY T.amount DESC;

SELECT U.username, U.email
FROM Users AS U
JOIN Transactions AS T ON U.user_id = T.user_id
GROUP BY U.user_id
HAVING COUNT(T.transaction_id) > 5;

SELECT T.transaction_id, T.transaction_date
FROM Transactions AS T
JOIN Users AS U ON T.user_id = U.user_id
WHERE U.username LIKE 'A%';

SELECT U.username, T.currency
FROM Users AS U
JOIN Transactions AS T ON U.user_id = T.user_id
WHERE T.currency = 'EUR';

SELECT T.status, COUNT(T.transaction_id) AS transaction_count
FROM Transactions AS T
JOIN Users AS U ON T.user_id = U.user_id
GROUP BY T.status;

2. List all leads from a particular company.
3. Create a new sales lead.
4. Update a lead's status to 'Qualified'.
5. Count the number of leads per status.
text_nat:
SELECT *
FROM Leads
WHERE assigned_to = 'John Doe'
AND status = 'New';

SELECT *
FROM Leads
WHERE company = 'Acme Corp';

UPDATE Leads
SET status = 'Qualified'
WHERE lead_id = 55;

SELECT status, COUNT(*) AS lead_count
FROM Leads
GROUP BY status;

SELECT L.name, L.company, S.name AS salesperson_name
FROM Leads AS L
JOIN Salespeople AS S ON L.assigned_to = S.name
WHERE S.region = 'West';

SELECT L.name, S.name AS salesperson_name
FROM Leads AS L
JOIN Salespeople AS S ON L.assigned_to = S.name;

SELECT L.name, L.email, S.region

SELECT L.name, S.name AS salesperson_name

SELECT S.name AS salesperson_name, COUNT(L.lead_id) AS total_leads
FROM Salespeople AS S
LEFT JOIN Leads AS L ON S.name = L.assigned_to

SELECT L.lead_id, L.name, S.name AS salesperson_name, S.region

SELECT L.name, S.name AS salesperson_name

SELECT L.lead_id, L.name, L.status, S.name AS assigned_salesperson
FROM Leads AS L
JOIN Salespeople AS S ON L.assigned_to = S.name
WHERE L.created_at BETWEEN '2023-01-01' AND '2023-01-31';

SELECT L.lead_id, L.name, S.name AS salesperson_name
FROM Leads AS L
JOIN Salespeople AS S ON L.assigned_to = S.name;

SELECT L.name, S.name AS salesperson_name
FROM Leads AS L

Schema: Artists (artist_id INT, name VARCHAR, genre VARCHAR), Albums (album_id INT, artist_id INT, title VARCHAR, release_year INT), Tracks (track_id INT, album_id INT, title VARCHAR, duration_seconds INT).
Queries:
1. Find all albums by a specific artist.
2. List all tracks on a particular album.
3. Add a new album.
4. Update the release year of an album.
5. Count the total duration of tracks per album.
text_nat:
CREATE TABLE Artists (
    artist_id INT PRIMARY KEY,
    name VARCHAR(255),
    genre VARCHAR(255)
);

CREATE TABLE Albums (
    album_id INT PRIMARY KEY,
    artist_id INT,
    title VARCHAR(255),
    release_year INT,
    FOREIGN KEY (artist_id) REFERENCES Artists(artist_id)
);

CREATE TABLE Tracks (
    track_id INT PRIMARY KEY,
    album_id INT,
    title VARCHAR(255),
    duration_seconds INT,
    FOREIGN KEY (album_id) REFERENCES Albums(album_id)
);

Schema: Teams (team_id INT, name VARCHAR, city VARCHAR), Matches (match_id INT, home_team_id INT, away_team_id INT, match_date DATETIME, home_score INT, away_score INT), Players (player_id INT, team_id INT, name VARCHAR, position VARCHAR).
Queries:
1. Find all matches played by a specific team.
2. List all players on a particular team.
3. Record a new match score.
4. Update a player's position.
5. Calculate the total wins for each team.

INSERT INTO Teams (team_id, name, city) VALUES (1, 'Real Madrid', 'Madrid');

-- 1. Find all matches played by a specific team (e.g., 'Real Madrid')
SELECT m.*
FROM Matches m
JOIN Teams t ON m.home_team_id = t.team_id
WHERE t.name = 'Real Madrid'
UNION ALL
SELECT m.*
FROM Matches m
JOIN Teams t ON m.away_team_id = t.team_id
WHERE t.name = 'Real Madrid';

-- 2. List all players on a particular team (e.g., 'Barcelona')
SELECT p.name, p.position
FROM Players p
JOIN Teams t ON p.team_id = t.team_id
WHERE t.name = 'Barcelona';

-- 3. Record a new match score (assuming match_id 3 already exists with null scores)
UPDATE Matches
SET home_score = 3, away_score = 0
WHERE match_id = 1;

-- 4. Update a player's position (e.g., player_id 1 to 'Striker')
UPDATE Players
SET position = 'Striker'
WHERE player_id = 1;

-- 5. Calculate the total wins for each team
SELECT t.name, COUNT(t.team_id) AS total_wins
FROM Teams t
JOIN Matches m ON t.team_id = m.home_team_id AND m.home_score > m.away_score
GROUP BY t.name
UNION ALL
SELECT t.name, COUNT(t.team_id) AS total_wins
FROM Teams t
JOIN Matches m ON t.team_id = m.away_team_id AND m.away_score > m.home_score
GROUP BY t.name;

FROM Players P
JOIN Teams T ON P.team_id = T.team_id;

GROUP BY T.name;

SELECT T.name, COUNT(M.match_id) AS away_matches

JOIN Matches M ON T.team_id = M.away_team_id
GROUP BY T.name;

SELECT P.name, P.position

WHERE T.name = 'Real Madrid';

SELECT M.match_id, M.match_date
FROM Matches M
JOIN Teams T ON M.home_team_id = T.team_id
WHERE T.name = 'Barcelona';

Queries:

Schema: Projects (project_id INT, name VARCHAR, manager_id INT, start_date DATE, end_date DATE), Employees (employee_id INT, name VARCHAR, position VARCHAR), ProjectAssignments (project_id INT, employee_id INT, role VARCHAR, start_date DATE, end_date DATE).
Queries:
1. Find all employees assigned to a specific project.
2. List all projects managed by a particular employee.
3. Assign an employee to a project.
4. Update an employee's role on a project.
5. Count the number of employees per project.
text_nat:
-- 1. Find all employees assigned to a specific project.
SELECT E.name AS employee_name, PA.role
FROM Employees AS E
JOIN ProjectAssignments AS PA ON E.employee_id = PA.employee_id
WHERE PA.project_id = 1;

-- 2. List all projects managed by a particular employee.
SELECT P.name AS project_name, P.start_date, P.end_date
FROM Projects AS P
JOIN Employees AS E ON P.manager_id = E.employee_id
WHERE E.employee_id = 2;

-- 3. Assign an employee to a project (example: employee 3 to project 2, role 'Developer').
INSERT INTO ProjectAssignments (project_id, employee_id, role, start_date, end_date)
VALUES (2, 3, 'Developer', '2023-01-15', '2023-06-15');

-- 4. Update an employee's role on a project (example: employee 3 on project 2 to 'Lead Developer').
UPDATE ProjectAssignments
SET role = 'Lead Developer'
WHERE project_id = 2 AND employee_id = 3;

-- 5. Count the number of employees per project.
SELECT P.name AS project_name, COUNT(PA.employee_id) AS number_of_employees
FROM Projects AS P
JOIN ProjectAssignments AS PA ON P.project_id = PA.project_id
GROUP BY P.name;

SELECT P.name AS project_name, E.name AS manager_name
FROM Projects AS P
JOIN Employees AS E ON P.manager_id = E.employee_id;

SELECT E.name AS employee_name, PA.role, P.name AS project_name
FROM Employees AS E
JOIN ProjectAssignments AS PA ON E.employee_id = PA.employee_id
JOIN Projects AS P ON PA.project_id = P.project_id
WHERE E.employee_id = 1;

SELECT P.name AS project_name, P.start_date, P.end_date, E.name AS manager_name
FROM Projects AS P
JOIN Employees AS E ON P.manager_id = E.employee_id
WHERE P.start_date < '2023-03-01';

SELECT E.name AS employee_name, PA.role
FROM Employees AS E
JOIN ProjectAssignments AS PA ON E.employee_id = PA.employee_id
WHERE PA.end_date > '2023-04-01';

SELECT P.name AS project_name, PA.role, E.name AS employee_name
FROM Projects AS P
JOIN ProjectAssignments AS PA ON P.project_id = PA.project_id
JOIN Employees AS E ON PA.employee_id = E.employee_id

SELECT E.name AS employee_name, P.name AS project_name

JOIN Projects AS P ON PA.project_id = P.project_id

SELECT E.name AS employee_name, E.position

Schema: Users (user_id INT, username VARCHAR, registration_date DATETIME, last_login DATETIME), Pages (page_id INT, url VARCHAR, title VARCHAR), PageViews (view_id INT, user_id INT, page_id INT, view_date DATETIME).
Queries:
1. Find all pages viewed by a specific user.
2. List the top 5 most viewed pages.
3. Record a new page view.
4. Update a user's last login date.
5. Count the total page views for each user.
text_nat:
-- Query 1: Find all pages viewed by a specific user (e.g., user_id = 1)
SELECT DISTINCT P.title, P.url
FROM Pages AS P
JOIN PageViews AS PV ON P.page_id = PV.page_id
WHERE PV.user_id = 1;

-- Query 2: List the top 5 most viewed pages
SELECT P.title, COUNT(PV.page_id) AS view_count
FROM Pages AS P
JOIN PageViews AS PV ON P.page_id = PV.page_id
GROUP BY P.title
ORDER BY view_count DESC
LIMIT 5;

-- Query 3: Record a new page view
-- (Assuming user_id = 1, page_id = 2, view_date = '2023-10-27 10:30:00')
INSERT INTO PageViews (user_id, page_id, view_date)
VALUES (1, 2, '2023-10-27 10:30:00');

-- Query 4: Update a user's last login date (e.g., user_id = 1)
UPDATE Users
SET last_login = '2023-10-27 10:35:00'
WHERE user_id = 1;

-- Query 5: Count the total page views for each user
SELECT U.username, COUNT(PV.view_id) AS total_views
FROM Users AS U
JOIN PageViews AS PV ON U.user_id = PV.user_id
GROUP BY U.username
ORDER BY total_views DESC;

-- Additional queries with single JOINs:

-- Find all users who viewed a specific page (e.g., page_id = 3)
SELECT U.username
FROM Users AS U
JOIN PageViews AS PV ON U.user_id = PV.user_id
WHERE PV.page_id = 3;

-- Get page details for a specific view_id (e.g., view_id = 5)
SELECT P.title, P.url
FROM Pages AS P
JOIN PageViews AS PV ON P.page_id = PV.page_id
WHERE PV.view_id = 5;

-- Get user details for a specific view_id (e.g., view_id = 5)
SELECT U.username, U.registration_date
FROM Users AS U
JOIN PageViews AS PV ON U.user_id = PV.user_id
WHERE PV.view_id = 5;

-- List all pages and their titles
SELECT P.page_id, P.title
FROM Pages AS P;

-- List users who have logged in after their registration date
SELECT U.username
FROM Users AS U
WHERE U.last_login > U.registration_date;

-- Count views per page, ordered by page_id
SELECT P.title, COUNT(PV.page_id)
FROM Pages AS P
JOIN PageViews AS PV ON P.page_id = PV.page_id
GROUP BY P.page_id
ORDER BY P.page_id;

-- Get the latest view date for each user
SELECT U.username, MAX(PV.view_date) AS latest_view
FROM Users AS U
JOIN PageViews AS PV ON U.user_id = PV.user_id
GROUP BY U.username;

-- Find pages viewed on a specific date (e.g., '2023-10-27')
SELECT DISTINCT P.title
FROM Pages AS P
JOIN PageViews AS PV ON P.page_id = PV.page_id
WHERE DATE(PV.view_date) = '2023-10-27';

WHERE P.page_id = PV.page_id
GROUP BY P.page_id
ORDER BY P.page_id;

-- Get the latest view date for each user
SELECT U.username, MAX(PV.view_date) AS latest_view
FROM Users AS U, PageViews AS PV
WHERE U.user_id = PV.user_id
GROUP BY U.username;

-- Find pages viewed on a specific date (e.g., '2023-10-27')
SELECT DISTINCT P.title
FROM Pages AS P, PageViews AS PV
WHERE P.page_id = PV.page_id
AND DATE(PV.view_date) = '2023-10-27';

Schema: Users (user_id INT, username VARCHAR, email VARCHAR), Repositories (repo_id INT, name VARCHAR, owner_id INT, created_at DATETIME), Commits (commit_id INT, repo_id INT, user_id INT, commit_message TEXT, commit_date DATETIME).
Queries:
1. Find all commits made by a specific user in a repository.
2. List all repositories owned by a particular user.
3. Record a new commit to a repository.
4. Update a repository's name.
5. Count the number of commits per repository.
text_nat:
SELECT
  C.commit_id,
  C.commit_message,
  C.commit_date
FROM Commits AS C
JOIN Users AS U
  ON C.user_id = U.user_id
JOIN Repositories AS R
  ON C.repo_id = R.repo_id
WHERE
  U.username = 'octocat' AND R.name = 'my-awesome-repo';

SELECT
  R.repo_id,
  R.name,
  R.created_at
FROM Repositories AS R
JOIN Users AS U
  ON R.owner_id = U.user_id
WHERE
  U.username = 'octocat';

INSERT INTO Commits (repo_id, user_id, commit_message, commit_date)
VALUES (
  (
    SELECT
      repo_id
    FROM Repositories
    WHERE
      name = 'my-awesome-repo'
  ),
  (
    SELECT
      user_id
    FROM Users
    WHERE
      username = 'octocat'
  ),
  'Initial commit',
  NOW()
);

UPDATE Repositories
SET
  name = 'my-fantastic-repo'
WHERE
  repo_id = (
    SELECT
      repo_id
    FROM Repositories
    WHERE
      name = 'my-awesome-repo'
  );

SELECT
  R.name,
  COUNT(C.commit_id) AS commit_count
FROM Repositories AS R
JOIN Commits AS C
  ON R.repo_id = C.repo_id
GROUP BY
  R.name
ORDER BY
  commit_count DESC;

SELECT
  U.username,
  R.name
FROM Users AS U
JOIN Repositories AS R
  ON U.user_id = R.owner_id;

SELECT
  C.commit_message,

JOIN Users AS U
  ON C.user_id = U.user_id;

JOIN Commits AS C

SELECT

  ON U.user_id = C.user_id;

SELECT

Schema: Products (product_id INT, name VARCHAR, material VARCHAR), ProductionBatches (batch_id INT, product_id INT, quantity INT, start_date DATETIME, end_date DATETIME, status VARCHAR), Employees (employee_id INT, name VARCHAR, role VARCHAR).
Queries:
1. Find all production batches for a specific product with 'Completed' status.
2. List all products produced in batches that started after a certain date.
3. Record a new production batch.
4. Update a batch's status to 'In Progress'.
5. Calculate the total quantity produced for each product.
text_nat:
SELECT PB.batch_id, PB.quantity, PB.start_date, PB.end_date
FROM ProductionBatches AS PB
JOIN Products AS P ON PB.product_id = P.product_id
WHERE P.name = 'Laptop' AND PB.status = 'Completed';

SELECT P.name, PB.start_date
FROM Products AS P
JOIN ProductionBatches AS PB ON P.product_id = PB.product_id
WHERE PB.start_date > '2023-01-01';

INSERT INTO ProductionBatches (product_id, quantity, start_date, end_date, status)
VALUES (101, 50, '2023-03-15', '2023-03-20', 'Scheduled');

UPDATE ProductionBatches
SET status = 'In Progress'
WHERE batch_id = 5;

SELECT P.name, SUM(PB.quantity) AS total_quantity_produced
FROM Products AS P
JOIN ProductionBatches AS PB ON P.product_id = PB.product_id
GROUP BY P.name;

SELECT PB.batch_id, P.name AS product_name
FROM ProductionBatches AS PB
JOIN Products AS P ON PB.product_id = P.product_id;

Schema: Routes (route_id INT, route_number VARCHAR, description TEXT), Stops (stop_id INT, name VARCHAR, latitude DECIMAL, longitude DECIMAL), RouteStops (route_id INT, stop_id INT, stop_order INT).
Queries:
1. Find all stops for a specific route.
2. List all routes that pass through a particular stop.
3. Add a new stop to a route.
4. Update a stop's latitude and longitude.
5. Count the number of stops per route.
text_nat:
-- 1. Find all stops for a specific route (e.g., route_id = 1)
SELECT S.name, S.latitude, S.longitude
FROM Stops AS S
JOIN RouteStops AS RS ON S.stop_id = RS.stop_id
WHERE RS.route_id = 1
ORDER BY RS.stop_order;

-- 2. List all routes that pass through a particular stop (e.g., stop_id = 101)
SELECT R.route_number, R.description
FROM Routes AS R
JOIN RouteStops AS RS ON R.route_id = RS.route_id
WHERE RS.stop_id = 101;

-- Add a new stop to a route (e.g., route_id = 2, stop_id = 105, at order 3)
INSERT INTO RouteStops (route_id, stop_id, stop_order)
VALUES (2, 105, 3);

-- Update a stop's latitude and longitude (e.g., stop_id = 102)
UPDATE Stops
SET latitude = 34.0522, longitude = -118.2437
WHERE stop_id = 102;

-- 5. Count the number of stops per route
SELECT R.route_number, COUNT(RS.stop_id) AS num_stops
FROM Routes AS R
JOIN RouteStops AS RS ON R.route_id = RS.route_id
GROUP BY R.route_number
ORDER BY num_stops DESC;

-- Example query 1: All stops on a route, including route description
SELECT S.name, S.latitude, S.longitude, R.description
FROM Stops AS S
JOIN RouteStops AS RS ON S.stop_id = RS.stop_id
JOIN Routes AS R ON RS.route_id = R.route_id
WHERE R.route_number = 'A101'
ORDER BY RS.stop_order;

-- Example query 2: Routes and their first stop
SELECT R.route_number, R.description, S.name AS first_stop_name
FROM Routes AS R
JOIN RouteStops AS RS ON R.route_id = RS.route_id
JOIN Stops AS S ON RS.stop_id = S.stop_id
WHERE RS.stop_order = 1;

-- Example query 3: Stops that are part of more than one route
SELECT S.name, COUNT(RS.route_id) AS num_routes
FROM Stops AS S
JOIN RouteStops AS RS ON S.stop_id = RS.stop_id
GROUP BY S.name
HAVING COUNT(RS.route_id) > 1;

-- Example query 4: Routes with no stops
SELECT R.route_number
FROM Routes AS R
LEFT JOIN RouteStops AS RS ON R.route_id = RS.route_id
WHERE RS.stop_id IS NULL;

-- Example single-join query: Get route number for each RouteStop entry
SELECT RS.route_id, R.route_number
FROM RouteStops AS RS
JOIN Routes AS R ON RS.route_id = R.route_id;

-- Another single-join query: Get stop name for each RouteStop entry
SELECT RS.stop_id, S.name
FROM RouteStops AS RS
JOIN Stops AS S ON RS.stop_id = S.stop_id;

-- Single-join query: Find stops by name (e.g., 'Central Station')
SELECT S.stop_id, S.latitude, S.longitude
FROM Stops AS S
WHERE S.name = 'Central Station';

-- Single-join query: All routes and their route number
SELECT route_id, route_number
FROM Routes;

-- Single-join query: All stops and their details
SELECT stop_id, name, latitude, longitude
FROM Stops;

-- Single-join query: All route-stop relationships
SELECT route_id, stop_id, stop_order
FROM RouteStops;

Schema: Users (user_id INT, username VARCHAR, email VARCHAR), Conversations (conversation_id INT, user1_id INT, user2_id INT, created_at DATETIME), Messages (message_id INT, conversation_id INT, sender_id INT, content TEXT, sent_at DATETIME).
Queries:
1. Find all messages in a specific conversation.
2. List all conversations involving a particular user.
3. Send a new message in a conversation.
4. Update a user's email.
5. Count the number of messages sent by each user.
text_nat:
SELECT *
FROM Messages
JOIN Conversations ON Messages.conversation_id = Conversations.conversation_id
WHERE Messages.conversation_id = 1;

SELECT C.conversation_id, U1.username AS user1_username, U2.username AS user2_username
FROM Conversations AS C
JOIN Users AS U1 ON C.user1_id = U1.user_id
JOIN Users AS U2 ON C.user2_id = U2.user_id
WHERE C.user1_id = 1 OR C.user2_id = 1;

INSERT INTO Messages (conversation_id, sender_id, content, sent_at)
VALUES (1, 2, 'Hello there!', NOW());

UPDATE Users
SET email = 'new_email@example.com'
WHERE user_id = 1;

SELECT U.username, COUNT(M.message_id) AS message_count
FROM Users AS U
JOIN Messages AS M ON U.user_id = M.sender_id
GROUP BY U.username;

SELECT C.conversation_id, COUNT(M.message_id) AS total_messages
FROM Conversations AS C
JOIN Messages AS M ON C.conversation_id = M.conversation_id
GROUP BY C.conversation_id;

SELECT U.username, M.content
FROM Users AS U
JOIN Messages AS M ON U.user_id = M.sender_id
WHERE M.conversation_id = 1;

SELECT C.conversation_id, U.username
FROM Conversations AS C
JOIN Users AS U ON C.user1_id = U.user_id;

SELECT M.content, C.created_at
FROM Messages AS M
JOIN Conversations AS C ON M.conversation_id = C.conversation_id;

SELECT U.username, U.email
FROM Users AS U
JOIN Conversations AS C ON U.user_id = C.user1_id
WHERE C.conversation_id = 2;

SELECT M.message_id, M.content, U.username AS sender_username
FROM Messages AS M
JOIN Users AS U ON M.sender_id = U.user_id
WHERE M.conversation_id = 3;

SELECT U.username, U.email, C.created_at
FROM Users AS U
JOIN Conversations AS C ON U.user1_id = C.user_id
OR U.user2_id = C.user_id
WHERE U.user_id = 1;

SELECT M.message_id, M.content, C.conversation_id, U1.username AS sender_username, U2.username AS recipient_username
FROM Messages AS M
JOIN Conversations AS C ON M.conversation_id = C.conversation_id
JOIN Users AS U1 ON M.sender_id = U1.user_id
JOIN Users AS U2 ON C.user1_id = U2.user_id OR C.user2_id = U2.user_id AND U2.user_id != U1.user_id
WHERE M.conversation_id = 1;

text_nat:
SELECT *
FROM Licenses
JOIN Content ON Licenses.content_id = Content.content_id
WHERE Licenses.content_id = 1;

SELECT C.title, C.type, C.creator
FROM Content AS C
JOIN Licenses AS L ON C.content_id = L.content_id
JOIN Users AS U ON L.user_id = U.user_id
WHERE U.username = 'alice';

INSERT INTO Licenses (content_id, user_id, license_type, issue_date, expiry_date)
VALUES (101, 201, 'premium', '2023-10-26', '2024-10-26');

UPDATE Licenses
SET expiry_date = '2025-01-01'
WHERE license_id = 5;

SELECT C.type, COUNT(L.license_id) AS license_count
FROM Content AS C
JOIN Licenses AS L ON C.content_id = L.content_id
GROUP BY C.type;

SELECT L.license_id, C.title, U.username
FROM Licenses AS L
JOIN Content AS C ON L.content_id = C.content_id
JOIN Users AS U ON L.user_id = U.user_id;

SELECT U.username, COUNT(L.license_id) AS total_licenses
FROM Users AS U
JOIN Licenses AS L ON U.user_id = L.user_id
GROUP BY U.username;

SELECT C.title, L.issue_date
FROM Content AS C
JOIN Licenses AS L ON C.content_id = L.content_id
WHERE C.type = 'movie';

SELECT L.license_type, U.email
FROM Licenses AS L
JOIN Users AS U ON L.user_id = U.user_id
WHERE L.license_type = 'standard';

SELECT C.creator, COUNT(L.license_id) AS licenses_by_creator
FROM Content AS C
JOIN Licenses AS L ON C.content_id = L.content_id
GROUP BY C.creator;

SELECT U.username, C.title
FROM Users AS U
JOIN Licenses AS L ON U.user_id = L.user_id
JOIN Content AS C ON L.content_id = C.content_id;

SELECT L.expiry_date, C.title
FROM Licenses AS L
JOIN Content AS C ON L.content_id = C.content_id
WHERE L.expiry_date < CURRENT_DATE();

SELECT U.username, L.issue_date
FROM Users AS U
JOIN Licenses AS L ON U.user_id = L.user_id
ORDER BY L.issue_date DESC;

SELECT C.title, C.type
FROM Content AS C
JOIN Licenses AS L ON C.content_id = L.content_id
WHERE C.creator = 'Jane Doe';

Schema: 
`Books` (book_id PK, title, author_id, genre, publication_date, status)
`Authors` (author_id PK, first_name, last_name, email)
`Editors` (editor_id PK, first_name, last_name, specialty)

Queries:
1. Get all books published by a specific author, ordered by publication date.
2. Count the number of books in each genre.
3. Find books currently in 'Editing' status and their authors.
4. Insert a new book and its author.
5. Update the status of a book from 'Draft' to 'Submitted for Review'.
text_nat:
-- Query 1: Get all books published by a specific author, ordered by publication date.
SELECT
    B.title,
    B.publication_date
FROM
    Books AS B
JOIN
    Authors AS A
ON
    B.author_id = A.author_id
WHERE
    A.first_name = 'Jane' AND A.last_name = 'Doe'
ORDER BY
    B.publication_date;

-- Query 2: Count the number of books in each genre.
SELECT
    genre,
    COUNT(book_id) AS number_of_books
FROM
    Books
GROUP BY
    genre;

-- Query 3: Find books currently in 'Editing' status and their authors.
SELECT
    B.title,
    A.first_name,
    A.last_name
FROM
    Books AS B
JOIN Authors AS A
ON B.author_id = A.author_id
WHERE
    B.status = 'Editing';

-- Query 4: Insert a new book and its author.
INSERT INTO Authors (author_id, first_name, last_name, email)
VALUES (4, 'New', 'Author', 'new.author@example.com');

INSERT INTO Books (book_id, title, author_id, genre, publication_date, status)
VALUES (6, 'The New Adventure', 4, 'Adventure', '2023-10-26', 'Draft');

-- Query 5: Update the status of a book from 'Draft' to 'Submitted for Review'.
UPDATE
    Books
SET
    status = 'Submitted for Review'
WHERE
    book_id = 1 AND status = 'Draft';

-- Additional queries with single JOINs

-- Get all books by authors whose last name starts with 'S'
SELECT
    B.title,
    A.first_name,
    A.last_name
FROM
    Books AS B
JOIN Authors AS A
ON B.author_id = A.author_id
WHERE
    A.last_name LIKE 'S%';

-- Get all authors and the titles of their books
SELECT
    A.first_name,
    A.last_name,
    B.title
FROM
    Authors AS A
JOIN Books AS B
ON A.author_id = B.author_id;

-- Find books published after 2020 and their author's email
SELECT
    B.title,
    A.email
FROM
    Books AS B
JOIN Authors AS A
ON B.author_id = A.author_id
WHERE
    B.publication_date > '2020-01-01';

-- List all authors and books, even if an author has no books (LEFT JOIN)
SELECT
    A.first_name,
    A.last_name,
    B.title
FROM
    Authors AS A
LEFT JOIN Books AS B
ON A.author_id = B.author_id;

-- Find books with 'Fantasy' genre and their authors' full names
SELECT
    B.title,
    A.first_name || ' ' || A.last_name AS author_full_name
FROM
    Books AS B
JOIN Authors AS A
ON B.author_id = A.author_id
WHERE
    B.genre = 'Fantasy';

-- Get the title of books and the specialty of editors (no direct link, so this is just an example of a join with a condition)
-- This specific query would only make sense if there was a link between Books and Editors, but for the sake of the exercise...
SELECT
    B.title,
    E.specialty
FROM
    Books AS B
JOIN Editors AS E
ON B.book_id = E.editor_id  -- Assuming a hypothetical link or for illustration
WHERE
    E.specialty = 'Fiction';

SELECT DISTINCT
    A.first_name,

FROM
    Authors AS A
JOIN Books AS B
ON A.author_id = B.author_id
WHERE
    B.genre = 'Mystery';

SELECT
    B.title,
    A.last_name
FROM
    Books AS B
JOIN Authors AS A
ON B.author_id = A.author_id
WHERE
    B.status = 'Published';

Schema: 
`Courses` (course_id PK, course_name, instructor_id, credits)
`Students` (student_id PK, first_name, last_name, email)
`Enrollments` (enrollment_id PK, student_id FK, course_id FK, enrollment_date, grade)

Queries:
1. List all courses a specific student is enrolled in, including their grades.
2. Find all students enrolled in a particular course.
3. Count the number of students enrolled in each course.
4. Enroll a student in a new course.
5. Update the grade for a specific student in a specific course.
text_nat:
-- 1. List all courses a specific student is enrolled in, including their grades.
SELECT
    C.course_name,
    E.grade
FROM
    Enrollments AS E
JOIN
    Courses AS C ON E.course_id = C.course_id
WHERE
    E.student_id = 1;

-- 2. Find all students enrolled in a particular course.
SELECT
    S.first_name,
    S.last_name
FROM
    Enrollments AS E
JOIN
    Students AS S ON E.student_id = S.student_id
WHERE
    E.course_id = 101;

-- 3. Count the number of students enrolled in each course.
SELECT
    C.course_name,
    COUNT(E.student_id) AS student_count
FROM
    Courses AS C
LEFT JOIN
    Enrollments AS E ON C.course_id = E.course_id
GROUP BY
    C.course_name;

-- 4. Enroll a student in a new course.
INSERT INTO Enrollments (student_id, course_id, enrollment_date, grade)
SELECT
    S.student_id,
    C.course_id,
    CURRENT_DATE,
    NULL
FROM
    Students AS S
JOIN
    Courses AS C ON C.course_id = 103 -- Assuming course_id 103 for the new course
WHERE
    S.student_id = 2; -- Assuming student_id 2 for the student to enroll

-- 5. Update the grade for a specific student in a specific course.
UPDATE Enrollments
SET grade = 'A'
FROM
    Students AS S
JOIN
    Courses AS C ON Enrollments.course_id = C.course_id
WHERE
    Enrollments.student_id = S.student_id
    AND S.student_id = 1
    AND Enrollments.course_id = 101;
text_alt:
-- 1. List all courses a specific student is enrolled in, including their grades.
SELECT
    C.course_name,
    E.grade
FROM
    Enrollments AS E,
    Courses AS C
WHERE
    E.course_id = C.course_id
    AND E.student_id = 1;

-- 2. Find all students enrolled in a particular course.
SELECT
    S.first_name,
    S.last_name
FROM
    Enrollments AS E,
    Students AS S
WHERE
    E.student_id = S.student_id
    AND E.course_id = 101;

-- 3. Count the number of students enrolled in each course.
SELECT
    C.course_name,
    COUNT(E.student_id) AS student_count
FROM
    Courses AS C
LEFT JOIN
    Enrollments AS E ON C.course_id = E.course_id
GROUP BY
    C.course_name;

-- 4. Enroll a student in a new course.
INSERT INTO Enrollments (student_id, course_id, enrollment_date, grade)
SELECT
    S.student_id,
    C.course_id,
    CURRENT_DATE,
    NULL
FROM
    Students AS S,
    Courses AS C
WHERE
    C.course_id = 103 -- Assuming course_id 103 for the new course
    AND S.student_id = 2; -- Assuming student_id 2 for the student to enroll

-- 5. Update the grade for a specific student in a specific course.
UPDATE Enrollments
SET grade = 'A'
FROM
    Students AS S,
    Courses AS C
WHERE
    Enrollments.course_id = C.course_id
    AND Enrollments.student_id = S.student_id
    AND S.student_id = 1
    AND Enrollments.course_id = 101;

`Artists` (artist_id PK, artist_name, genre)
`Performances` (performance_id PK, festival_id FK, artist_id FK, stage_name, performance_time)

1. List all artists performing at a specific festival, including their stage and time.
2. Find all festivals where a particular artist is performing.
3. Count the number of performances for each artist across all festivals.

5. Update the performance time for an artist at a festival.

SELECT
  A.artist_name,
  P.stage_name,
  P.performance_time
FROM Performances AS P
JOIN Artists AS A
  ON P.artist_id = A.artist_id
WHERE
  P.festival_id = 1;

SELECT
  F.festival_name,
  F.start_date,
  F.location
FROM Festivals AS F
JOIN Performances AS P
  ON F.festival_id = P.festival_id
WHERE
  P.artist_id = 2;

  A.artist_name,
  COUNT(P.performance_id) AS total_performances
FROM Artists AS A
LEFT JOIN Performances AS P
  ON A.artist_id = P.artist_id
GROUP BY
  A.artist_name
ORDER BY
  total_performances DESC;

Schema: 
`Recipes` (recipe_id PK, recipe_name, instructions, cook_time_minutes, prep_time_minutes, user_id)
`Ingredients` (ingredient_id PK, ingredient_name, unit_of_measure)
`RecipeIngredients` (recipe_ingredient_id PK, recipe_id FK, ingredient_id FK, quantity)

Queries:
1. Get all ingredients for a specific recipe, including quantities.
2. Find all recipes that contain a specific ingredient.
3. Count the number of recipes created by each user.
4. Add a new recipe with its ingredients.
5. Update the instructions for a specific recipe.
text_nat:
SELECT i.ingredient_name, ri.quantity, i.unit_of_measure
FROM Ingredients i
JOIN RecipeIngredients ri ON i.ingredient_id = ri.ingredient_id
WHERE ri.recipe_id = 1;

SELECT r.recipe_name, r.instructions
FROM Recipes r
JOIN RecipeIngredients ri ON r.recipe_id = ri.recipe_id
JOIN Ingredients i ON ri.ingredient_id = i.ingredient_id
WHERE i.ingredient_name = 'Chicken Breast';

SELECT u.user_id, COUNT(r.recipe_id) AS num_recipes
FROM Recipes r
GROUP BY r.user_id;

INSERT INTO Recipes (recipe_name, instructions, cook_time_minutes, prep_time_minutes, user_id)
VALUES ('Spaghetti Carbonara', 'Cook pasta. Fry pancetta. Mix eggs and cheese. Combine all.', 20, 10, 101);

INSERT INTO RecipeIngredients (recipe_id, ingredient_id, quantity)
SELECT r.recipe_id, i.ingredient_id, 200
FROM Recipes r
JOIN Ingredients i ON i.ingredient_name = 'Spaghetti'
WHERE r.recipe_name = 'Spaghetti Carbonara';

INSERT INTO RecipeIngredients (recipe_id, ingredient_id, quantity)
SELECT r.recipe_id, i.ingredient_id, 150
FROM Recipes r
JOIN Ingredients i ON i.ingredient_name = 'Pancetta'
WHERE r.recipe_name = 'Spaghetti Carbonara';

UPDATE Recipes
SET instructions = 'Cook pasta al dente. Fry diced pancetta until crispy. Whisk eggs, Pecorino Romano, and black pepper. Combine pasta, pancetta, and egg mixture quickly.'
WHERE recipe_id = 5;

`Reviews` (review_id PK, product_id FK, customer_id FK, rating, review_text, review_date)

SELECT r.review_id, r.rating, r.review_text, r.review_date, c.first_name, c.last_name

Schema: 
`Employees` (employee_id PK, first_name, last_name, department_id)
`Goals` (goal_id PK, employee_id FK, goal_description, target_date, actual_completion_date, status)

Queries:
1. List all active goals for a specific employee.
2. Find all employees with overdue goals.
3. Count the number of goals by status for each department.
4. Assign a new goal to an employee.
5. Update the status of a goal to 'Completed'.
text_nat:
-- 1. List all active goals for a specific employee.
SELECT
    G.goal_description,
    G.target_date
FROM
    Goals AS G
JOIN
    Employees AS E ON G.employee_id = E.employee_id
WHERE
    E.employee_id = 101 AND G.status = 'In Progress';

-- 2. Find all employees with overdue goals.
SELECT DISTINCT
    E.first_name,
    E.last_name
FROM
    Employees AS E
JOIN
    Goals AS G ON E.employee_id = G.employee_id
WHERE
    G.status != 'Completed' AND G.target_date < CURRENT_DATE;

-- 3. Count the number of goals by status for each department.
SELECT
    D.department_name,
    G.status,
    COUNT(G.goal_id) AS goal_count
FROM
    Goals AS G
JOIN
    Employees AS E ON G.employee_id = E.employee_id
JOIN
    Departments AS D ON E.department_id = D.department_id
GROUP BY
    D.department_name, G.status
ORDER BY
    D.department_name, G.status;

-- 4. Assign a new goal to an employee.
INSERT INTO Goals (employee_id, goal_description, target_date, status)
SELECT
    E.employee_id,
    'Improve SQL skills',
    '2024-12-31',
    'In Progress'
FROM
    Employees AS E
WHERE
    E.employee_id = 102;

-- 5. Update the status of a goal to 'Completed'.
UPDATE Goals
SET
    status = 'Completed',
    actual_completion_date = CURRENT_DATE
WHERE
    goal_id = 205;
text_alt:

    Goals AS G
WHERE

    Departments AS D

Schema: 
`Transactions` (transaction_id PK, customer_id, transaction_date, total_amount)
`TransactionItems` (item_id PK, transaction_id FK, product_id, quantity, unit_price)
`Products` (product_id PK, product_name, category)

Queries:
1. Get all items for a specific transaction, including product names.
2. Calculate the total sales for each product category within a date range.
3. Find all transactions made by a specific customer.
4. Insert a new transaction with multiple items.
5. Update the total amount of a transaction.
text_nat:
-- Query 1: Get all items for a specific transaction, including product names.
SELECT
    ti.item_id,
    ti.product_id,
    p.product_name,
    ti.quantity,
    ti.unit_price
FROM
    TransactionItems ti
JOIN
    Products p ON ti.product_id = p.product_id
WHERE
    ti.transaction_id = 101;

-- Query 2: Calculate the total sales for each product category within a date range.
SELECT
    p.category,
    SUM(ti.quantity * ti.unit_price) AS total_sales
FROM
    Transactions t
JOIN
    TransactionItems ti ON t.transaction_id = ti.transaction_id
JOIN
    Products p ON ti.product_id = p.product_id
WHERE
    t.transaction_date BETWEEN '2023-01-01' AND '2023-01-31'
GROUP BY
    p.category;

-- Query 3: Find all transactions made by a specific customer.
SELECT
    t.transaction_id,
    t.transaction_date,
    t.total_amount
FROM
    Transactions t
WHERE
    t.customer_id = 5;

-- Query 4: Insert a new transaction with multiple items.
INSERT INTO Transactions (transaction_id, customer_id, transaction_date, total_amount)
VALUES (105, 7, '2023-02-15', 0);

INSERT INTO TransactionItems (item_id, transaction_id, product_id, quantity, unit_price)
SELECT 201, 105, 301, 2, 10.50
UNION ALL
SELECT 202, 105, 302, 1, 25.00;

-- Query 5: Update the total amount of a transaction.
UPDATE Transactions t
SET total_amount = (
    SELECT SUM(ti.quantity * ti.unit_price)
    FROM TransactionItems ti
    WHERE ti.transaction_id = t.transaction_id
)
WHERE t.transaction_id = 105;

WHERE t.transaction_id = 105;

Schema: 
`Projects` (project_id PK, project_name, lead_researcher_id, start_date, end_date, budget)
`Researchers` (researcher_id PK, first_name, last_name, department)

Queries:
1. List all projects led by a specific researcher.
2. Find all projects with a budget exceeding a certain amount.
3. Calculate the total budget allocated to each department for projects.
4. Insert a new research project.
5. Update the end date of a specific project.
text_nat:
-- Query 1: List all projects led by a specific researcher.
SELECT
    p.project_id,
    p.project_name
FROM
    Projects AS p
JOIN
    Researchers AS r ON p.lead_researcher_id = r.researcher_id
WHERE
    r.first_name = 'Maria' AND r.last_name = 'Gonzales';

-- Query 2: Find all projects with a budget exceeding a certain amount.
SELECT
    project_name,
    budget
FROM
    Projects
WHERE
    budget > 100000;

-- Query 3: Calculate the total budget allocated to each department for projects.
SELECT
    r.department,
    SUM(p.budget) AS total_department_budget
FROM
    Projects AS p
JOIN
    Researchers AS r ON p.lead_researcher_id = r.researcher_id
GROUP BY
    r.department;

-- Query 4: Insert a new research project.
INSERT INTO Projects (project_name, lead_researcher_id, start_date, end_date, budget)
VALUES ('AI in Healthcare', (SELECT researcher_id FROM Researchers WHERE first_name = 'Carlos' AND last_name = 'Ramirez'), '2023-09-01', '2025-08-31', 250000);

-- Query 5: Update the end date of a specific project.
UPDATE Projects
SET end_date = '2024-12-31'
WHERE project_name = 'Quantum Computing Applications';

Schema: 
`Vehicles` (vehicle_id PK, license_plate, make, model, current_mileage)
`Fuelings` (fueling_id PK, vehicle_id FK, fueling_date, mileage_at_fueling, fuel_amount_liters, cost)

Queries:
1. Get all fueling records for a specific vehicle, ordered by date.
2. Calculate the average fuel cost per liter for each vehicle.
3. Find the total fuel consumed by all vehicles in a given month.
4. Insert a new fueling record for a vehicle.
5. Update the current mileage of a vehicle after fueling.
text_nat:
SELECT *
FROM Fuelings f
JOIN Vehicles v ON f.vehicle_id = v.vehicle_id
WHERE v.license_plate = 'ABC-123'
ORDER BY f.fueling_date DESC;

SELECT
    v.make,
    v.model,
    AVG(f.cost / f.fuel_amount_liters) AS average_cost_per_liter
FROM Vehicles v
JOIN Fuelings f ON v.vehicle_id = f.vehicle_id
GROUP BY v.vehicle_id, v.make, v.model;

SELECT
    SUM(f.fuel_amount_liters) AS total_fuel_consumed_liters
FROM Fuelings f
WHERE STRFTIME('%Y-%m', f.fueling_date) = '2023-10';

INSERT INTO Fuelings (vehicle_id, fueling_date, mileage_at_fueling, fuel_amount_liters, cost)
VALUES (1, '2023-10-27', 12500, 45.5, 75.20);

UPDATE Vehicles
SET current_mileage = (SELECT f.mileage_at_fueling FROM Fuelings f WHERE f.fueling_id = LAST_INSERT_ROWID())
WHERE vehicle_id = (SELECT f.vehicle_id FROM Fuelings f WHERE f.fueling_id = LAST_INSERT_ROWID());
text_alt:
SELECT *
FROM Fuelings f, Vehicles v
WHERE f.vehicle_id = v.vehicle_id AND v.license_plate = 'ABC-123'
ORDER BY f.fueling_date DESC;

SELECT
    v.make,
    v.model,
    AVG(f.cost / f.fuel_amount_liters) AS average_cost_per_liter
FROM Vehicles v, Fuelings f
WHERE v.vehicle_id = f.vehicle_id
GROUP BY v.vehicle_id, v.make, v.model;

SELECT
    SUM(f.fuel_amount_liters) AS total_fuel_consumed_liters
FROM Fuelings f
WHERE STRFTIME('%Y-%m', f.fueling_date) = '2023-10';

VALUES (1, '2023-10-27', 12500, 45.5, 75.20);

UPDATE Vehicles
SET current_mileage = (SELECT f.mileage_at_fueling FROM Fuelings f WHERE f.fueling_id = LAST_INSERT_ROWID())
WHERE vehicle_id = (SELECT f.vehicle_id FROM Fuelings f WHERE f.fueling_id = LAST_INSERT_ROWID());

Schema: 
`Movies` (movie_id PK, title, genre, runtime_minutes, release_year)
`Theaters` (theater_id PK, theater_name, city, capacity)
`Showtimes` (showtime_id PK, movie_id FK, theater_id FK, showtime_date, showtime_time, available_seats)

Queries:
1. List all showtimes for a specific movie in a given city.
2. Find all movies currently showing at a specific theater.
3. Count the number of showtimes for each movie.
4. Add a new showtime for a movie at a theater.
5. Update the number of available seats for a specific showtime.
text_nat:
SELECT
  S.showtime_id,
  M.title,
  T.theater_name,
  S.showtime_date,
  S.showtime_time,
  S.available_seats
FROM Showtimes AS S
JOIN Movies AS M
  ON S.movie_id = M.movie_id
JOIN Theaters AS T
  ON S.theater_id = T.theater_id
WHERE
  M.title = 'The Matrix' AND T.city = 'New York';

SELECT DISTINCT
  M.title,
  M.genre,
  M.runtime_minutes
FROM Movies AS M
JOIN Showtimes AS S
  ON M.movie_id = S.movie_id
JOIN Theaters AS T
  ON S.theater_id = T.theater_id
WHERE
  T.theater_name = 'Grand Cinema';

SELECT
  M.title,
  COUNT(S.showtime_id) AS number_of_showtimes
FROM Movies AS M
LEFT JOIN Showtimes AS S
  ON M.movie_id = S.movie_id
GROUP BY
  M.title;

INSERT INTO Showtimes (movie_id, theater_id, showtime_date, showtime_time, available_seats)
SELECT
  M.movie_id,
  T.theater_id,
  '2024-03-15',
  '19:00:00',
  150
FROM Movies AS M
JOIN Theaters AS T
  ON M.title = 'Inception' AND T.theater_name = 'Regal Cinemas';

UPDATE Showtimes
SET
  available_seats = 100
WHERE
  showtime_id = 123
  AND movie_id = (
    SELECT
      M.movie_id
    FROM Movies AS M
    WHERE
      M.title = 'The Dark Knight'
  );
text_alt:
SELECT
  S.showtime_id,
  M.title,
  T.theater_name,
  S.showtime_date,
  S.showtime_time,
  S.available_seats
FROM Showtimes AS S, Movies AS M, Theaters AS T
WHERE
  S.movie_id = M.movie_id AND S.theater_id = T.theater_id AND M.title = 'The Matrix' AND T.city = 'New York';

SELECT DISTINCT
  M.title,
  M.genre,
  M.runtime_minutes
FROM Movies AS M, Showtimes AS S, Theaters AS T
WHERE
  M.movie_id = S.movie_id AND S.theater_id = T.theater_id AND T.theater_name = 'Grand Cinema';

SELECT
  M.title,
  COUNT(S.showtime_id) AS number_of_showtimes
FROM Movies AS M LEFT JOIN Showtimes AS S
  ON M.movie_id = S.movie_id
GROUP BY
  M.title;

  M.movie_id,
  T.theater_id,
  '2024-03-15',

  M.title = 'Inception' AND T.theater_name = 'Regal Cinemas';

  showtime_id = 123

    SELECT
      M.movie_id
    FROM Movies AS M
    WHERE
      M.title = 'The Dark Knight'
  );

Schema: 
`Customers` (customer_id PK, first_name, last_name, email)
`Agents` (agent_id PK, first_name, last_name, department)
`Interactions` (interaction_id PK, customer_id FK, agent_id FK, interaction_date, interaction_type, notes)

Queries:
1. List all interactions for a specific customer, ordered by date.
2. Find all interactions handled by a specific agent within a date range.
3. Count the number of interactions by type for each agent.
4. Log a new customer interaction.
5. Update the notes for a specific interaction.
text_nat:
SELECT *
FROM Interactions i
JOIN Customers c ON i.customer_id = c.customer_id
WHERE c.customer_id = 1
ORDER BY i.interaction_date;

SELECT i.*, c.first_name, c.last_name
FROM Interactions i
JOIN Agents a ON i.agent_id = a.agent_id
JOIN Customers c ON i.customer_id = c.customer_id
WHERE a.agent_id = 101 AND i.interaction_date BETWEEN '2023-01-01' AND '2023-01-31';

SELECT
    a.first_name,
    a.last_name,
    i.interaction_type,
    COUNT(i.interaction_id) AS interaction_count
FROM Agents a
JOIN Interactions i ON a.agent_id = i.agent_id
GROUP BY a.agent_id, a.first_name, a.last_name, i.interaction_type
ORDER BY a.first_name, i.interaction_type;

INSERT INTO Interactions (customer_id, agent_id, interaction_date, interaction_type, notes)
SELECT c.customer_id, a.agent_id, '2023-02-15', 'Call', 'Customer inquired about new features'
FROM Customers c
JOIN Agents a ON a.agent_id = 201
WHERE c.customer_id = 5;

UPDATE Interactions
SET notes = 'Customer provided positive feedback on recent service'

Schema: 
`Rooms` (room_id PK, room_number, floor, capacity, status)
`Patients` (patient_id PK, first_name, last_name, admission_date)
`Admissions` (admission_id PK, patient_id FK, room_id FK, admission_start_date, admission_end_date)

Queries:
1. List all occupied rooms and the patients in them.
2. Find all available rooms on a specific floor.
3. Count the number of occupied rooms by floor.
4. Admit a patient to an available room.
5. Update the status of a room to 'Vacant' after a patient discharge.
text_nat:
-- 1. List all occupied rooms and the patients in them.
SELECT
  R.room_number,
  P.first_name,
  P.last_name
FROM Rooms AS R
JOIN Admissions AS A
  ON R.room_id = A.room_id
JOIN Patients AS P
  ON A.patient_id = P.patient_id
WHERE
  R.status = 'Occupied' AND A.admission_end_date IS NULL;

-- 2. Find all available rooms on a specific floor (e.g., floor 3).
SELECT
  room_number,
  capacity
FROM Rooms
WHERE
  status = 'Available' AND floor = 3;

-- 3. Count the number of occupied rooms by floor.
SELECT
  R.floor,
  COUNT(R.room_id) AS occupied_rooms_count
FROM Rooms AS R
JOIN Admissions AS A
  ON R.room_id = A.room_id
WHERE
  R.status = 'Occupied' AND A.admission_end_date IS NULL
GROUP BY
  R.floor;

-- 4. Admit a patient to an available room (patient_id 101, room_id 201).
INSERT INTO Admissions (patient_id, room_id, admission_start_date, admission_end_date)
VALUES
  (101, 201, '2023-10-26', NULL);

UPDATE Rooms
SET
  status = 'Occupied'
WHERE
  room_id = 201;

-- 5. Update the status of a room to 'Vacant' after a patient discharge (admission_id 301).
UPDATE Admissions
SET
  admission_end_date = '2023-10-27'
WHERE
  admission_id = 301;

UPDATE Rooms
SET
  status = 'Available'
WHERE
  room_id = (SELECT
               room_id
             FROM Admissions
             WHERE
               admission_id = 301);

`Progress` (progress_id PK, user_id FK, course_id FK, completed_modules, last_accessed_date, status)

Queries:
1. List the progress of a specific user in all their enrolled courses.
2. Find all users who have completed a particular course.
3. Calculate the average completed modules for each course.
4. Record a user's progress in a course.
5. Update the 'status' of a user's course progress to 'Completed'.
text_nat:
-- 1. List the progress of a specific user in all their enrolled courses.
SELECT
    u.username,
    c.course_name,
    p.completed_modules,
    p.total_modules,
    p.status
FROM
    Users AS u
JOIN
    Progress AS p ON u.user_id = p.user_id
JOIN
    Courses AS c ON p.course_id = c.course_id
WHERE
    u.user_id = 1;

-- 2. Find all users who have completed a particular course.
SELECT
    u.username,
    u.email
FROM
    Users AS u
JOIN
    Progress AS p ON u.user_id = p.user_id
WHERE
    p.course_id = 101 AND p.status = 'Completed';

-- 3. Calculate the average completed modules for each course.
SELECT
    c.course_name,
    AVG(p.completed_modules) AS average_completed_modules
FROM
    Courses AS c
LEFT JOIN
    Progress AS p ON c.course_id = p.course_id
GROUP BY
    c.course_name;

-- 4. Record a user's progress in a course.

SET status = 'Completed', last_accessed_date = CURRENT_DATE
WHERE user_id = 2 AND course_id = 101;

Schema: 
`Teams` (team_id PK, team_name, sport, city)
`Players` (player_id PK, first_name, last_name, position, team_id FK)
`Games` (game_id PK, home_team_id FK, away_team_id FK, game_date, score_home, score_away)

Queries:
1. List all players for a specific team, including their positions.
2. Find all games played by a specific team within a date range.
3. Count the number of players on each team.
4. Add a new player to a team.
5. Update the score for a specific game.
text_nat:
-- 1. List all players for a specific team, including their positions.
SELECT
    p.first_name,
    p.last_name,
    p.position
FROM
    Players AS p
JOIN
    Teams AS t ON p.team_id = t.team_id
WHERE
    t.team_name = 'Lakers';

-- 2. Find all games played by a specific team within a date range.
SELECT
    g.game_date,
    th.team_name AS home_team,
    ta.team_name AS away_team,
    g.score_home,
    g.score_away
FROM
    Games AS g
JOIN
    Teams AS th ON g.home_team_id = th.team_id
JOIN
    Teams AS ta ON g.away_team_id = ta.team_id
WHERE
    (th.team_name = 'Lakers' OR ta.team_name = 'Lakers')
    AND g.game_date BETWEEN '2023-01-01' AND '2023-03-31';

-- 3. Count the number of players on each team.
SELECT
    t.team_name,
    COUNT(p.player_id) AS player_count
FROM
    Teams AS t
LEFT JOIN
    Players AS p ON t.team_id = p.team_id
GROUP BY
    t.team_name;

-- 4. Add a new player to a team.
INSERT INTO Players (player_id, first_name, last_name, position, team_id)
SELECT
    101, 'New', 'Player', 'Guard', t.team_id
FROM
    Teams AS t
WHERE
    t.team_name = 'Lakers';

-- 5. Update the score for a specific game.
UPDATE Games
SET
    score_home = 110,
    score_away = 105
WHERE
    game_id = (SELECT g.game_id FROM Games AS g JOIN Teams AS th ON g.home_team_id = th.team_id WHERE th.team_name = 'Lakers' AND g.game_date = '2023-01-15' LIMIT 1);

Queries:
1. Get the quantity of a specific product in all warehouses.
2. Find all products with quantity less than 10 in a specific warehouse.
3. Calculate the total value of stock in each warehouse.
4. Add new stock for a product in a warehouse.
5. Update the quantity on hand for a product in a warehouse.
text_nat:
SELECT
    p.product_name,
    w.warehouse_name,
    s.quantity_on_hand
FROM
    Products AS p
JOIN
    Stock AS s ON p.product_id = s.product_id
JOIN
    Warehouses AS w ON s.warehouse_id = w.warehouse_id
WHERE
    p.product_name = 'Laptop';

SELECT
    p.product_name,
    s.quantity_on_hand
FROM
    Products AS p
JOIN
    Stock AS s ON p.product_id = s.product_id
JOIN
    Warehouses AS w ON s.warehouse_id = w.warehouse_id
WHERE
    w.warehouse_name = 'Main Warehouse' AND s.quantity_on_hand < 10;

SELECT
    w.warehouse_name,
    SUM(p.unit_cost * s.quantity_on_hand) AS total_value
FROM
    Warehouses AS w
JOIN
    Stock AS s ON w.warehouse_id = s.warehouse_id
JOIN
    Products AS p ON s.product_id = p.product_id
GROUP BY
    w.warehouse_name;

Schema: 
`Customers` (customer_id PK, first_name, last_name, email, join_date)
`Tiers` (tier_id PK, tier_name, min_points, max_points, benefits)
`LoyaltyPoints` (point_id PK, customer_id FK, points_earned, transaction_date, description)

Queries:
1. Get the current loyalty points for a specific customer.
2. Find all customers in a particular loyalty tier.
3. Calculate the total points earned by each customer.
4. Award loyalty points to a customer for a transaction.
5. Update a customer's loyalty tier based on their points.
text_nat:
CREATE TABLE CustomerTiers (
    customer_id INT PRIMARY KEY,
    tier_id     INT NOT NULL,
    updated_at  DATETIME NOT NULL,
    CONSTRAINT fk_ct_customer FOREIGN KEY (customer_id) REFERENCES Customers(customer_id),
    CONSTRAINT fk_ct_tier     FOREIGN KEY (tier_id)     REFERENCES Tiers(tier_id)
);

CREATE VIEW CustomerPointTotals AS
SELECT c.customer_id,
       c.email,
       SUM(lp.points_earned) AS total_points,
       COUNT(lp.point_id)    AS transaction_count,
       MAX(lp.transaction_date) AS last_transaction
FROM Customers c
JOIN LoyaltyPoints lp ON lp.customer_id = c.customer_id
GROUP BY c.customer_id, c.email;

DELIMITER $$

CREATE PROCEDURE GetCustomerPoints(IN p_customer_id INT)
BEGIN
    SELECT p.customer_id,
           CONCAT(c.first_name, ' ', c.last_name) AS customer_name,
           p.total_points,
           t.tier_name,
           t.benefits
    FROM CustomerPointTotals p
    JOIN Customers c ON c.customer_id = p.customer_id
    JOIN CustomerTiers ct ON ct.customer_id = p.customer_id
    JOIN Tiers t ON t.tier_id = ct.tier_id
    WHERE p.customer_id = p_customer_id;
END$$

CREATE PROCEDURE GetCustomersInTier(IN p_tier_name VARCHAR(50))
BEGIN
    SELECT c.customer_id,
           c.first_name,
           c.last_name,
           c.email,
           c.join_date,
           ct.updated_at AS tier_assigned_on
    FROM Tiers t
    JOIN CustomerTiers ct ON ct.tier_id = t.tier_id
    JOIN Customers c ON c.customer_id = ct.customer_id
    WHERE t.tier_name = p_tier_name
    ORDER BY c.last_name, c.first_name;
END$$

CREATE PROCEDURE GetTotalPointsByCustomer()
BEGIN
    SELECT c.customer_id,
           c.email,
           SUM(lp.points_earned) AS total_points,
           COUNT(lp.point_id) AS transaction_count,
           MAX(lp.transaction_date) AS last_transaction
    FROM Customers c
    JOIN LoyaltyPoints lp ON lp.customer_id = c.customer_id
    GROUP BY c.customer_id, c.email
    ORDER BY total_points DESC;
END$$

CREATE PROCEDURE GetTierSummary()
BEGIN
    SELECT t.tier_name,
           t.min_points,
           COUNT(ct.customer_id) AS member_count,
           ROUND(AVG(p.total_points), 1) AS avg_points
    FROM Tiers t
    JOIN CustomerTiers ct ON ct.tier_id = t.tier_id
    JOIN CustomerPointTotals p ON p.customer_id = ct.customer_id
    GROUP BY t.tier_id, t.tier_name, t.min_points
    ORDER BY t.min_points;
END$$

CREATE PROCEDURE UpdateCustomerTier(IN p_customer_id INT)
BEGIN
    INSERT INTO CustomerTiers (customer_id, tier_id, updated_at)
    SELECT p.customer_id, t.tier_id, NOW()
    FROM CustomerPointTotals p
    JOIN Tiers t ON p.total_points BETWEEN t.min_points AND COALESCE(t.max_points, 2147483647)
    WHERE p.customer_id = p_customer_id
    ON DUPLICATE KEY UPDATE tier_id = VALUES(tier_id), updated_at = NOW();
END$$

CREATE PROCEDURE AwardPoints(IN p_customer_id INT, IN p_points INT, IN p_description VARCHAR(255))
BEGIN
    IF NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM Customers WHERE customer_id = p_customer_id) THEN
        SIGNAL SQLSTATE '45000' SET MESSAGE_TEXT = 'Unknown customer_id';
    END IF;
    INSERT INTO LoyaltyPoints (customer_id, points_earned, transaction_date, description)
    VALUES (p_customer_id, p_points, NOW(), p_description);
    CALL UpdateCustomerTier(p_customer_id);
END$$

DELIMITER ;

CALL AwardPoints(101, 250, 'Order #5521 - electronics');
CALL AwardPoints(102, 40, 'Order #5522 - groceries');
CALL GetCustomerPoints(101);
CALL GetCustomersInTier('Gold');
CALL GetTotalPointsByCustomer();
CALL GetTierSummary();

      AND p.customer_id = p_customer_id
    ON DUPLICATE KEY UPDATE tier_id = VALUES(tier_id), updated_at = NOW();
END$$

CREATE PROCEDURE AwardPoints(IN p_customer_id INT, IN p_points INT, IN p_description VARCHAR(255))
BEGIN
    IF NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM Customers WHERE customer_id = p_customer_id) THEN
        SIGNAL SQLSTATE '45000' SET MESSAGE_TEXT = 'Unknown customer_id';
    END IF;
    INSERT INTO LoyaltyPoints (customer_id, points_earned, transaction_date, description)
    VALUES (p_customer_id, p_points, NOW(), p_description);

Schema: 
`Organizations` (organization_id PK, org_name, contact_person, type)
`Grants` (grant_id PK, grant_name, description, available_funds, deadline)
`Applications` (application_id PK, organization_id FK, grant_id FK, submission_date, requested_amount, status)

Queries:
1. List all applications for a specific grant, including organization details.
2. Find all grants with a deadline in the next month.
3. Count the number of applications by status for each grant.
4. Submit a new grant application for an organization.
5. Update the status of an application to 'Approved'.
text_nat:
-- Grant management module: reporting views, lookup procedures and write operations.

CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW v_application_detail AS
SELECT a.application_id,
       a.grant_id,
       g.grant_name,
       g.deadline,
       o.organization_id,
       o.org_name,
       o.contact_person,
       o.type AS org_type,
       a.submission_date,
       a.requested_amount,
       a.status
FROM Applications a
JOIN Grants g ON g.grant_id = a.grant_id
JOIN Organizations o ON o.organization_id = a.organization_id;

CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW v_application_counts_by_status AS
SELECT g.grant_id, g.grant_name, a.status, COUNT(a.application_id) AS application_count
FROM Grants g
JOIN Applications a ON a.grant_id = g.grant_id
GROUP BY g.grant_id, g.grant_name, a.status;

CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW v_grants_due_next_month AS
SELECT g.grant_id, g.grant_name, g.available_funds, g.deadline
FROM Grants g
WHERE g.deadline >= DATE_FORMAT(CURDATE() + INTERVAL 1 MONTH, '%Y-%m-01')
  AND g.deadline <  DATE_FORMAT(CURDATE() + INTERVAL 2 MONTH, '%Y-%m-01');

DELIMITER //

CREATE PROCEDURE list_applications_for_grant(IN p_grant_id INT)
BEGIN
    SELECT a.application_id, o.org_name, o.contact_person, o.type AS org_type,
           a.submission_date, a.requested_amount, a.status
    FROM Applications a
    JOIN Organizations o ON o.organization_id = a.organization_id
    WHERE a.grant_id = p_grant_id
    ORDER BY a.submission_date, a.application_id;
END //

CREATE PROCEDURE organization_history(IN p_organization_id INT)
BEGIN
    SELECT a.application_id, g.grant_name, g.deadline,
           a.submission_date, a.requested_amount, a.status
    FROM Applications a
    JOIN Grants g ON g.grant_id = a.grant_id
    WHERE a.organization_id = p_organization_id
    ORDER BY a.submission_date DESC;
END //

CREATE PROCEDURE submit_application(IN p_organization_id INT,
                                    IN p_grant_id INT,
                                    IN p_requested_amount DECIMAL(12,2))
BEGIN
    INSERT INTO Applications (organization_id, grant_id, submission_date, requested_amount, status)
    SELECT o.organization_id, g.grant_id, CURDATE(), p_requested_amount, 'Submitted'
    FROM Grants g
    JOIN Organizations o ON o.organization_id = p_organization_id
    WHERE g.grant_id = p_grant_id
      AND g.deadline >= CURDATE()
      AND g.available_funds >= p_requested_amount;

    IF ROW_COUNT() = 0 THEN
        SIGNAL SQLSTATE '45000'
            SET MESSAGE_TEXT = 'Application rejected: unknown organization/grant, past deadline or insufficient funds';
    END IF;
END //

CREATE PROCEDURE approve_application(IN p_application_id INT)
BEGIN
    UPDATE Applications a
    JOIN Grants g ON g.grant_id = a.grant_id
    SET a.status = 'Approved',
        g.available_funds = g.available_funds - a.requested_amount
    WHERE a.application_id = p_application_id
      AND a.status <> 'Approved'
      AND g.available_funds >= a.requested_amount;

    IF ROW_COUNT() = 0 THEN
        SIGNAL SQLSTATE '45000'
            SET MESSAGE_TEXT = 'Approval failed: application already approved, missing or funds exhausted';
    END IF;
END //

Schema: 
`Games` (game_id PK, game_name, genre, release_year)
`Players` (player_id PK, username, join_date)
`HighScores` (score_id PK, game_id FK, player_id FK, score, achieve_date)

Queries:
1. Get the top 10 high scores for a specific game, including player usernames.
2. Find all high scores achieved by a specific player.
3. Count the number of scores submitted for each game.
4. Record a new high score for a player in a game.
5. Update a player's high score for a specific game if the new score is higher.

-- Arcade high-score module: leaderboard views and the five required operations.

-- Leaderboard view: every score with its game and player details, ranked per game.
CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW v_game_leaderboard AS
SELECT g.game_id,
       g.game_name,
       g.genre,
       p.player_id,
       p.username,
       h.score,
       h.achieve_date,
       RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY g.game_id
                    ORDER BY h.score DESC, h.achieve_date ASC) AS rank_in_game
FROM HighScores h
JOIN Games g ON g.game_id = h.game_id
JOIN Players p ON p.player_id = h.player_id;

-- Per-game score volume; subqueries keep games that have never been played.
CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW v_game_score_counts AS
SELECT g.game_id,
       g.game_name,
       (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM HighScores h WHERE h.game_id = g.game_id) AS score_count,
       (SELECT COALESCE(MAX(h.score), 0) FROM HighScores h WHERE h.game_id = g.game_id) AS best_score
FROM Games g;

-- 1. Top 10 high scores for a specific game, with player usernames.
SELECT p.username, h.score, h.achieve_date
FROM HighScores h
JOIN Games g ON g.game_id = h.game_id
JOIN Players p ON p.player_id = h.player_id
WHERE g.game_id = 3
ORDER BY h.score DESC, h.achieve_date ASC
LIMIT 10;

-- 2. All high scores achieved by a specific player.
SELECT p.username, g.game_name, g.genre, g.release_year, h.score, h.achieve_date
FROM HighScores h
JOIN Games g ON g.game_id = h.game_id
JOIN Players p ON p.player_id = h.player_id
WHERE h.player_id = 17
ORDER BY h.achieve_date DESC, h.score DESC;

-- 3. Number of scores submitted for each game.
SELECT game_id, game_name, score_count, best_score
FROM v_game_score_counts
ORDER BY score_count DESC, game_name;

-- 4. Record a new high score; the join rejects unknown ids and pre-join dates.
INSERT INTO HighScores (game_id, player_id, score, achieve_date)
SELECT g.game_id, p.player_id, 48200, DATE '2024-05-02'
FROM Games g
JOIN Players p ON p.join_date <= DATE '2024-05-02'
WHERE g.game_id = 3 AND p.player_id = 17;

-- 5. Raise a player's score for a game (identified by name) only if the run is better.
UPDATE HighScores h
JOIN Games g ON g.game_id = h.game_id
SET h.score = 51750,
    h.achieve_date = DATE '2024-06-11'
WHERE h.player_id = 17
  AND g.game_name = 'Nebula Rally'
  AND h.score < 51750;

-- Report: current leader of every game next to that game's score volume.
SELECT c.game_name, c.score_count, l.username AS leader, l.score AS leading_score
FROM v_game_score_counts c
JOIN v_game_leaderboard l ON l.game_id = c.game_id AND l.rank_in_game = 1
ORDER BY l.score DESC;

-- Report: genre totals built from the ranked leaderboard rows.
SELECT l.genre,
       COUNT(DISTINCT l.game_id) AS games_played,
       COUNT(DISTINCT l.player_id) AS players,
       MAX(l.score) AS genre_record
FROM v_game_leaderboard l
JOIN Players p ON p.player_id = l.player_id
WHERE p.join_date >= DATE '2023-01-01'
GROUP BY l.genre
ORDER BY genre_record DESC;
